doc_description: Amcor plc’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for FY2020—its first full year after acquiring Bemis—covers COVID-19 impacts and results in its Flexibles and Rigid Packaging segments, a completed $500m share buyback and new USD/EUR bond issues, progress toward $180m merger synergies and 2025 recyclability targets, and an adverse ICFR opinion for segregation-of-duties.

structure.title: Preface
structure.summary:
- Annual Report on Form 10-K for Amcor plc for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2020, filed with the U.S. SEC.
- Company and listing details: Amcor plc (incorporated in Jersey) with principal offices in the U.K.; NYSE-listed ordinary shares (AMCR) and 1.125% Guaranteed Senior Notes due 2027 (AUKF/27); no Section 12(g) securities.
- Registrant status and compliance: well-known seasoned issuer; large accelerated filer; filed all required reports and Interactive Data Files; auditor attestation under SOX 404(b); not a shell company.
- Market and share data: aggregate market value of non-affiliate holdings of $17.4 billion; 1,568,481,519 shares outstanding as of August 25, 2020.
- Documents incorporated by reference: Part III information to be provided via the 2020 Proxy Statement.
- Table of Contents overview: Part I (Business; Risk Factors; Properties; Legal Proceedings), Part II (Market for Equity; Selected Financial Data; MD&A; Market Risk; Financial Statements; Controls and Procedures), Part III (Governance, Compensation, Ownership, Related Parties, Auditor Fees), Part IV (Exhibits, Signatures).
- Forward-looking statements caution: safe harbor under the PSLRA; no obligation to update; risks include COVID-19 impacts; shifts in consumer demand; customer concentration and consolidation; competition; acquisition integration risks; growth and innovation challenges; IP risks; global economic and international operating risks; raw material and energy price/availability; supply and counterparty credit risks; IT systems failures; talent attraction/retention; environmental, health and safety compliance costs; labor disputes; LIBOR transition; FX and interest rate risks; credit rating changes; hedging effectiveness; goodwill/intangibles impairment; internal control effectiveness; insurance limitations; litigation/regulatory developments; evolving government regulations; and product development/IP execution.
- Company background: Amcor plc formed in 2018 (Jersey) to facilitate the combination with Bemis Company, Inc.; name changed to Amcor plc in October 2018.
- Bemis merger: completed June 11, 2019; Bemis shareholders received 5.1 Amcor shares per Bemis share; Amcor Limited shareholders received CDIs on ASX; Amcor shares listed on NYSE (AMCR), CDIs on ASX (AMC); legacy Amcor Limited and Bemis shares delisted.
- Business strategy:
  - Focused portfolio: primary packaging for fast-moving consumer goods with favorable industry structure, attractive growth, and leadership-driven competitive advantages across flexible and rigid packaging, specialty cartons, and closures.
  - Differentiated capabilities (“The Amcor Way”): Talent, Commercial Excellence, Operational Leadership, Innovation, and Cash & Capital Discipline.
  - Shareholder value creation: strong cash flow; dividends; organic growth in defensive end markets; targeted acquisitions; share buybacks; emphasis on relatively low volatility (constant currency) and leadership ambition to be the leading global packaging company serving customers, employees, shareholders, and the environment.

structure.title: Business
structure.heading: Item 1. Business
structure.start_phrase:
Amcor plc (ARBN 630 385 278) is a holding company originally incorporated un der the name Arctic Jersey Limited as a limited company under the Laws of the Bailiwick of Jersey in July
2018, in order to effect the Company's combination with Bemis Company , Inc.
structure.summary:
- Overview: Amcor plc is a Jersey-incorporated holding company formed in 2018 to execute a combination with Bemis Company, Inc.; renamed Amcor plc and became a public limited company in October 2018.
- Bemis merger: Completed June 11, 2019. Bemis shareholders received 5.1 Amcor shares per Bemis share; Amcor Limited shareholders received one CDI per Amcor Limited share. Amcor now trades on NYSE (AMCR) and ASX via CDIs (AMC); Amcor Limited and Bemis shares were delisted from ASX and NYSE, respectively.
- Strategy: Focused portfolio in primary packaging for fast-moving consumer goods, targeting attractive industry structures and growth, leveraging scale and leadership across flexibles, rigids, specialty cartons, and closures.
- Differentiated capabilities (“The Amcor Way”): Talent, Commercial Excellence, Operational Leadership, Innovation, and Cash and Capital Discipline.
- Shareholder value: Emphasis on strong cash generation, dividends, organic growth in defensive end markets, targeted acquisitions, and share buybacks; aims for low volatility on a constant currency basis.
- Segments (ASC 280): Two reportable segments—Flexibles and Rigid Packaging—serving customers across Europe, North America, Latin America, Africa, and Asia Pacific.
- Flexibles Segment: One of the world’s largest flexible packaging suppliers with ~40,000 employees, 181 principal sites in 39 countries; accounted for ~78% of FY2020 consolidated net sales.
- Rigid Packaging Segment: Manufactures rigid containers in the Americas with ~6,000 employees at 50 principal sites in 11 countries; ~22% of FY2020 consolidated net sales.
- Marketing and distribution: Primarily direct sales supported by technical, engineering, design, field service, and customer service teams; global footprint of sales offices and plants for responsive service.
- Customers and concentration: No single customer >10% of FY2020 net sales; PepsiCo accounted for ~11.1% and ~11.0% in FY2019 and FY2018, respectively; arrangements are diversified and changes would typically be gradual.
- Competition: Highly competitive on service, innovation, quality, and price; competitors include Aptar, Ball, Berry Global, CCL Industries, Crown, Graphic Packaging, Huhtamaki, International Paper, Mayr-Melnhof, O-I Glass, Sealed Air, Silgan, Sonoco, WestRock, and private companies; precise market share not determinable due to business diversity.
- Backlog and working capital: Inventory managed to balance favorable raw material procurement with prompt order fulfillment; manufacturing backlogs not a significant factor.
- Raw materials: Major inputs include polymer resins/films, paper, inks, adhesives, aluminum, and chemicals; sourced from diverse global suppliers with generally available supply but price volatility possible.
- Intellectual property: Portfolio of patents, patent applications, licenses, trademarks, and trade secrets; combined IP provides competitive advantage; loss of any single patent/license not expected to be materially adverse.
- Sustainability and innovation: Positions packaging as essential for product protection and waste reduction; 2018 pledge that all packaging will be recyclable or reusable by 2025, with increased recycled content and collaboration to expand recycling infrastructure and consumer engagement; innovation and partnerships are central growth drivers.
- Environmental compliance: Operations subject to wide-ranging environmental laws across jurisdictions; substantial compliance asserted via EHS management systems and audits, but potential liabilities and evolving regulations acknowledged; references to contingencies and risk factors.
- Employees: ~47,000 employees as of June 30, 2020; ~42% covered by collective bargaining; labor relations satisfactory with no significant stoppages over the past three years.
- Seasonality: No material seasonal effects in either segment.
- Research and development: Additional details referenced in Significant Accounting Policies note.
- Executive leadership: Key officers include Ronald Delia (CEO, former CFO and ARP Latin America GM), Michael Casamento (CFO), Peter Konieczny (President, Flexibles EMEA), Eric Roegner (President, Rigid Packaging), Fred Stephan (President, Flexibles North America; former Bemis NA President), and Ian Wilson (EVP, Strategy & Development).
- Filings and investor information: Large accelerated filer; SEC filings available on the SEC website and via Amcor’s investor relations site; company address provided; website information not incorporated by reference.

structure.title: Risk Factors
structure.heading: Item 1A. Risk Factors
structure.start_phrase:
The following factors, as well as factors described elsewhere in this Ann ual Report on Form 10-K, or in other filings by the Company with the Securiti es and Exchange Commission, could
adversely affect the Company's consolidated financial position, re sults of operations or cash flows.
structure.summary:
Summary of main points covered in the partial document (Item 1A. Risk Factors):

- Strategic risks:
  - Shifts in consumer demand and packaging formats can reduce sales; difficulty predicting preferences and launching timely, cost‑effective innovations.
  - Dependence on key customers; loss, volume reductions, adverse contract terms, insourcing, or price pressure from customer consolidation (largest customer ~11% of net sales in FY2018–2019) could materially affect results.
  - Intense competition and potential disruptive technologies may erode margins and market share.
  - Growth challenges: limits to organic expansion (market saturation, customer slowdowns) and difficulties identifying/closing attractive acquisitions.
  - Integration risks: operational disruption and uncertainty realizing expected synergies (e.g., targeted ~$180m pre‑tax annual net cost synergies from Bemis).
  - Intellectual property risks: theft, weak protection in some markets, costly disputes, and potential infringement claims.

- Operational risks:
  - Global health outbreaks (COVID-19): demand volatility, temporary facility or customer shutdowns, supply chain disruptions, capital market impacts, impairments (e.g., $25.6m equity-method investment write‑down).
  - Global economic weakness and political uncertainty (e.g., Brexit) can depress demand, disrupt payments and supply, and pressure prices/margins.
  - International operations: complex, changing legal/regulatory regimes, civil unrest, sanctions compliance, FX controls, inflation (including hyperinflation), and enforcement challenges in emerging markets; 74% developed/26% emerging market sales mix.
  - Raw materials and inputs: price volatility and availability for polymers, inks/solvents, aluminum, cartonboard, energy, and labor; delays in pricing pass‑throughs can hurt margins.
  - Commercial/production risks: equipment failures, pandemics, disasters, project overruns, supply shortages, and counterparty credit defaults (customers, suppliers, financial institutions).
  - Information technology and cybersecurity: system failures, cyberattacks, cloud security risks, and data breaches leading to operational, legal, financial, and reputational harm.
  - Talent: challenges attracting, developing, and retaining key personnel.
  - Environmental, health, and safety: compliance costs; evolving climate/GHG and plastics regulations; potential bans, increased operating costs, and remediation liabilities.
  - Labor relations: potential strikes or protests disrupting operations.

- Financial risks:
  - LIBOR phase‑out and uncertain transition to SOFR may affect variable‑rate debt and interest expense.
  - Foreign exchange risk (transactional and translational), including volatility in EUR, BRL, MXN and Argentina’s hyperinflation accounting, with timing lags in cost pass‑throughs impacting margins.
  - Interest rate increases could raise borrowing costs.
  - Credit rating downgrades may reduce market access and increase financing costs.
  - Hedging effectiveness risks for interest rates and FX; counterparty default risk on hedges.
  - Goodwill/intangible impairment risk (total ~$7.3b) from changes in cash flows, discount rates, or external conditions (e.g., COVID-19).
  - Internal controls: SOX 404 compliance; remediation underway for segregation‑of‑duties weaknesses in key IT systems; failure could harm reporting reliability and valuation.
  - Insurance limits: potential gaps in coverage and exposure via captive insurer.

- Legal and compliance risks:
  - Litigation, regulatory inquiries, and governmental proceedings (including potential COVID‑19 related claims) may lead to substantial costs or adverse judgments.
  - Environmental, health, and safety regulation tightening (GHG/climate, materials restrictions) and stringent healthcare/food packaging rules could raise costs or limit materials.
  - Dependence on patents and proprietary technology; enforcement limits, competitive workarounds, and monitoring costs.

- Jurisdictional/shareholder risks (Jersey, Channel Islands):
  - Shareholder rights and corporate law differ from U.S. norms; potential changes may reduce investor protections.
  - Difficulty for U.S. investors to serve or enforce judgments abroad; exclusive forum provisions favor the Royal Court of Jersey for certain disputes.

structure.title: Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.heading: Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations
structure.start_phrase: Management’ s Discussion and Analysis should be read in conjunct ion with the Consolidated Financial Statements and related Not es included in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K.
structure.summary:
- Scope and purpose: Management’s Discussion and Analysis for Amcor plc covering FY2020 vs. FY2019, to be read with the consolidated financial statements.

- Company overview: Global packaging leader serving food, beverage, pharmaceutical, medical, home and personal-care markets; ~47,000 employees, ~231 sites in 40+ countries; focus on lightweight, recyclable/reusable packaging with more recycled content.

- COVID-19 impacts:
  - Operations largely deemed essential; minimal disruptions but notable volatility in demand (especially Rigid Packaging in on-the-go channels).
  - Comprehensive health/safety measures, business continuity plans, active supply chain monitoring.
  - Community support initiatives (donations and funding).
  - Outlook remains uncertain regarding duration, severity, and macro recovery.

- Bemis acquisition and integration:
  - Completed June 2019 for $5.2B all-stock; $1.4B debt assumed.
  - Targeting ~$180M pre-tax synergies by FY2022.
  - 2019 Bemis Integration Plan: ~$200M total integration costs (approx. $165M restructuring/related, $35M general integration), ~$150M cash outflows expected; FY2020 cash payments ~$80M; primarily impacts Flexibles and Corporate; completion expected by FY2022.

- Other restructuring:
  - 2018 Rigid Packaging Restructuring Plan: ~$110M expected costs (increased by ~$15M in FY2020), focus on footprint optimization and overhead reduction; completion expected FY2021.
  - 2016 Flexibles Restructuring Plan: ~$230.8M costs; substantially completed FY2019.

- Impairments and special accounting:
  - Equity method investment in AMVIG impaired: $25.6M (2020), with prior impairments in 2019 and 2018.
  - Highly inflationary accounting in Argentina (from July 2018): negative impacts of $27.7M (2020) and $30.2M (2019).

- Consolidated results (FY2020 vs. FY2019):
  - Net sales up 31.8% to $12.47B; growth primarily from Bemis; currency and lower raw material pass-through reduced reported growth; volumes roughly flat, slight unfavorable price/mix.
  - Operating income up to $994.0M; net income attributable to Amcor up 42.3% to $612.2M.
  - Diluted EPS up to $0.382; share count higher due to Bemis.
  - Gross margin expanded to 20.3% (from 19.0%).
  - SG&A and R&D higher, reflecting Bemis base and integration/transaction costs.
  - Restructuring and related costs lower year over year.
  - Other income declined due to nonrecurrence of prior-year remedy gains; interest expense stable; interest income up; other non-operating income improved (Bemis pension impacts).
  - Income tax expense higher on increased profit; effective tax rate fell to 22.6% (fewer non-deductible Bemis transaction costs; greater U.S. mix).

- Segment performance:
  - Flexibles: Net sales up 48.5% (strong acquisition effect); Adjusted EBIT up 63.4% to $1,335.1M; benefits from plant, SG&A cost improvements and synergies; slight unfavorable price/mix.
  - Rigid Packaging: Net sales down 6.1%; Adjusted EBIT down 5.9% to $290.1M; favorable costs and volumes offset by unfavorable price/mix and COVID-19 channel pressure.

- Non-GAAP measures:
  - Use of Adjusted EBIT, adjusted net income, and net debt to assess performance; reconciliations provided.
  - FY2020 Adjusted EBIT: $1,497.1M; adjusted net income from continuing operations: $1,027.9M.
  - Adjustments include restructuring, acquisition-related costs (inventory step-up, advisory/legal), amortization of acquired intangibles, hyperinflation impacts, pension settlements, and other specified items.

- Capital structure, liquidity, and cash flows:
  - Net debt ~$5.49B (total debt $6.23B; cash $0.74B).
  - Operating cash flow increased to $1.38B (benefit from Bemis).
  - Investing cash inflow $37.9M (remedy proceeds), with higher capex of $399.5M post-acquisition.
  - Financing cash outflow $1.24B, driven by $500M on-market share buyback; continued dividends ($761.1M).
  - Available undrawn credit facilities ~$1.8B; investment-grade ratings maintained.
  - 2020 funding actions: extended and then canceled 364-day facility; issued $500M 10-year USD and €500M 7-year senior unsecured notes; filed S-3 shelf.
  - Commercial paper usage backstopped by committed bank facilities; detailed liquidity risk framework and covenant compliance.
  - Contractual obligations schedule provided (debt, interest, leases, purchase obligations, benefits); no significant off-balance sheet arrangements beyond disclosed commitments.
  - Share repurchases: $500M program completed (53.9M shares canceled); treasury shares activity for compensation.

- Supplemental guarantor information:
  - Listing of guaranteed senior notes by Amcor Finance (USA), Bemis, and Amcor UK Finance; guarantee structure among Amcor plc and key subsidiaries.
  - Combined obligor group summarized financial statements presented under amended SEC rules.

- Critical accounting estimates and judgments:
  - Pensions (assumptions, sensitivity, expense outlook).
  - Goodwill and intangible asset valuation and impairment testing (methods and key assumptions).
  - Deferred taxes and uncertain tax positions (valuation allowances, judgments).
  - Equity method investments (other-than-temporary impairment assessment).
  - Acquisition fair value measurements (valuation techniques and assumptions).
  - Consideration of COVID-19 in all relevant estimates.

- New accounting pronouncements: Referenced in the notes to the financial statements.

structure.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.heading: Item 7A. Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk
structure.start_phrase: Our activities expose us to a variety of market risks and financial ri sks.
structure.summary:
- The section outlines Amcor’s market and financial risk management framework, including centralized hedging under defined authorities, use of foreign exchange contracts, commodity fixed-price swaps (some on behalf of customers), and interest rate swaps; no speculative trading. Some instruments are economic hedges but may not qualify for hedge accounting under U.S. GAAP, which can increase income statement volatility. The company may also use non-functional currency loans to economically hedge net investments in non-U.S. subsidiaries.
- It notes no material changes in the nature of risks vs. prior periods, but highlights increased volatility linked to COVID-19 across interest rate, foreign exchange, commodity/raw material, and credit risks in fiscal 2020 and 2019.
- Interest rate risk: Managed via a mix of fixed and variable debt and interest rate swaps. A 1% rise in relevant USD floating rates would have reduced fiscal 2020 income before taxes and equity in affiliates by $17.1 million.
- Foreign exchange risk: Operations in 40+ countries; exposure to currency movements and translation effects. A 1% adverse change in the average EUR exchange rate would have lowered fiscal 2020 net sales by $22.3 million. Net sales by functional currency: USD entities 49% (2020) and 36% (2019); EUR entities 18% (2020) and 24% (2019); other currencies 33% (2020) and 40% (2019).
- Raw material and commodity price risk: Key inputs include resins, film, aluminum, liquids, and other materials (inks, solvents, adhesives) plus energy. Contractual mechanisms often allow pass-through of input cost changes, but timing and recovery vary by material and market. A 1% increase in resin/film/aluminum/liquid prices not passed to customers would have reduced income by $56.9 million (2020) and $41.4 million (2019).
- Credit risk: Arises from deposits, FX and other financial transactions, and OTC commodity derivatives. Managed via counterparty limits, approved high-quality institutions, and defined dealing/settlement procedures. No significant concentration of derivative-related credit risk as of June 30, 2020 and 2019.

- Revenue recognition: All revenue arises from contracts with customers for flexible and rigid packaging. Contracts are typically purchase orders, with or without master supply agreements. Revenue recognized at a point in time upon shipment when control transfers, net of returns/claims and taxes; no material contract assets or liabilities; revenue disaggregated by geography.
- Significant judgments in revenue: Single performance obligation to supply packaging. Variable consideration (discounts, rebates, incentives) estimated using the most-likely-amount method and updated each period. Up-front customer payments are deferred (prepaid/other assets) and recognized as reductions of revenue over contract terms.
- Practical expedients: External sales commissions expensed as incurred (amortization period ≤ one year). Shipping and handling treated as fulfillment costs (in cost of products sold) while related billings are in net sales. Government-assessed transactional taxes excluded from transaction price (and from net sales). No time value of money adjustment when payment/performance timing differences are ≤ one year.
- Research and development: Expensed as incurred.
- Restructuring costs: Recognized when a liability is incurred; severance recorded when probable, estimable, and a plan is committed (policy discussion continues beyond the excerpt).

- Revenue recognition policy: the company sells flexible and rigid packaging across food, consumer, and healthcare markets; contracts are primarily purchase orders or combined with master supply agreements; revenue is recognized at a point in time upon shipment when control transfers; net of returns and claims; taxes collected from customers are excluded; no material contract assets or liabilities; revenue is disaggregated by geography.
- Significant judgments: concludes a single performance obligation to supply packaging; variable consideration (e.g., prompt payment discounts, rebates, incentives) estimated using the most likely amount method based on forecasts and updated each period; upfront customer payments/incentives are deferred as assets and recognized as reductions to revenue over the contract term.
- Practical expedients: external sales commissions expensed as incurred and included in SG&A; shipping and handling treated as fulfillment costs in cost of products sold, with related billings included in net sales; government-assessed taxes collected from customers excluded from the transaction price and net sales; no time value of money adjustment when payment timing is one year or less.
- Research and development costs are expensed as incurred.
- Restructuring costs are recognized when liabilities are incurred; severance is recorded when probable, estimable, and the company is committed to the plan, based on standard customary practices.

nodes.title: Significant Judgments
nodes.heading: Significant Judgments
nodes.start_phrase: Determining whether products and services are considered distinct pe rformance obligations that should be accounted for separately versus together may require significant judgment.
nodes.summary:
- Highly inflationary accounting: Recognized impacts of $27.7 million (FY2020) and $30.2 million (FY2019) in the consolidated statement of income.
- Revenue recognition:
  - Business model: Sells flexible and rigid packaging to food, consumer products, and healthcare markets.
  - Contract types: Purchase orders, and purchase orders combined with master supply, pricing, or quality agreements; all revenue is from contracts with customers.
  - Timing: Revenue recognized at a point in time upon shipment when control transfers.
  - Presentation: Net of returns and customer claims; excludes taxes collected for remittance to authorities.
  - Contract balances: No material contract assets or liabilities.
  - Disaggregation: Revenue broken out by geography (referenced in Segments note).
- Significant judgments:
  - Performance obligations: Single obligation to supply packaging; other potential obligations in master agreements are not distinct.
  - Variable consideration: Includes prompt payment discounts, rebates, and incentives; measured using the most likely amount based on forecasted sales and updated each period.
  - Customer incentives: Up-front payments under long-term agreements deferred as assets and recognized as reductions to revenue over the contract term.
- Practical expedients and related policies:
  - Sales channel: Primarily direct sales force; external sales commissions expensed as incurred (amortization period ≤ one year) within SG&A.
  - Shipping/handling: Treated as fulfillment costs in cost of products sold; amounts billed to customers recorded in net sales.
  - Taxes: Government-assessed transactional taxes excluded from transaction price and net sales.
  - Financing component: No time value of money adjustment when payment-performance timing is ≤ one year.
- Other policies:
  - Research and development: Expensed as incurred.
  - Restructuring: Costs recognized when liability is incurred; severance based on customary practices; provisions recorded when probable, estimable, and the plan is committed (text ends thereafter).

nodes.title: Practical Expedients
nodes.heading: Practical Expedients
nodes.start_phrase: The Company sells primarily through its direct sales force.
nodes.summary:
- Notes amounts related to highly inflationary accounting recognized in the consolidated statement of income: $27.7 million (FY2020) and $30.2 million (FY2019).
- Describes revenue recognition for sales of flexible and rigid packaging to food, consumer products, and healthcare markets, primarily under purchase orders and/or master supply agreements; all revenue is from contracts with customers.
- Performance obligation is typically satisfied at a point in time upon shipment when control transfers; revenue reported net of returns/claims and taxes remitted to authorities.
- States there are no material contract assets or contract liabilities; revenue is disaggregated by geography (referenced in Note 20, “Segments”).
- Significant judgments: determines that master supply agreement components are not distinct; concludes a single performance obligation to supply packaging.
- Variable consideration (e.g., prompt payment discounts, sales rebates, incentives tied to metrics like volume) is estimated using the most likely amount method, updated each period based on forecasts and agreement-specific rebate percentages.
- Up-front payments under long-term customer agreements are deferred in prepaid/other assets and recognized as reductions to revenue over the contract term.
- Practical expedients/policies: external sales commissions (primarily direct sales model) expensed as incurred and included in SG&A; shipping/handling treated as fulfillment costs in cost of products sold, with related billings included in net sales; government-assessed taxes excluded from transaction price and not included in net sales; no time value of money adjustment when payment-performance timing is one year or less.
- Research and development costs are expensed as incurred.
- Restructuring costs are recognized when the liability is incurred; severance provisions recorded when probable, estimable, and the company is committed to the plan, based on standard customary practices.

nodes.title: Research and Development
nodes.heading: Research and Development:
nodes.start_phrase: Research and development expenditures are expensed as incurred.
nodes.summary:
- Notes highly inflationary accounting impacts recorded in the consolidated statement of income: $27.7 million (FY 2020) and $30.2 million (FY 2019).
- Revenue recognition policies for flexible and rigid packaging sold to food, consumer products, and healthcare markets:
  - Contracts primarily consist of purchase orders, sometimes with master supply agreements; all revenue is from contracts with customers.
  - Performance obligation satisfied at a point in time upon shipment when control transfers.
  - Revenue recognized net of returns, customer claims, and taxes collected for remittance; no material contract assets or liabilities.
  - Revenue disaggregated by geography (referenced in Segment note).
- Significant judgments in revenue recognition:
  - Determination that only one performance obligation exists (to supply packaging), as other potential obligations are not distinct.
  - Variable consideration (prompt payment discounts, rebates, incentives) estimated using the most-likely-amount method, based on forecasted sales and agreement-specific rebate percentages, updated each period.
  - Up-front payments under long-term customer agreements are deferred in prepaid/other assets and recognized as reductions to revenue over the contract term.
- Practical expedients and classifications:
  - External sales commissions expensed as incurred (amortization period one year or less) and recorded in SG&A.
  - Shipping and handling treated as fulfillment costs (cost of products sold); amounts billed to customers recorded in net sales.
  - Government-assessed taxes (e.g., sales, VAT, excise, use) excluded from transaction price and from net sales.
  - No time value of money adjustments when payment-performance timing differences are one year or less.
- Research and development costs expensed as incurred.
- Restructuring costs recognized when liabilities are incurred; severance provisions recorded when probable, estimable, and the plan is committed (policy based on standard customary practices).

nodes.title: Restructuring Costs
nodes.heading: Restructuring Costs:
nodes.start_phrase: Restructuring costs are recognized when the liability is incurred.
nodes.summary:
- Notes on highly inflationary accounting impacts recognized in the consolidated statement of income for fiscal 2020 and 2019.
- Revenue recognition policies for flexible and rigid packaging:
  - Contracts primarily via purchase orders and master supply agreements; all revenue treated as from contracts with customers.
  - Performance occurs at a point in time upon shipment when control transfers.
  - Revenue reported net of returns/claims and customer taxes; no material contract assets or liabilities.
  - Revenue disaggregated by geography (referenced to segment note).
- Significant judgments in revenue:
  - Assessment of performance obligations; concluded a single performance obligation to supply packaging.
  - Variable consideration (prompt payment discounts, rebates, incentives) estimated using the most likely amount based on forecasts and updated each period.
  - Customer contract incentives (up-front payments) deferred and recognized as a reduction of revenue over contract terms.
- Practical expedients and classifications:
  - External sales commissions expensed as incurred.
  - Shipping and handling treated as fulfillment costs (in cost of products sold); amounts billed included in net sales.
  - Taxes assessed on transactions (e.g., sales/VAT/excise/use taxes) excluded from transaction price and net sales.
  - No time value of money adjustment when payment-performance timing is one year or less.
- Research and development costs expensed as incurred.
- Restructuring accounting:
  - Recognition of severance and other liabilities when probable, estimable, and committed; absent standard practice, recognize when incurred.
  - Asset write-offs when committed and assets no longer in use; accelerated depreciation until use ceases.
  - Other restructuring costs (e.g., equipment relocation) recognized as incurred; reference to detailed note.
- Cash and cash equivalents:
  - Highly liquid investments with maturities of three months or less (including readily liquidatable CDs) carried at cost approximating fair value.
- Trade receivables, net:
  - Stated net of allowances for returns and doubtful accounts; allowance determined using customer credit factors, history, terms, macro trends, and status.
  - Disclosed allowance balances for 2020 and 2019; current-year allowance expense in SG&A.
  - Factoring arrangements accounted for under ASC 860:
    - True sales recorded as reductions of receivables and operating cash inflows.
    - Non-qualifying transfers treated as secured borrowings within receivables and short-term debt.
    - Factoring costs primarily reduce net sales; disclosed balances for non-true-sale arrangements in 2020 and 2019.
- Inventories:
  - Measured at lower of FIFO cost or net realizable value; FIFO approximates replacement cost.
  - Breakdown provided for raw materials/supplies, WIP/finished goods, and reserves; net inventory totals disclosed for 2020 and 2019.
- Property, plant and equipment:
  - Carried at cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment; includes capitalized interest on construction.
  - Straight-line depreciation over useful lives or lease term (if shorter) including finance-leased assets and leasehold improvements.
  - Periodic review and prospective changes to useful lives; maintenance and repairs expensed.

nodes.title: Cash and Cash Equivalents
nodes.heading: Cash and Cash Equivalents:
nodes.start_phrase: The Company considers all highly liquid temporary investments wi th a maturity of three months or less when purchased to be cash equivalent s.
nodes.summary:
- Restructuring accounting: Severance liabilities recognized when incurred; fixed assets to be disposed are written off once disposal is committed and assets are no longer in use; depreciation is accelerated while assets continue to be used until use ceases; relocation and other restructuring costs are expensed as incurred. Reference to Note 6, “Restructuring Plans.”
- Cash and cash equivalents: Highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less, including penalty-free certificates of deposit; carried at cost approximating fair value.
- Trade receivables, net: Stated net of allowances for returns and doubtful accounts; collectability assessed using customer creditworthiness, history, payment practices, industry/economic trends, and current status. Allowance for doubtful accounts was $35.3 million at June 30, 2020 and $34.4 million at June 30, 2019; related expense recorded in SG&A.
- Receivables factoring (ASC 860): True sales (no recourse, no control retained) reduce trade receivables; proceeds presented in operating cash flows. Transactions not qualifying as true sales are treated as secured borrowings and recorded in trade receivables, net and short-term debt; factoring costs primarily reduce net sales. Factored receivables accounted for as secured borrowings were $0 at June 30, 2020 and $152.7 million at June 30, 2019.
- Inventories: Carried at lower of cost (FIFO) or net realizable value; FIFO approximates replacement cost. Balances at June 30, 2020 vs. 2019 (in millions): raw materials and supplies $808.6/$864.6; work in process and finished goods $1,127.6/$1,180.9; reserves $(104.3)/$(91.7); inventory, net $1,831.9/$1,953.8.
- Property, plant and equipment, net: Recorded at cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment; includes capitalized construction-period interest; repairs and maintenance expensed. Depreciated on a straight-line basis over estimated useful lives or lease term (for leasehold improvements and leased assets); useful lives reviewed periodically.

nodes.title: Trade Receivables, Net
nodes.heading: Trade Receivables, Net:
nodes.start_phrase: Trade accounts receivable, net, are stated at the amount the Com pany expects to collect, which is net of an allowance for sales ret urns and the estimated losses resulting from the inability of its customers to make required payments.
nodes.summary:
- Restructuring accounting: Recognizes severance liabilities when incurred; writes off fixed assets once committed to disposal and no longer in use; accelerates depreciation on assets still in use until cessation; records relocation and other costs as incurred. References Note 6 for details.
- Cash and cash equivalents: Includes highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less (e.g., readily liquidatable CDs); carried at cost approximating fair value.
- Trade receivables, net: Presented net of allowances for sales returns and doubtful accounts; collectability assessed using customer credit factors, history, terms, macro trends, and current aging. Allowance balances were $35.3 million (2020) and $34.4 million (2019); related expense recorded in SG&A.
- Receivables factoring (ASC 860): True sales (without recourse) reduce trade receivables and are included in operating cash flows; arrangements not qualifying as true sales are treated as secured borrowings, reflected in trade receivables and short-term debt; factoring costs primarily reduce net sales. Non-true-sale amounts were $0 (2020) and $152.7 million (2019).
- Inventories: Stated at lower of cost (FIFO) or net realizable value. Balances at June 30 (in millions): raw materials/supplies $808.6 (2020), $864.6 (2019); WIP/finished goods $1,127.6, $1,180.9; reserves $(104.3), $(91.7); net inventory $1,831.9, $1,953.8.
- Property, plant and equipment: Carried at cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment; includes capitalized interest on construction; routine maintenance expensed. Depreciated straight-line over useful lives or lease term (for leasehold/leased assets); useful lives reviewed and adjusted prospectively.

nodes.title: Inventories
nodes.heading: Inventories:
nodes.start_phrase: Inventories are valued primarily at the lower of cost, as determined by the first-in, first-out ("FIFO") method, or net realizable value.
nodes.summary:
- Restructuring accounting policies: recognition of severance liabilities when incurred per communicated plans or legal/local practice; write-off of fixed assets committed for disposal and no longer in use; accelerated depreciation on assets used temporarily until taken out of service; other costs (e.g., equipment relocation) expensed as incurred. Reference to Note 6 for more details.
- Cash and cash equivalents: highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less, including readily liquidatable certificates of deposit; carried at cost approximating fair value.
- Trade receivables, net: presented net of allowances for returns and doubtful accounts; allowance determined using customer-specific factors (creditworthiness, history, terms) plus macro and portfolio considerations. Allowance balances were $35.3 million (2020) and $34.4 million (2019); current-year adjustments recorded in SG&A.
- Receivables factoring: accounted for under ASC 860. True sales without recourse reduce trade receivables and are included in operating cash flows. Transactions not qualifying as true sales are treated as secured borrowings, recorded within trade receivables, net, and short-term debt; related costs primarily reduce net sales. Non-true-sale factored amounts were $0 (2020) and $152.7 million (2019).
- Inventories: valued at lower of cost (FIFO) or net realizable value; FIFO approximates replacement cost. Balances at June 30: raw materials/supplies $808.6m (2020), $864.6m (2019); WIP and finished goods $1,127.6m (2020), $1,180.9m (2019); reserves $(104.3)m (2020), $(91.7)m (2019); inventory, net $1,831.9m (2020) and $1,953.8m (2019).
- Property, plant and equipment, net: carried at cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment; includes capitalized interest on constructed assets. Maintenance and repairs expensed as incurred. Depreciation (including for finance leases) on a straight-line basis over estimated useful lives, or lease term for leasehold improvements/leased assets if shorter; useful lives reviewed periodically and adjusted prospectively.

nodes.title: Property, Plant and Equipment, Net
nodes.heading: Property, Plant and Equipment, Net:
nodes.start_phrase: Property, plant and equipment ("PP&E"), net is carried at cost less accumulated depreciation and impairment and includes expenditure s for new facilities and equipment and those costs which substantially increase the useful li ves or capacity of existing PP&E.
nodes.summary:
- Restructuring accounting: Recognizes severance when incurred per policy or local practice; writes off fixed assets when committed for disposal and no longer in use; accelerates depreciation on assets still in temporary use until cease-use; other costs (e.g., equipment relocation) expensed as incurred. References Note 6 on restructuring plans.
- Cash and cash equivalents: Highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less, including penalty-free CDs; carried at cost approximating fair value.
- Trade receivables: Reported net of allowances for returns and doubtful accounts; allowance based on creditworthiness, history, terms, macro/industry trends, and account status. Allowance totaled $35.3 million (2020) and $34.4 million (2019); current-year provisions recorded in SG&A.
- Receivables factoring (ASC 860): True sales (without recourse) reduce trade receivables and appear in operating cash flows; arrangements retaining effective control are secured borrowings recorded in trade receivables and short-term debt. Factored receivables as secured borrowings were $0 (2020) and $152.7 million (2019). Factoring costs primarily reduce net sales.
- Inventories: Stated at lower of cost (FIFO) or net realizable value; FIFO approximates replacement cost. Balances at June 30 (in millions): 2020—Raw materials $808.6, WIP/finished $1,127.6, reserves $(104.3), net $1,831.9; 2019—Raw materials $864.6, WIP/finished $1,180.9, reserves $(91.7), net $1,953.8.
- Property, plant and equipment: Carried at cost less depreciation and impairment; capitalizes construction-period interest; routine maintenance expensed. Straight-line lives: leasehold land over lease term; land improvements up to 30 years; buildings up to 45; plant/equipment up to 25; finance leases shorter of lease term or 5–25 years. Tax depreciation generally accelerated; related deferred taxes recognized.
- Impairment of long-lived assets: Tests PP&E and finite-lived intangibles when indicators arise; if undiscounted cash flows are less than carrying value, writes down to fair value (market quotes, DCF, or appraisals). Impairment losses (in millions): 2020—SG&A $0.7, restructuring $20.8, total $21.5; 2019—SG&A $47.7, restructuring $27.4, total $75.1; 2018—SG&A $0.4, restructuring $4.0, total $4.4.
- Leasing: Operating leases for facilities, land, vehicles, equipment. Recognizes right-of-use assets and lease liabilities at present value of lease payments, including reasonably certain renewals; uses incremental borrowing rate; straight-line lease expense. Short-term leases (≤12 months) not capitalized. Variable payments excluded from measurement and expensed as incurred.
- Goodwill: Not amortized; tested annually or upon triggering events. COVID-19 impacts assessed in Q3 FY2020 with no triggering event as of March 31, 2020. Goodwill assigned to operating-segment reporting units; post-Bemis acquisition, Flexibles Americas split into Flexibles North America and Flexibles Latin America, resulting in six goodwill-reporting units. Impairment testing may use a qualitative screen; quantitative tests use discounted cash flows sensitive to assumptions (e.g., revenue growth).

nodes.title: Impairment of Long-lived Assets
nodes.heading: Impairment of Long-lived Assets:
nodes.start_phrase: The Company reviews long-lived assets, primarily PP&E and certain ide ntifiable intangible assets with finite lives, for impairment when facts or circumstances indicate the carrying amount of an asset or asset group may not be recove rable.
nodes.summary:
- Depreciation and useful lives: Leasehold land over lease term; land improvements up to 30 years; buildings up to 45 years; plant and equipment up to 25 years; finance leases depreciated over the shorter of the lease term or 5–25 years. For tax, accelerated depreciation methods are used, with deferred taxes recorded for book–tax differences.
- Impairment of long‑lived assets: PP&E and finite‑lived intangibles are tested for impairment when indicators arise. Recoverability is assessed using undiscounted cash flows; if not recoverable, assets are written down to fair value determined via market quotes, discounted cash flows, or appraisals. Impairment losses recorded (in millions): total $21.5 (2020), $75.1 (2019), $4.4 (2018), split between SG&A ($0.7, $47.7, $0.4) and restructuring and related expenses ($20.8, $27.4, $4.0).
- Leasing (operating leases): Recognition of right‑of‑use assets and lease liabilities at commencement based on the present value of lease payments over the lease term, including renewal options reasonably certain to be exercised. Uses incremental borrowing rate when no implicit rate is provided. Lease expense recognized on a straight‑line basis. Short‑term leases (12 months or less) are not recognized on the balance sheet. Variable lease payments not tied to an index/rate are excluded from measurement and expensed as incurred.
- Goodwill: Not amortized; tested annually or upon triggering events. COVID‑19‑related review in Q3 FY2020 indicated no impairment trigger as of March 31, 2020. Following the Bemis acquisition, the Company reorganized segments, creating six reporting units with goodwill. Impairment testing may begin with a qualitative assessment; if needed, a quantitative test uses discounted cash flows, which are sensitive to assumptions such as revenue growth and market factors.

nodes.title: Leasing
nodes.heading: Leasing:
nodes.start_phrase: The Company has operating leases for certain manufacturing sites, offi ce space, warehouses, land, vehicles and equipment.
nodes.summary:
- Depreciation policies and useful lives:
  - Leasehold land: over lease term
  - Land improvements: up to 30 years
  - Buildings: up to 45 years
  - Plant and equipment: up to 25 years
  - Finance leases: shorter of lease term or 5–25 years
  - For tax, accelerated depreciation methods are used; related book–tax differences are recognized as deferred income taxes.

- Impairment of long‑lived assets (PP&E and finite‑lived intangibles):
  - Reviewed when indicators suggest carrying amounts may not be recoverable.
  - If undiscounted cash flows are less than carrying value, assets are written down to fair value, determined via market quotes, discounted cash flows, or external appraisals.
  - Impairment losses recognized (in millions):
    - 2020: total $21.5 (SG&A $0.7; Restructuring $20.8)
    - 2019: total $75.1 (SG&A $47.7; Restructuring $27.4)
    - 2018: total $4.4 (SG&A $0.4; Restructuring $4.0)

- Leasing (operating leases for manufacturing sites, offices, warehouses, land, vehicles, equipment):
  - Recognize right‑of‑use assets and lease liabilities at commencement based on the present value of remaining lease payments, including renewal options reasonably certain to be exercised.
  - Use incremental borrowing rate when no implicit rate is available.
  - Short‑term leases (12 months or less, including reasonably certain holding periods) are not recorded on the balance sheet.
  - Lease expense recognized on a straight‑line basis; variable payments not dependent on an index/rate are excluded from measurement and expensed as incurred.
  - Leases are reevaluated regularly for renewal option economics/strategy.

- Goodwill:
  - Not amortized; tested annually or upon triggering events.
  - COVID‑19 impacts considered in Q3 FY2020; no triggering event identified as of March 31, 2020.
  - Goodwill assigned to reporting units (operating segments). Following the Bemis acquisition, Flexibles Americas was disaggregated into Flexibles North America and Flexibles Latin America, resulting in six reporting units tested for impairment.
  - Impairment testing allows an initial qualitative screen; if needed, a quantitative test uses discounted cash flow methods, with key assumptions including revenue growth and other market factors.

nodes.title: Goodwill
nodes.heading: Goodwill:
nodes.start_phrase: Goodwill represents the excess of cost over the fair value of net assets acquired in a business combination.
nodes.summary:
- Depreciation and useful lives:
  - Leasehold land: over lease term; land improvements: up to 30 years; buildings: up to 45 years; plant and equipment: up to 25 years; finance leases: shorter of lease term or 5–25 years.
  - For tax, accelerated depreciation methods are used; differences vs. book depreciation are recorded as deferred income taxes.

- Impairment of long‑lived assets:
  - PP&E and finite‑lived intangibles are reviewed for impairment upon indicators; recoverability based on undiscounted cash flows; write‑downs to fair value using market quotes, discounted cash flows, or appraisals.
  - Impairment losses recognized in the consolidated statement of income (in millions):
    - 2020: SG&A $0.7, Restructuring $20.8, Total $21.5
    - 2019: SG&A $47.7, Restructuring $27.4, Total $75.1
    - 2018: SG&A $0.4, Restructuring $4.0, Total $4.4

- Leasing policy:
  - Operating leases for facilities, land, vehicles, and equipment; recognize right‑of‑use assets and lease liabilities at commencement based on present value of remaining payments, including reasonably certain renewals.
  - Short‑term leases (≤12 months) not recorded on balance sheet.
  - Incremental borrowing rate used when implicit rate is unavailable.
  - Lease expense recognized on a straight‑line basis; variable payments not based on an index/rate are excluded from measurement and expensed as incurred.

- Goodwill:
  - Not amortized; tested annually in Q4 or upon triggering events (e.g., performance declines, competitive pressures, market changes). COVID‑19 considered; no triggering event as of March 31, 2020.
  - Reporting units align with operating segments; following the Bemis acquisition, Flexibles Americas split into Flexibles North America and Flexibles Latin America, resulting in six goodwill‑bearing reporting units.
  - Testing approach allows qualitative screening; if necessary, quantitative fair value via discounted cash flows using assumptions for revenue growth, operating income growth, terminal value, and discount rates.
  - Annual tests: quantitative in 2020 and 2018; qualitative in 2019; no impairments, and management noted no subsequent impairment indicators through June 30, 2020.

- Other intangible assets:
  - Finite‑lived intangibles amortized straight‑line over 1–20 years; tested for impairment upon indicators and written down to fair value if impaired.
  - Internal‑use software development costs capitalized within intangible assets.

- Fair value measurements:
  - Fair values reflect exit prices; hierarchy applied:
    - Level 1: quoted prices in active markets,
    - Level 2: observable inputs (direct or corroborated),
    - Level 3: unobservable inputs (internal models).

- Financial instruments and hedging:
  - All derivatives recorded at fair value.
  - Non‑designated derivatives: changes recognized in income.
  - Designated hedges: effective portions offset changes in hedged items in earnings or are recorded in OCI until recognition; hedge ineffectiveness recognized in earnings.
  - Instruments include FX forwards, currency swaps, and interest rate swaps (see Note 11).

- Employee benefit plans:
  - Defined contribution plans with expenses of $63.5 million (2020), $39.9 million (2019), and $39.8 million (2018).

nodes.title: Other Intangible Assets, Net
nodes.heading: Other Intangible Assets, Net:
nodes.start_phrase: Contractual or separable intangible assets that have finite us eful lives are amortized against income using the straight-line meth od over their estimated useful lives, with original periods ranging from one to 20 years.
nodes.summary:
- Goodwill impairment testing: Annual assessment in Q4 using quantitative analyses in FY2020 and FY2018 and a qualitative analysis in FY2019; no impairments identified and fair values substantially exceeded carrying amounts in 2020 and 2018. Post-assessment review, including COVID-19 considerations as of June 30, 2020, indicated no triggering events for impairment.
- Other intangible assets: Finite-lived intangibles amortized straight-line over 1–20 years; impairment testing performed upon indicators using undiscounted cash flows, with write-downs to fair value via discounted cash flows or appraisals if impaired. Internal-use software development costs are capitalized within other intangible assets.
- Fair value measurements: Assets and liabilities measured at exit price using a three-level hierarchy—Level 1 (quoted prices in active markets), Level 2 (observable inputs), Level 3 (unobservable inputs/models).
- Financial instruments and derivatives: All derivatives recognized at fair value; accounting depends on hedge designation and effectiveness. Non-designated derivatives flow through earnings; designated hedges recorded in earnings or OCI consistent with the hedged item, with hedge ineffectiveness recognized in earnings. References to use of FX forwards, currency swaps, and interest rate swaps.
- Employee benefit plans: Sponsorship of defined contribution plans with recognized expenses of $63.5 million (2020), $39.9 million (2019), and $39.8 million (2018).

nodes.title: Fair Value Measurements
nodes.heading: Fair Value Measurements:
nodes.start_phrase: The fair values of the Company's financial assets and financial lia bilities reflect the amounts that would be received to sell the asse ts or paid to transfer the liabilities in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement dat e (exit price).
nodes.summary:
- Goodwill impairment testing: Valuations consider operating income growth, terminal values, and discount rates. Annual impairment analysis is performed in Q4. Quantitative tests were done in FY2020 and FY2018; a qualitative test was done in FY2019. In all three years, no goodwill impairment was identified, and in FY2020 and FY2018 fair values substantially exceeded carrying amounts. Management also assessed subsequent events, including COVID-19 impacts as of June 30, 2020, and concluded no impairment indicators were present.
- Other intangible assets: Finite‑lived intangibles are amortized on a straight‑line basis over 1–20 years, reflecting the pattern of economic benefits. These assets are tested for impairment upon indicators; if impaired, they are written down to fair value using discounted cash flows or appraisals. Internal‑use software development costs are capitalized within intangible assets.
- Fair value measurements: Fair value is an exit price measured using a three‑level hierarchy:
  • Level 1: quoted prices in active markets for identical items.
  • Level 2: directly or indirectly observable inputs corroborated by market data.
  • Level 3: unobservable inputs, including internal models where market activity is limited.
- Financial instruments and derivatives: All derivatives are recognized at fair value on the balance sheet. For derivatives not designated as hedges, changes flow through earnings. For designated hedges, changes either offset hedged items in earnings or are recorded in other comprehensive income and reclassified when the hedged item affects earnings; hedge ineffectiveness is recognized in earnings. Instruments include FX forwards, currency swaps, and interest rate swaps (see Note 11).
- Employee benefits: The company sponsors defined contribution plans; expenses were $63.5 million (FY2020), $39.9 million (FY2019), and $39.8 million (FY2018).

nodes.title: Financial Instruments
nodes.heading: Financial Instruments:
nodes.start_phrase: The Company recognizes all derivative instruments on the consolidated balance sheet at fair value.
nodes.summary:
- Goodwill impairment: Annual testing in Q4; quantitative analyses in FY2018 and FY2020 and qualitative in FY2019, all concluding no impairment with fair values substantially exceeding carrying amounts. Management reassessed at June 30, 2020, including COVID-19 impacts, and determined no impairment indicators. Notes that changes in discount rates, growth/margins, or macro conditions could cause future impairments.
- Finite-lived intangible assets: Amortized on a straight-line basis over 1–20 years to match economic benefits; tested for impairment upon indicators and written down to fair value using discounted cash flows or appraisals if not recoverable.
- Internal-use software: Development costs capitalized within other intangible assets.
- Fair value measurements: Defined as exit prices using a three-level hierarchy—Level 1 (quoted prices in active markets), Level 2 (observable inputs), Level 3 (unobservable inputs/models).
- Derivative financial instruments: Recognized at fair value on the balance sheet; accounting through earnings or other comprehensive income depends on hedge designation and effectiveness. Non-hedge derivatives flow through earnings; hedge ineffectiveness recognized in earnings. Instruments include FX forwards, currency swaps, and interest rate swaps (see Note 11).
- Employee benefit plans: Company sponsors defined contribution plans; expenses were $63.5 million (FY2020), $39.9 million (FY2019), and $39.8 million (FY2018).

nodes.title: Employee Benefit Plans
nodes.heading: Employee Benefit Plans:
nodes.start_phrase: The Company sponsors various defined contribution plans to which it make s contributions on behalf of employees.
nodes.summary:
- Goodwill: Annual impairment testing performed in Q4 (quantitative in 2020 and 2018; qualitative in 2019) with no impairments; fair values substantially exceeded carrying amounts. Post-assessment review through June 30, 2020, including COVID-19 considerations, indicated no triggering events.
- Other intangible assets: Finite-lived intangibles amortized straight-line over 1–20 years; tested for impairment upon indicators, written down to fair value if impaired. Internal-use software development costs are capitalized as intangible assets.
- Fair value measurements: Valuation based on exit price using a three-level hierarchy (Level 1 quoted prices, Level 2 observable inputs, Level 3 unobservable inputs/models).
- Financial instruments/derivatives: All derivatives recognized at fair value. Accounting depends on hedge designation and effectiveness; non-hedges through earnings; qualifying hedges recorded in earnings or OCI accordingly; hedge ineffectiveness recognized in earnings. References to currency and interest rate derivatives.
- Employee benefits: Defined contribution plan expenses were $63.5m (2020), $39.9m (2019), $39.8m (2018). Defined benefit plans rely on critical assumptions (discount rate, asset returns, salary inflation, mortality). Funded status recognized on the balance sheet; liabilities remeasured annually; use of 10% corridor amortization; service cost in operating income, other components in non-operating income.
- Equity method investments: Significant influence investments accounted for under the equity method; other-than-temporary impairments reset cost basis. Impairments recorded for AMVIG in each of the last three fiscal years.
- Share-based compensation: Expense for service/market condition awards recognized straight-line over vesting at grant-date fair value; performance condition awards reassessed each period; cash-settled awards treated as liabilities and remeasured; forfeitures estimated.
- Income taxes: Asset-liability method for deferred taxes; differences due to timing of recognition. Valuation allowances recorded when realization is not more likely than not. Uncertain tax positions assessed and accrued as needed; interest and penalties recorded in tax expense.

nodes.title: Equity Method Investments
nodes.heading: Equity Method Investments:
nodes.start_phrase: Investments in ordinary shares of companies, in which the Company belie ves it exercises significant influence over operating and financial p olicies, are accounted for using the equity method of accounting.
nodes.summary:
- Pension and postretirement benefits: The company sponsors defined benefit plans and deems related accounting estimates critical due to sensitivity to assumptions (long-term asset returns, discount rates, salary inflation, mortality, market conditions, actuarial valuations, and plan changes). Funded status is recognized on the balance sheet (overfunded as assets, underfunded as liabilities). Liabilities are remeasured annually or upon triggering events. Actuarial gains/losses beyond a 10% corridor and prior service costs are amortized straight-line over the average remaining service period or life expectancy for plans with many inactive participants. Service cost is in operating income; other components of net benefit cost are in other non-operating income (loss), net.
- Equity method investments: Investments with significant influence are accounted for under the equity method (cost adjusted for share of earnings/losses). Other-than-temporary impairments reset the cost basis and are not reversed. The company recorded impairment losses on its AMVIG Holdings Limited investment in each of the last three fiscal years.
- Share-based compensation: For awards with service or market conditions, expense is recognized straight-line over the vesting period using grant-date fair value and estimated forfeitures. For performance condition awards, vesting probability is reassessed each reporting period with cost adjusted accordingly. Cash-settled awards are liability-classified and remeasured to fair value each reporting period. Forfeiture estimates consider employee level, economic conditions, time to vest, and historical experience.
- Income taxes: The company applies the asset and liability method, recognizing deferred taxes for temporary differences and using enacted rates. Tax expense differs from current taxes payable due to timing differences. Deferred tax assets (including loss and credit carryforwards) are reduced by valuation allowances when realization is not more likely than not. The company evaluates and records uncertain tax positions under the prescribed recognition and measurement guidance, and records related interest and penalties as tax expense.

nodes.title: Share-based Compensation

nodes.summary:

Funded status is recognized on the balance sheet (overfunded as assets, underfunded as liabilities). Liabilities are remeasured annually or upon triggering events. Actuarial gains/losses beyond a 10% corridor and prior service costs are amortized straight-line over participants’ average remaining service or life expectancy. Service cost is in operating income; other net benefit components are in other non-operating income (loss).

- Equity method investments: Holdings with significant influence are accounted for under the equity method (cost adjusted for share of investee results). Other-than-temporary impairments reset the cost basis and are not reversed. The company has recognized recent impairments on its AMVIG Holdings Limited investment.

- Share-based compensation: For awards with service or market conditions, expense is recognized straight-line over the vesting period using grant-date fair value and estimated vesting. For performance conditions, vesting probability is reassessed each period with cost adjusted accordingly. Cash-settled awards are liability-classified and remeasured to fair value each reporting period. Forfeiture rates are estimated based on role, economic factors, time to vest, and history.

- Income taxes: The asset-liability method is used, recording deferred taxes for temporary differences and carryforwards using enacted rates. Tax expense differs from current payable due to timing differences. Deferred tax assets may be reduced by valuation allowances when realization is not more likely than not. Uncertain tax positions are evaluated under prescribed recognition/measurement guidance, with related interest and penalties recorded in the tax provision.

nodes.title: Income Taxes
nodes.heading: Income Taxes:
nodes.start_phrase: The Company uses the asset and liability method to account for incom e taxes.
nodes.summary:
- Defined benefit pension plans: Treatment relies on critical estimates (expected return on assets, discount rate, salary inflation, mortality and other actuarial assumptions). Funded status is recognized on the balance sheet (overfunded as assets, underfunded as liabilities). Plans are remeasured annually or upon triggering events. Actuarial gains/losses beyond a 10% corridor and prior service costs are amortized on a straight-line basis over average remaining service periods (or life expectancy for plans with many inactive participants). Service cost is in operating income; other net benefit cost components are in other non-operating income (loss), net.

- Equity method investments: Used when the Company has significant influence. Investments are carried at cost and adjusted for the Company’s share of post-acquisition earnings/losses. Other-than-temporary impairments reset the cost basis with no reversal for later recoveries. Recent impairments have been recognized for the AMVIG investment (see Note 7).

- Share-based compensation: For awards with service or market conditions, expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the vesting period using grant-date fair value and estimated forfeitures. For performance-condition awards, vesting probability is reassessed each period with corresponding cost adjustments. Cash-settled awards are treated as liabilities and remeasured to fair value each reporting period. Forfeiture estimates consider employee level, economic conditions, time to vest, and historical experience.

- Income taxes: Applies the asset-liability method. Deferred taxes arise from differences between tax bases and financial reporting amounts using enacted laws/rates; tax expense differs from current payable due to timing differences. Deferred tax assets (including loss and credit carryforwards) are reduced by a valuation allowance when realization is not more likely than not. The Company evaluates and records uncertain tax positions under prescribed recognition and measurement guidance; interest and penalties are recorded as tax expense (see Note 16).

nodes.title: New Accounting Guidance

No material impact on condensed consolidated financial statements.

nodes.title: Acquisitions and Divestitures
nodes.heading: Note 4 - Acquisitions and Divestitures
nodes.start_phrase: On June 11, 2019, the Company completed the acquisition of 100% of the outstanding shares of Bemis Company, Inc ("Bemis"), a global manufactu rer of flexible packaging products based in the United States.
nodes.summary: Note 4 details Amcor’s acquisition of Bemis Company, Inc., completed on June 11, 2019. Each Bemis share was exchanged for 5.1 Amcor ordinary shares, with 91.7 million Bemis shares outstanding, implying issuance of approximately 467.7 million Amcor shares. Using Amcor’s June 11, 2019 closing price of $11.18 per share, total equity consideration was $5,229.6 million. The acquisition aimed to position Amcor as a global leader in consumer packaging, expanding its flexible packaging footprint and scale across North America, Latin America, Asia Pacific, and Europe, and strengthening R&D capabilities. The transaction was accounted for as a business combination under ASC 805. The purchase price allocation was finalized in Q4 fiscal 2020, with measurement period adjustments resulting in a $229.9 million increase to goodwill, including a $210.6 million decrease to property, plant and equipment, a $99.0 million decrease to finite-lived intangibles, a $184.1 million decrease to deferred tax liabilities, a $97.9 million increase in other non-current liabilities, and other adjustments to assets held for sale and working capital.

nodes.title: Bemis Company, Inc.
nodes.heading: Bemis Company, Inc.

nodes.summary:

Measurement period adjustments increased goodwill by $229.9 million, driven by a $210.6 million decrease in property, plant and equipment, a $99.0 million decrease in finite-lived intangibles, a $184.1 million decrease in deferred tax liabilities, a $97.9 million increase in other non-current liabilities, and other working capital and held-for-sale adjustments.
- Final purchase price allocation (in millions): total identifiable assets $4,845.9; total liabilities assumed $2,983.9; net identifiable assets $1,862.0; goodwill $3,367.6; net assets acquired $5,229.6. Included within assets were $1,180.1 of PP&E, $1,931.2 of other intangible assets, $665.4 of inventories, and $464.2 of assets held for sale; liabilities included $1,365.3 of long-term debt and $598.5 of deferred tax liabilities.
- Identifiable intangible assets acquired (fair value and useful lives): customer relationships $1,650.0 (15 years), technology $110.0 (7 years), other $171.2 (7 years), totaling $1,931.2.
- Goodwill of $3,367.6 million allocated to the Flexibles Segment, not tax deductible; represents expected synergies and benefits from non-separable assets such as assembled workforce and non-contractual relationships.

nodes.title: Divestitures
nodes.heading: Divestitures
nodes.start_phrase: Closing of the Bemis acquisition was conditional upon the receipt of regulatory approvals, approval by both Amcor and Bemis shareholders, and s atisfaction of other customary conditions.
nodes.summary:
- The Bemis acquisition required regulatory and shareholder approvals and other customary conditions to close.
- To meet regulatory requirements, the company divested:
  - EC Remedy: three Bemis medical packaging facilities in the UK and Ireland, completed in Q1 FY2020; proceeds $397.1 million; recorded a $8.8 million loss due to reclassifying cumulative foreign currency translation from AOCI to discontinued operations.
  - U.S. Remedy: three Amcor medical packaging facilities in the U.S., completed in Q4 FY2019; proceeds $214.2 million; gain of $159.1 million.
- The company also sold an equity method investment acquired with Bemis in Q3 FY2020 for $27.7 million, with no gain as it was recorded at fair value upon acquisition.
- Unaudited pro forma information is presented as if the Bemis acquisition and both remedies occurred as of July 1, 2017, combining Amcor and Bemis historical results.
  - Pro forma results:
    - Net sales: $12,972.4 million (2019) and $13,146.3 million (2018).
    - Income from continuing operations: $565.5 million (2019) and $535.0 million (2018).
  - Pro forma adjustments:
    - Exclude net sales of the EC and U.S. Remedies.
    - Exclude income from the EC Remedy (discontinued operations) and the U.S. Remedy (reported in GAAP continuing operations).
    - Exclude acquisition-related charges.
    - Include acquisition accounting adjustments (e.g., amortization/depreciation from fair value step-ups to PP&E).
    - Exclude non-recurring purchase accounting impacts (inventory step-up and sales backlog amortization).
- The pro forma results are not indicative of actual or future results and do not reflect expected synergies or costs to achieve them.

nodes.title: Discontinued Operations
nodes.heading: Note 5 - Discontinued Operations

nodes.summary:

- Upon closing the Bemis acquisition on June 11, 2019, the EC Remedy was classified as a discontinued operation under ASC 205-20. The sale closed on August 8, 2019.

- Assets and liabilities of the EC Remedy (within the Flexibles Segment) were presented as held for sale on the June 30, 2019 consolidated balance sheet and measured at the lower of carrying value or fair value less costs to sell.
- Discontinued operations results (in millions):
  - 2020: Net sales $15.8; income (loss) from discontinued operations $(7.1); tax expense $(0.6); net loss from discontinued operations $(7.7).
  - 2019: Net sales $9.6; income from discontinued operations $0.9; tax expense $(0.2); net income from discontinued operations $0.7.

nodes.title: Restructuring Plans
nodes.heading: Note 6 - Restructuring Plans
nodes.start_phrase: In connection with the acquisition of Bemis, the Company initiat ed restructuring activities in the fourth quarter of 2019 aimed at integ rating and optimizing the combined organization.
nodes.summary:
- Note 6 outlines multiple restructuring and integration initiatives, including objectives, expected synergies, cost breakdowns (cash vs. non-cash), timing, and impacted segments.

- 2019 Bemis Integration Plan:
  - Purpose: Integrate and optimize the organization following the Bemis acquisition.
  - Synergy target: Approximately $180 million pre-tax by end of fiscal 2022 (procurement, supply chain, G&A).
  - Total integration costs: Approximately $200 million, including $165 million restructuring/related and $35 million general integration.
  - Restructuring/related breakdown: ~$90 million employee-related, ~$25 million fixed-asset related, ~$20 million other restructuring, ~$30 million restructuring-related.
  - Cash impact: About $150 million of total costs to be cash (including ~$115 million restructuring/related).
  - FY2020 cash payments: $80.2 million total, including $54.1 million restructuring/related.
  - Scope/timing: Affects Flexibles and Corporate; expected completion by end of fiscal 2022.
  - Notes: Restructuring-related costs are directly tied to restructuring but not accounted for as exit/disposal; general integration costs are separate. Restructuring-related costs primarily tied to facility closures, graphics changes, and training on relocated equipment.

- 2018 Rigid Packaging Restructuring Plan:
  - Announced August 21, 2018 to reduce structural costs and optimize the manufacturing footprint via facility closures, headcount reductions, productivity, and overhead improvements.
  - Total pre-tax restructuring costs: ~ $110 million, increased by ~$15 million in Q4 FY2020 due mainly to additional non-cash impairments.
  - Cash expenditures: ~$65–$70 million; FY2020 cash payments were $23.6 million.
  - Expected completion: Fiscal 2021.

- 2016 Flexibles Restructuring Plan:
  - Announced June 9, 2016 to optimize cost base and drive earnings in Flexibles by footprint optimization, capacity alignment, utilization improvements, and organizational streamlining (especially in Europe).
  - Actions: Closed eight manufacturing facilities; reduced headcount.
  - Total pre-tax restructuring costs: $230.8 million ($166.7 million employee terminations, $31.4 million fixed-asset impairments, $32.7 million other costs such as equipment dismantling and lease terminations).
  - Cash expenditures: ~ $166 million; FY2019 cash payments were $14.4 million.
  - Status: Substantially completed by end of fiscal 2019.

- Other Restructuring Plans:
  - Individually immaterial; restructuring charges of ~$17.9 million (FY2020), $18.8 million (FY2019), and $25.8 million (FY2018).
