nodes.title: Derivative Instruments
nodes.heading: Note 11 - Derivative Instruments
nodes.start_phrase: The Company periodically uses derivatives and other financial inst ruments to hedge exposures to interest rates, commodity and currency risk s.
nodes.summary: This note explains the company’s use of derivatives exclusively for risk management—not speculation—covering interest rate, foreign currency, and commodity exposures. It outlines formal hedge designations (fair value and cash flow) and ongoing effectiveness testing. For interest rate risk, the company manages a mix of fixed and variable debt and uses interest rate swaps, cross-currency interest rate swaps, and interest rate locks. Fair value hedge swaps and the related debt remeasurements are recognized in interest expense; non-designated swaps flow through other non-operating income (loss). Notional amounts of receive-fixed/pay-variable swaps were $837.1 million (2020) and $841.1 million (2019). A $100 million (€89.0 million) cross-currency interest rate swap position in 2020 was not hedge-designated, with changes recognized in earnings. In Q3 FY2020, the company executed $250.0 million of Treasury locks as a cash flow hedge for anticipated long-term debt; upon issuing unsecured senior notes on June 19, 2020, it settled the locks with a $19.8 million loss recorded in accumulated other comprehensive loss and amortized to interest expense over the notes’ 10-year life. For foreign currency risk, the company uses forward contracts, designating qualifying positions as cash flow hedges with effective portions in AOCI and reclassified to earnings when hedged transactions occur; ineffective portions and non-designated forwards are recognized in earnings. Outstanding forward notional was $1.6 billion (2020) versus $1.0 billion (2019). The company also uses foreign-currency borrowings as net investment hedges, recording effective portions in AOCI and ineffective amounts in other non-operating income (loss).

nodes.title: Interest Rate Risk
nodes.heading: Interest Rate Risk
nodes.start_phrase: The Company's policy is to manage exposure to interest rate risk by maintaining a mixture of fixed-rate and variable-rate debt, monitori ng global interest rates and, where appropriate, hedging floating interest rate exposure or debt at fixed interest rates through various interest rate derivative instruments including, but not limited to, i nterest rate swaps, cross-currency interest rate swaps, and interest rate locks.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Company’s use of derivative and other financial instruments to hedge interest rate, commodity, and foreign currency risks; no speculative trading; formal hedge designation and ongoing effectiveness assessments for qualifying hedges.
- Interest rate risk management:
  - Strategy: Maintain mix of fixed and variable debt; hedge via interest rate swaps, cross-currency interest rate swaps, and interest rate locks.
  - Accounting:
    - Fair value hedges: Changes in fair value of swaps and the hedged debt recognized in interest expense.
    - Non-designated swaps: Fair value changes recognized in other non-operating income (loss), net.
  - Volumes:
    - Receive-fixed/pay-variable interest rate swaps outstanding: $837.1 million at June 30, 2020 ($841.1 million at June 30, 2019).
    - Cross-currency interest rate swaps outstanding: $100 million (€89.0 million) at June 30, 2020; not designated, changes recognized in earnings.
  - Treasury locks:
    - Entered six Treasury lock agreements in Q3 FY2020 (notional $250.0 million) as cash flow hedges of anticipated long-term debt issuance; deemed highly effective.
    - Upon issuing unsecured senior notes on June 19, 2020, settled locks with $19.8 million cash payment; loss recorded in AOCI and amortized to interest expense over the 10-year note life.
- Foreign currency risk management:
  - Strategy: Hedge exchange rate volatility using forward contracts; manage net investment exposure primarily via borrowings in relevant currencies.
  - Accounting:
    - Cash flow hedges: Effective portion of forward contracts’ fair value changes to AOCI and reclassified to earnings when hedged transactions occur; ineffective portion to earnings in the same line item as the hedged item.
    - Non-designated forwards: Fair value changes recognized in the consolidated statement of income.
    - Net investment hedges: Effective remeasurement gains/losses on designated external borrowings to AOCI; ineffectiveness to other non-operating income (loss), net.
  - Volumes: Outstanding forward contract notional amounts of $1.6 billion at June 30, 2020 ($1.0 billion at June 30, 2019).

nodes.title: Foreign Currency Risk
nodes.heading: Foreign Currency Risk
nodes.start_phrase: The Company manufactures and sells its products and finances opera tions in a number of countries throughout the world and, as a result, is exp osed to movements in foreign currency exchange rates.
nodes.summary:
- Overview: Note describes the Company’s use of derivative and other financial instruments exclusively for hedging interest rate, foreign currency, and commodity risks. Hedges are formally designated as fair value or cash flow hedges when qualifying, with ongoing effectiveness assessments. Non‑hedge (non-designated) derivatives’ fair value changes are recognized in earnings.

- Interest rate risk:
  - Strategy: Maintain a mix of fixed- and variable-rate debt; use interest rate swaps, cross-currency interest rate swaps, and interest rate locks.
  - Accounting:
    - Fair value hedges: Changes in fair value of swaps and the hedged debt are recognized in interest expense.
    - Non-designated swaps: Fair value changes recognized in other non-operating income (loss), net.
  - Activity/positions:
    - Receive-fixed/pay-variable interest rate swaps notional: $837.1 million (June 30, 2020) vs. $841.1 million (2019).
    - Cross-currency interest rate swaps notional: $100 million (€89.0 million) outstanding at June 30, 2020; not designated, changes recognized in earnings.
    - Treasury locks: Six agreements totaling $250.0 million designated as cash flow hedges for anticipated long-term debt. Upon issuing 10-year unsecured senior notes on June 19, 2020, the locks were settled with a $19.8 million cash payment; loss recorded in AOCI and to be amortized to interest expense over the notes’ life.

- Foreign currency risk:
  - Strategy: Hedge exchange rate volatility arising from global manufacturing, sales, and financing via forward contracts.
  - Accounting:
    - Cash flow hedges: Effective portions to AOCI and reclassified to earnings when hedged transactions affect results; ineffective portions to earnings. Non-designated forwards’ fair value changes recognized in earnings.
  - Activity/positions:
    - Outstanding forward contract notional: $1.6 billion (June 30, 2020) vs. $1.0 billion (2019).
    - Net investment hedges: Use borrowings in local currencies; effective portions to AOCI, ineffective to other non-operating income (loss). Upon disposal of the hedged net investment, related AOCI amounts are reclassified to earnings.
    - Commercial paper: $67.0 million designated as a net investment hedge at the start of FY2020; settled during the quarter ended December 31, 2019. Related AOCI balances remain until sale or liquidation of the subsidiaries. No net investment hedges outstanding at June 30, 2020.

- Commodity risk:
  - Exposure: Raw materials subject to price volatility (e.g., weather, supply, political/economic factors).
  - Strategy: Minimize volatility by passing commodity price risk to customers, including use of fixed-price swaps purchased on customers’ behalf; centrally managed and cash-settled at maturity with costs/benefits passed through to customers.
  - Accounting: Changes in fair value of commodity hedges recognized in AOCI; cumulative hedge amounts recognized in earnings when the forecast transaction occurs.
  - Outstanding commodity contracts:
    - Aluminum: 44,944 tons (June 30, 2020) vs. 29,342 tons (2019).
    - PET resin: 26,006,000 lbs (June 30, 2020); not applicable in 2019.

nodes.title: Commodity Risk
nodes.heading: Commodity Risk
nodes.start_phrase: Certain raw materials used in the Company's production processes a re subject to price volatility caused by weather, supply conditions, political and economic variables and other unpredictable factors.
nodes.summary:

At the start of FY2020, $67.0 million of commercial paper was designated as a net investment hedge; it was settled in Q2 FY2020, with cumulative amounts remaining in AOCI until sale/liquidation of related subsidiaries. At June 30, 2020, forwards to buy 2.0m shares at an average $10.68 maturing June 2021 (prior year: 1.0m at $11.00 maturing June 2020). Classified as current liabilities; equity reduced at inception by share fair value; carrying value based on present value of settlement cost.

nodes.title: Income Taxes
nodes.heading: Note 16 - Income Taxes
nodes.start_phrase: Amcor plc is a tax resident of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland ("UK").
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Note 16 – Income Taxes for Amcor plc, a UK tax resident (prior to the Bemis acquisition, parent was Australian). Covers income before tax, tax expense, effective tax rates and reconciliations, deferred taxes, valuation allowances, carryforwards, indefinite reinvestment, uncertain tax positions, audit status, and Swiss Tax Reform impacts.
- Income before taxes: Split between domestic (UK) and foreign for fiscal years 2020, 2019, 2018; foreign operations generated the majority of pretax income.
- Income tax expense: Presented by current and deferred components, split domestic/foreign for 2020–2018.
- Tax rate reconciliation: Reconciles to statutory rates of 18.5% (UK, 2020), 19% (UK, 2019), and 30% (Australia, 2018). Key drivers include foreign tax rate differentials, non-deductible expenses, tax law changes, valuation allowance changes, and other items.
- Effective tax rates: 22.6% (2020), 28.4% (2019), 16.4% (2018). 2020 reflects a benefit from Swiss tax law changes largely offset by current-period true-ups; higher than UK statutory rate due to earnings in higher-tax jurisdictions outside the UK.
- Deferred taxes: Details of deferred tax assets (inventories, employee benefits, provisions, NOLs, credits, other accruals) and liabilities (PPE, intangible assets including Swiss reform impacts, receivables, derivatives, undistributed foreign earnings). Net deferred tax liability was $537.0m at June 30, 2020 (vs. $820.8m in 2019).
- Valuation allowance: Increased by $72.9m in 2020 (also increased in 2019 and 2018), primarily due to the deferred tax asset arising from Swiss Tax Reform; methodology nets the Swiss DTA against intangible-related DTL with a valuation allowance to amounts more-likely-than-not realizable.
- Undistributed earnings: Decrease in DTL for undistributed foreign earnings in 2020 includes $82.5m tax impact from the EC Remedy sale. About $968.2m of foreign subsidiary earnings are indefinitely reinvested; a cumulative DTL of $26.9m recorded for amounts no longer indefinitely reinvested; remaining undistributed earnings can be repatriated at no tax cost.
- Carryforwards: As of June 30, 2020, UK NOLs and credits (tax effected) of ~$2.9m with no expiry; non-UK NOLs and other attributes of ~$50.9m (majority no expiry), with valuation allowances recorded; utilization depends on future taxable income in relevant jurisdictions.
- Uncertain tax positions: Unrecognized tax benefits of $101.1m (2020) and $102.6m (2019), all of which would favorably impact the ETR if recognized. Interest and penalties accrued were $7.1m (2020), $13.8m (2019), $2.9m (2018). Rollforward provided (additions, reductions, settlements, acquisitions).
- Audits and exposure: Open tax years include US federal (2016–2019), HMRC (2019), and various US states and non-US jurisdictions (2011–2019). Reserves considered adequate, but outcomes could materially impact results or cash flows.
- Swiss Tax Reform: Swiss law changes in 2020 removed certain regimes and introduced new measures. In Q4 2020, Amcor recorded a net $21.7m benefit from an allowed step-up of intangible assets for tax purposes, recognized through reduced deferred tax expense and reflected within intangible-related deferred tax balances with an associated valuation allowance.

nodes.start_phrase: Share-based compensation expense of $34.0 million, $18.6 million an d $21.0 million was primarily recorded in general and administrative expe nses for fiscal years 2020, 2019 and 2018, respectively.
nodes.summary:
- Share rights program: Granted to directors, officers, and employees with vesting restrictions that prohibit disposal during the vesting period. Fair value measured at grant using the Company’s share closing price adjusted for dividend yield.
- Share rights activity (FY2020): Non-vested rights remained 1.5 million year over year; during the year 1.0 million were granted, 0.9 million exercised, and 0.1 million forfeited. Weighted-average grant-date fair value moved from $10.0 to $8.4. Grant-date fair values of awards granted were $8.8 (2020), $9.2 (2019), $11.0 (2018). Fair value of vested share rights: $10.7m (2020), $13.9m (2019), $12.9m (2018).
- Share-based compensation expense: Total of $34.0m (2020), $18.6m (2019), $21.0m (2018), primarily in G&A. By award type in 2020: share options $11.4m, restricted shares/units $2.6m, performance rights/shares $11.8m, share rights $8.2m; cash-settled awards were $0 in 2020 (vs. $2.7m in 2019 and $2.6m in 2018).
- Unrecognized compensation cost: $73.4m related to unvested awards as of June 30, 2020, expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 2.1 years.
- Earnings per share (Note 18): Company uses the two-class method; basic EPS excludes shares to be repurchased; diluted EPS includes dilutive equity awards.
- EPS results (in USD): 
  - Net income available to ordinary shareholders: $611.8m (2020), $429.4m (2019), $573.9m (2018); with continuing operations $619.5m, $428.7m, $573.9m; discontinued operations $(7.7)m, $0.7m, $—.
  - Weighted-average shares for basic EPS: 1,600.0m (2020), 1,180.3m (2019), 1,154.4m (2018); diluted: 1,601.6m, 1,183.8m, 1,161.7m.
  - Basic EPS: $0.382 (2020), $0.364 (2019), $0.497 (2018); Diluted EPS: $0.382 (2020), $0.363 (2019), $0.494 (2018). Continuing operations EPS presented separately; small loss from discontinued operations in 2020.
- Antidilutive awards excluded from diluted EPS: 36.9m (2020), 5.6m (2019), 10.3m (2018) shares.

nodes.title: Earnings Per Share Computations
nodes.heading: Note 18 - Earnings Per Share Computations
nodes.start_phrase: The Company applies the two-class method when computing its e arnings per share ("EPS"), which requires that net income per share for each c lass of share be calculated assuming all of the Company's net income is distributed as dividends to each class of share based on their contractual rights.
nodes.summary:
- Note 18 explains the Company’s earnings per share (EPS) methodology, using the two-class method that allocates net income to each class of shares based on contractual rights.
- Basic EPS excludes ordinary shares subject to forward repurchase and is calculated from net income available to ordinary shareholders divided by the weighted-average basic shares.
- Diluted EPS reflects potentially dilutive securities (share options, restricted shares, performance rights/shares, and share rights) when dilutive.
- Detailed EPS data are presented for fiscal years 2020, 2019, and 2018, including:
  - Numerators: net income attributable to Amcor plc, adjustments for earnings attributable to shares to be repurchased, and splits between continuing and discontinued operations.
  - Denominators: weighted-average shares outstanding, reductions for shares to be repurchased, and the effect of dilutive shares.
  - Per-share results for basic and diluted EPS, showing modest dilution and small losses from discontinued operations in 2020.
- Certain stock awards were anti-dilutive and excluded from diluted EPS: 36.9 million (2020), 5.6 million (2019), and 10.3 million (2018).

- Note 19 addresses contingencies and legal proceedings.
- Brazil tax contingencies: Ongoing governmental assessments and litigation mainly related to excise and income taxes; the Company intends to defend vigorously and does not expect a material impact. Accruals recorded were $11.9 million (2020) and $16.4 million (2019), with reasonably possible losses in excess of accruals of $18.4 million (2020) and $23.7 million (2019). Collateral posted as of June 30, 2020 included $34.0 million in letters of credit, $0.9 million in judicial insurance, and $10.1 million in cash deposits.
- Environmental contingencies: The Company is a potentially responsible party at several U.S. waste sites and has recorded $17.1 million for estimated remediation at these sites, plus $46.6 million for other global remediation obligations. Insurance may not fully cover exposures; however, management does not expect a material adverse effect on liquidity, results, or financial condition.
- Legal proceedings related to the Amcor–Bemis transaction:
  - An appraisal action funded by Burford Capital on behalf of two funds contesting the merger exchange ratio was filed in Missouri; it was settled via a Confidential Settlement Agreement on June 24, 2020 and dismissed with prejudice two days later.
  - Two federal securities lawsuits (Dixon and Stein) alleging inadequate proxy disclosures were filed in the Southern District of New York; they were consolidated into a single class action on March 10, 2020.

nodes.title: Contingencies and Legal Proceedings
nodes.heading: Note 19 - Contingencies and Legal Proceedings
nodes.start_phrase: The Company's operations in Brazil are involved in various go vernmental assessments and litigation, principally related to cl aims for excise and income taxes.
nodes.summary:
- Overview: Note 19 outlines the company’s contingencies and legal proceedings, focusing on Brazil tax matters, environmental obligations, and litigation related to the Amcor–Bemis merger.

- Brazil contingencies:
  - Involvement in governmental assessments and litigation primarily for excise and income taxes; company will vigorously defend and does not expect material impact on results, financial position, or cash flows.
  - Accruals: $11.9 million at June 30, 2020 ($16.4 million at June 30, 2019) recorded in other non-current liabilities.
  - Reasonably possible loss in excess of accruals: $18.4 million at June 30, 2020 ($23.7 million at June 30, 2019).
  - Potential need to post collateral in Brazil; amounts pledged/required not expected to significantly impact liquidity.
  - Collateral provided as of June 30, 2020: letters of credit $34.0 million, judicial insurance $0.9 million, cash deposits with courts $10.1 million.
  - Acknowledges litigation uncertainties; accruals reflect best estimates where loss is probable.

- Environmental matters:
  - Identified as a potentially responsible party at several U.S. waste sites; may have material remediation obligations, with insurance potentially only partial.
  - Accrued $17.1 million for estimated future remediation at PRP sites.
  - Additional $46.6 million accrued for remediation at various owned, operated, or formerly owned/operated worldwide locations.
  - Belief that accruals are adequate, though ultimate payments could exceed amounts; does not expect a material adverse effect on liquidity, results, or financial condition.

- Legal proceedings:
  - Burford Capital–funded appraisal action by two Bemis shareholders disputing the Amcor share exchange ratio: formal demand (June 24, 2019), petition filed (Sept. 6, 2019), Bemis answer (Nov. 4, 2019); settled via Confidential Settlement Agreement on June 24, 2020; case dismissed with prejudice two days later.
  - Two federal lawsuits (Dixon and Stein) by purported Bemis shareholders in SDNY alleging proxy disclosure violations under the Securities Exchange Act and SEC rules; filed April 2019 and consolidated into a single class action on March 10, 2020.

nodes.title: Segments
nodes.heading: Note 20 - Segments
nodes.start_phrase: The Company's business is organized and presented in the t wo reportable segments outlined below:
nodes.summary:
- Segment overview: The company reports two primary segments—Flexibles and Rigid Packaging—with “Other” capturing equity-method investments (including AMVIG), undistributed corporate costs, eliminations, and ancillary activities.
- Segment composition:
  - Flexibles: Flexible and film packaging for food & beverage, medical/pharma, fresh produce, snacks, personal care, and other industries.
  - Rigid Packaging: Rigid plastic containers and plastic caps serving beverages (CSDs, water, juices, sports drinks, dairy, spirits, beer) and food/personal care.
- Segment structure changes post-Bemis acquisition: In FY20, Flexibles Americas was split into Flexibles North America and Flexibles Latin America; five Flexibles operating segments were aggregated into one reporting segment based on similarity of economics, products, technologies, customers, delivery models, and regulation.
- Performance measure change: Beginning Q4 FY19 (in connection with the Bemis acquisition), management shifted segment performance metric to Adjusted EBIT from continuing operations. Adjusted EBIT is operating income adjusted for specified non-core items and includes equity in income (loss) of affiliates.
- Governance: The Global Management Team (GMT)—the CEO and direct reports—allocates resources and evaluates performance using Adjusted EBIT; segment accounting policies align with Note 2.
- AMVIG treatment: Accounted for under the equity method; its results are excluded from segment net sales.
- FY20–FY18 summary financials by segment:
  - Net sales grew to $12.5B in FY20 (from $9.5B in FY19), with Flexibles as the primary contributor; intersegment sales were minimal.
  - Adjusted EBIT in FY20: $1,497.1M (Flexibles $1,335.1M; Rigid Packaging $290.1M; Other $(128.1)M).
- Reconciliation items from Adjusted EBIT to EBIT include: restructuring programs, impairments in equity-method investments (AMVIG), material acquisition and integration costs (notably Bemis), amortization of acquired intangibles (including sales backlog), economic net investment hedging impacts, hyperinflation effects (Argentina), net legal settlements, and pension settlements.
- FY20 EBIT from continuing operations: $995.9M; interest income/expense and equity in income (loss) of affiliates disclosed; pre-tax income provided.
- Capital expenditures and D&A: FY20 capex $399.5M; depreciation and amortization $607.2M, both detailed by segment.
- Assets: Total assets by segment are not disclosed as GMT does not use them for performance/resource allocation.
- Customer concentration: No single customer >10% of sales in FY20; PepsiCo accounted for ~11% in FY19 and FY18 across both segments; no other customer exceeded 10% in those years.
- Product sales mix: FY20 comprised Films and other flexible products ($8.64B), Specialty flexible folding cartons ($1.11B), and Containers, preforms and closures ($2.72B).
- Geographic details:
  - Net sales disaggregated by region (North America, Latin America, Europe, Asia Pacific) for FY18–FY20, by segment; Jersey (domicile) had no sales.
  - Long-lived assets totaled $3.61B at June 30, 2020, with $1.56B in the U.S. and the remainder in other countries; none in Jersey and no single other country >10%.
- Note 21 – Deed of Cross Guarantee: Amcor plc and specified wholly owned Australian subsidiaries entered a Deed of Cross Guarantee (June 24, 2019), with ARP North America Holdco Ltd and ARP LATAM Holdco Ltd added on Sept. 25, 2019; subsidiaries are relieved from preparing separate financial and directors’ reports under ASIC Instrument 2016/785; ASIC-required consolidated financial statements for the deed group will be presented.

The closed (and extended closed) group as of June 30, 2020 includes multiple Australian entities plus ARP North America Holdco Ltd and ARP LATAM Holdco Ltd (both added September 25, 2019). - By joining the Deed, these subsidiaries are relieved from preparing separate financial and directors’ reports under ASIC Corporations (Wholly‑owned Companies) Instrument 2016/785. ASIC‑specific consolidated financial disclosures for the deed group are provided.
- Statement of Income (in millions): FY2020 vs FY2019 shows net sales 323.6 vs 352.8; significant other income driving operating income 4,192.0 vs 1,025.7; net income 4,163.8 vs 995.3; 2020 includes an income tax credit.
- Summarized Statement of Comprehensive Income: OCI of 32.2 in 2020 vs 65.4 in 2019 (cash flow hedges, FX translation, net investment hedges); total comprehensive income 4,196.0 vs 1,060.7.
- Summarized Statement of Income and Accumulated Losses: retained earnings rose from 2,519.0 to 5,935.2 in 2020 after net income and dividends; dividends recognized 747.6 (2020) and 665.9 (2019).
- Balance Sheet (in millions): total assets 13,551.9 (2020) vs 11,589.0 (2019), driven by other non‑current assets; liabilities decreased to 1,067.8 from 2,022.8 with lower long‑term debt (355.8 vs 1,587.7) but higher short‑term debt (507.3 vs 155.3); shareholders’ equity increased to 12,484.1 from 9,566.2.
- Note 22 provides supplemental cash flow details: interest paid (net) 212.3 (2020), 219.8 (2019), 209.4 (2018); income taxes paid 304.4 (2020), 147.7 (2019), 149.7 (2018); non‑cash investing includes accrued but unpaid PP&E purchases of 78.0, 75.0, and 68.4; non‑cash financing includes 2019 equity issuance of 5,229.6 for the Bemis acquisition.

nodes.title: Supplemental Cash Flow Information
nodes.heading: Note 22 - Supplemental Cash Flow Information

nodes.summary:
- Document section: Deed of Cross Guarantee including a consolidated Balance Sheet (in millions) as of June 30, 2020 and 2019, and Note 22 – Supplemental Cash Flow Information.
- Assets:
  - Total assets increased to $13,551.9 from $11,589.0.
  - Current assets decreased to $895.6 from $933.6 (lower trade receivables and inventories; cash down).
  - Non-current assets rose to $12,656.3 from $10,655.4, driven largely by a jump in other non-current assets ($12,454.6 vs. $10,417.7); goodwill and intangibles relatively stable; PP&E slightly lower; deferred tax assets declined.
- Liabilities:

  - Current liabilities increased to $709.1 from $431.8, largely due to higher short-term debt ($507.3 vs. $155.3); trade payables fell.
  - Non-current liabilities decreased significantly, mainly from a reduction in long-term debt ($355.8 vs. $1,587.7).
- Shareholders’ equity:
  - Total equity increased to $12,484.1 from $9,566.2.
  - Growth primarily from higher retained earnings ($5,935.2 vs. $2,519.0); additional paid-in capital decreased; accumulated other comprehensive income rose modestly.
- Note 22 – Supplemental Cash Flow Information:
  - Interest paid (net): $212.3 (2020), $219.8 (2019), $209.4 (2018).
  - Income taxes paid: $304.4 (2020), $147.7 (2019), $149.7 (2018).
  - Non-cash investing: PP&E purchases accrued but unpaid of $78.0 (2020), $75.0 (2019), $68.4 (2018).
  - Non-cash financing: In 2019, $5,229.6 of ordinary shares issued as total equity consideration for the Bemis acquisition.

structure.title: Changes In and Disagreements With Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure
structure.heading: Item 9. Changes In and Disagreements With Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure
structure.start_phrase: null.
structure.summary:
- Item 9: No changes in or disagreements with accountants on accounting or financial disclosure.
- Item 9A: Management (CEO and CFO) evaluated disclosure controls and procedures as of June 30, 2020; while designed to ensure timely, accurate SEC reporting, such controls provide only reasonable assurance. They concluded the disclosure controls were not effective due to an ongoing material weakness in internal control over financial reporting first disclosed in March 2019.
- Management’s report on internal control over financial reporting: Management is responsible for ICFR, aimed at reliable GAAP financial reporting; evaluation performed using the COSO 2013 framework.
- Key ICFR elements highlighted: accurate recordkeeping, authorization of transactions, and prevention/detection of unauthorized asset use.
- Material weakness definition and acknowledgment of inherent control limitations.
- Specific material weakness: deficiencies in the design and operating effectiveness of period-end reporting controls, notably inadequate segregation of conflicting duties within key IT systems. This did not cause a misstatement but could have led to one not being prevented or detected timely.

structure.title: Controls and Procedures
structure.heading: Item 9A. Controls and Procedures
structure.start_phrase: Our management, with the participation of our Chief Executive Of ficer and Chief Financial Officer, has evaluated the effectiveness of o ur disclosure controls and procedures as of June 30, 2020.
structure.summary:
- Item 9: Reports no changes in, or disagreements with, accountants on accounting or financial disclosure.
- Item 9A: Management evaluated disclosure controls as of June 30, 2020 and concluded they were not effective due to a continuing material weakness in internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) related to segregation of duties within key IT systems used for period-end reporting. No misstatements occurred, but the deficiency could have led to them. ICFR is assessed under the COSO 2013 framework and was audited by PricewaterhouseCoopers AG.
- Remediation plan: Implement new security roles, automate segregation-of-duties monitoring, add compensating controls, and provide training; rollout focused on largest standardized ERP locations in FY2020 with expansion in FY2021. Remediation expected by end of FY2021, though COVID-19 may delay timing.
- Completed remediation: A separate material weakness related to U.S. GAAP technical accounting and U.S. registrant filing experience has been remediated through added staffing, policy alignment, enhanced close reviews, and training; tested and deemed effective by Q4 FY2020.
- Changes in ICFR: Aside from the actions described, no changes in Q4 FY2020 that materially affected or are likely to materially affect ICFR.
- Item 9B: No other information.
- Item 10: Director/executive officer and governance information to be provided in a forthcoming proxy statement (incorporated by reference); governance documents (committee charters, guidelines, code of conduct) are available on the company’s website.

structure.title: Other Information
structure.heading: Item 9B. Other Information
structure.start_phrase: null.
structure.summary:
- Management, including the CEO and CFO, evaluated internal control over financial reporting (ICFR) as of June 30, 2020, and concluded ICFR was not effective due to an unresolved previously identified material weakness.
- PricewaterhouseCoopers AG audited the effectiveness of ICFR as of June 30, 2020; their report is included in Item 8 of the Form 10-K.
- Remediation plan for the material weakness focuses on period-end reporting controls: reducing segregation-of-duties conflicts in key IT systems (new security roles, automated monitoring), adding compensating controls, and providing training. Rollout began in major standardized ERP locations in fiscal 2020, expanding in fiscal 2021. Remediation is expected by end of fiscal 2021, but timing may be impacted by COVID-19 restrictions; effectiveness will be confirmed after sustained operation and testing.
- A separate, previously reported material weakness related to limited U.S. GAAP and SEC reporting expertise has been remediated as of June 30, 2020, following hiring experienced personnel, aligning policies with U.S. GAAP, enhancing close reviews, and conducting technical training; operating effectiveness testing in Q4 2020 was successful.
- Aside from the described actions, there were no changes in ICFR during the fourth fiscal quarter of 2020 that materially affected or are likely to materially affect ICFR.
- Item 9B (Other Information): None.
- Part III, Item 10: Director, executive officer, and corporate governance information will be provided in a definitive proxy statement within 120 days of June 30, 2020 and incorporated by reference; executive officer information appears in Part I; governance documents are available on the company’s website.

Initial efforts targeted major standardized ERP locations in fiscal 2020, expanding in fiscal 2021. Remediation is expected by end of fiscal 2021 but may be delayed due to COVID-19 constraints; effectiveness will be confirmed after sufficient operation and testing.

nodes.summary:
- Registrant: Amcor plc. As of June 30, 2020, two classes registered under Exchange Act Section 12: (i) Ordinary Shares, $0.01 par; (ii) 1.125% Guaranteed Senior Notes due 2027. Both listed on NYSE; CHESS Depositary Interests (CDIs) representing ordinary shares trade on ASX.

- Share capital: Authorized $100,000,000 comprising 9,000,000,000 ordinary shares ($0.01 par) and 1,000,000,000 preferred shares ($0.01 par). 1,568,481,519 ordinary shares issued and outstanding as of August 25, 2020. No preferred shares outstanding.
- Ordinary share rights: Equal voting rights (one vote per share), no fixed income, right to declared dividends, and right to notice/attendance/vote at general meetings. CDIs represent beneficial ownership of shares; references to “shares” include CDIs where context permits.
- Preferred shares: Board may create classes/series with rights set in a statement of rights; may have priority over ordinary shares for dividends and/or liquidation.
- Board authority to issue shares: Board may issue ordinary or preferred shares without further shareholder action unless required by law or stock exchange rules.
- Winding up: After paying debts and expenses, any surplus distributed to shareholders pro rata by number of shares. With a special resolution, assets may be divided in specie among shareholders/classes.
- Voting mechanics: Ordinary resolutions pass by a majority of voting rights represented and voting; special resolutions require two-thirds (or higher if Articles prescribe). Preferred share voting (if any) set in their rights. No restrictions on non-residents exercising voting rights. No cumulative voting under Jersey law.
- No preemptive rights for shareholders to acquire newly issued ordinary shares.
- Variation of class rights: May be varied by special resolution at a separate class meeting, unless terms of issue provide otherwise.
- Share form and transfer: Shares may be certificated or uncertificated; certificated holders entitled to free share certificates. Fully paid registered shares generally freely transferable unless restricted by law or other instrument.
- Dividends: 
  - Declared and paid at the board’s discretion; board may rescind before payment if financial position no longer justifies payment; no shareholder approval required.
  - Paid equally per ordinary share; may be satisfied from any source permitted by law (excluding nominal capital account and capital redemption reserve), including in-kind distributions or securities of another company.
  - Cash dividends declared in U.S. dollars.
  - Directors authorizing dividends must make a statutory solvency statement under Jersey law.
  - Board may require payments by electronic transfer to a shareholder-designated account.
  - No interest accrues on unpaid dividends unless share terms specify otherwise.
  - Unclaimed dividends after 11 months may have payment stopped and amounts used for Amcor’s benefit until claimed or disposed of per unclaimed monies laws.

nodes.title: Alteration of Share Capital
nodes.heading: Alteration of Share Capital
nodes.start_phrase: Under the Jersey Companies Law, Amcor may, by special resolution of i ts shareholders: increase its share capital; consolidate and sub-divid e; convert shares into or from stock; re-denominate any of its shares into another currency or reduce its share capital, capital red emption reserve or share premium account in any way.
nodes.summary:
- Alteration of share capital: By special shareholder resolution under Jersey Companies Law, Amcor can increase capital; consolidate or subdivide shares; convert shares into/from stock; re-denominate shares into another currency; and reduce share capital, capital redemption reserve, or share premium account.
- Redeemable shares: Ordinary shares are initially non-redeemable. The board may issue redeemable shares or convert non-redeemable shares into redeemable shares, with redemption per their terms and at Amcor’s and/or the holder’s option. Conversion of issued non-redeemable shares requires holder consent or a special resolution.
- Purchase of own shares: Amcor may buy back its own shares or CDIs and either cancel them or hold them as treasury shares, subject to Jersey law and its Articles. A special shareholder resolution is required. For on-market purchases, the resolution must set the maximum number of shares/CDIs, the price range (min/max), and an expiry date not more than five years from the resolution. Off-market purchases require a written contract approved in advance by shareholders, excluding the selling shareholder.
- Shareholder meetings:
  - Annual general meetings: Must be held once every calendar year, with no more than 18 months between meetings; timing and place set by the Board. General meetings may be called by Board resolution or as otherwise provided by Jersey law.
  - Extraordinary/special meetings: The Board may call and, upon request, must convene an extraordinary general meeting. Shareholders with at least 10% of voting rights can require the directors to call a meeting. The Board must call the meeting as soon as practicable and no later than two months after the requisition. If the Board does not proceed within 21 days to call a meeting to be held within two months, the requisitionists (holding more than half of their total voting rights) may call it, provided it is not held after three months from the requisition date.
- Notice of meetings: Notices must be sent to all shareholders per the Articles and applicable stock exchange listing rules. The Board determines content, but notices must specify whether the meeting is annual or extraordinary and state the general nature of the business and any other matters required by Jersey Companies Law.

- Voting for directors: If nominees exceed available seats, those with the highest votes up to the number of seats are elected; an absolute majority is not required.
- Removal of directors: A director may be removed only by ordinary resolution of shareholders.

nodes.title: Election of Directors
nodes.heading: Election of Directors
nodes.start_phrase: Amcor directors are appointed by Amcor's board of directors and shall hold offic e until the next annual general meeting following such appointment.
nodes.summary:
- Record date for voting and attendance: Amcor may set a shareholder record date 10–60 days before a meeting and may set a separate cutoff time for CDI holders to be on the CDI register to direct the Depositary Nominee or appoint a proxy.
- Quorum: No business may be conducted unless holders representing at least a majority of the total voting rights entitled to vote are present in person or by proxy.
- No action by written consent: Shareholder actions must occur at a duly called general meeting; unanimous written consents are prohibited.
- Shareholder proposals: Shareholders of record eligible to vote may require inclusion of business at the annual meeting by giving notice 90–120 days before the anniversary of the prior annual meeting; proposed business must be proper for shareholder action.
- Director nominations by shareholders: Permitted subject to informational and procedural requirements in the Articles; timing—90–120 days before the anniversary for annual meetings, and no later than the 10th day after notice is mailed for extraordinary meetings called to elect directors.
- Meeting admission conditions: The board or meeting chair may impose safety and conduct measures (e.g., ID checks, searches, restricted items) and may refuse entry for noncompliance.
- Board of Directors—election and tenure: Directors are appointed by the board until the next annual general meeting and are subject to annual re-election by shareholders; if nominees exceed available seats, directors are elected by plurality (no absolute majority required).
- Removal of directors: Directors may be removed only by ordinary resolution of shareholders (specific grounds not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Removal of Directors
nodes.heading: Removal of Directors
nodes.start_phrase: Under the Articles of Association, a director may only be removed from offi ce by ordinary resolution of Amcor shareholders as a result of:
nodes.summary:
- Meeting record date: Amcor may set a shareholder/voting/proxy record date 60–10 days before the meeting; a separate cutoff may be set for CDI holders to be on the CDI register to direct the Depositary Nominee.
- Quorum: Business at a general meeting requires a quorum representing at least a majority of total voting rights present in person or by proxy.
- No written consents: Shareholder actions must occur at duly called general or class meetings; unanimous written consent is prohibited.
- Shareholder proposals: Eligible shareholders may require inclusion of resolutions for the annual general meeting by giving notice 120–90 days before the anniversary of the prior AGM; business must be a proper matter for shareholder action.
- Director nominations: Shareholders may nominate directors subject to information and timing requirements—annual meetings: notice 120–90 days before the prior AGM anniversary; extraordinary meetings to elect directors: within 10 days after notice of the meeting is mailed.
- Admission/security at meetings: The board or meeting chair may impose identification, searches, item restrictions, and other measures for safety/order, and may refuse entry for non-compliance.
- Board elections: Directors are appointed by the board and serve until the next AGM; all directors stand for annual re-election. If nominees exceed seats, directors are elected by plurality (no absolute majority needed).
- Director removal: Removal only by ordinary resolution and only for specified misconduct: conviction (including nolo contendere) of a serious felony involving moral turpitude or U.S. securities law violation (excluding purely vicarious liability), or material dishonest acts (e.g., embezzlement) for personal gain likely chargeable as a felony; terms follow U.S. law (and equivalents elsewhere).
- Board vacancies: Only the board (by majority of sitting directors, even if less than a quorum) may fill vacancies; appointees serve until the next AGM.
- Business combinations: A three-year prohibition on business combinations with “interested shareholders” unless the board approved the combination or the acquisition of the stake before it occurred (subject to specified exceptions). An interested shareholder generally is one owning more than 15% of voting stock, or an affiliate/associate that owned more than 15% within the prior three years.
- Ownership disclosure: Holders must comply with U.S. Exchange Act Section 13(d). Amcor may require persons it believes hold (or held within three years) interests in shares to confirm and provide details.
- Sanctions for non-disclosure: If a person fails to respond adequately, the relevant shares (and any issued in right of them) may have voting rights suspended, dividends/distributions withheld (without interest), and transfers not registered except for “excepted transfers,” including acceptance of a takeover offer under Jersey Companies Law and on-market transfers via the NYSE, ASX, or another exchange where Amcor shares are normally traded.

nodes.title: Vacancies
nodes.heading: Vacancies
nodes.start_phrase: The Articles of Association provide that any vacancy occurring on the Amcor board (whether caused by increase in size of the Amcor board, or by death, disabi lity, resignation, removal or otherwise) shall only be filled by a majority of the Amcor board then in office, even though fewer than a quorum.
nodes.summary:
- Director misconduct standards: A director can be disqualified for a conviction (including nolo contendere) of a serious felony involving moral turpitude or U.S. securities law violations (excluding purely vicarious liability), or for materially dishonest acts (e.g., embezzlement) intended to personally enrich the director at the Company’s expense and likely chargeable as a felony. Terms are defined by U.S. law or equivalent in other jurisdictions.
- Board vacancies: Any vacancy (including from board size changes or director departure) may be filled only by a majority of the remaining directors, even if below quorum; appointees serve until the next annual general meeting.
- Business combinations with interested shareholders: A three-year prohibition on combinations with an “interested shareholder” unless the board approved the combination or the transaction creating that status (with certain other exceptions). An interested shareholder generally includes anyone (with affiliates/associates) owning more than 15% of voting stock, or affiliates/associates that held more than 15% within the prior three years.
- Shareholding disclosure: Holders must comply with Exchange Act Section 13(d). The Company may demand confirmation and details of current or past (last three years) interests. Non-compliance or false/inadequate responses trigger sanctions on the relevant shares: suspension of voting rights, withholding of dividends/distributions (without interest), and restrictions on transfers, except for “excepted transfers” such as transfers via NYSE/ASX/other listed exchanges or pursuant to a takeover under Jersey Companies Law.

nodes.title: Business Combinations with Interested Shareholders
nodes.heading: Business Combinations with Interested Shareholders
nodes.start_phrase: Under the Articles of Association, Amcor is prohibited from engaging in an y business combination with any "interested shareholder" for a period of thre e years following the time that such shareholder became an interested shareholder (subject to certain s pecified exceptions), unless (in addition to other exceptions) prior to su ch business combination the board approved either the business combination or the transaction which resulted in the shareholde r becoming an "interested shareholder."
nodes.summary:
- Defines misconduct triggering director removal for cause: conviction (including nolo contendere) of a serious felony involving moral turpitude or U.S. federal/state securities law violations (excluding purely vicarious liability), and material acts of dishonesty (e.g., embezzlement) for personal gain that would likely constitute a felony; terms defined by U.S. law with equivalents in other jurisdictions.
- Board vacancy rules: any vacancy (including from board size increases) may be filled only by a majority of the sitting directors, even if fewer than a quorum; appointees serve until the next annual general meeting.
- Business combinations restrictions: three-year prohibition on combinations with an “interested shareholder” unless the board approved the combination or the transaction creating interested shareholder status beforehand, subject to other specified exceptions; “interested shareholder” generally means a holder (with affiliates/associates) of more than 15% of voting stock, or one who held more than 15% within the prior three years.
- Shareholding disclosure and enforcement: beneficial owners must comply with Exchange Act Section 13(d); the company can require confirmation and details of current or past (within three years) holdings; non-compliance triggers sanctions on the relevant shares—loss of voting rights, withholding of dividends/distributions without interest, and transfer registration blocks—subject to “excepted transfers” such as transfers via a takeover under Jersey Companies Law or through NYSE/ASX/other usual trading venues.

nodes.title: Disclosure of Shareholding Ownership
nodes.heading: Disclosure of Shareholding Ownership
nodes.start_phrase: Holders of beneficial interests in Amcor ordinary shares must comply with th e beneficial ownership disclosure obligations contained in sectio n 13(d) of the Exchange Act and the rules promulgated thereunder.
nodes.summary:
- Director misconduct triggering consequences: conviction (including nolo contendere) of a serious felony involving moral turpitude or U.S. securities law violations (excluding convictions based solely on vicarious liability); or material dishonesty for personal gain (e.g., embezzlement) likely chargeable as a felony. Terms follow U.S. law (with equivalents in other jurisdictions).

- Board vacancies: filled only by a majority of the remaining board, even if below quorum; appointees serve until the next annual general meeting.

- Business combinations with interested shareholders: three-year prohibition on combinations with an “interested shareholder” unless the board approved the combination or the transaction creating interested status beforehand (with certain other exceptions). “Interested shareholder” generally includes anyone (with affiliates/associates) owning more than 15% of voting stock now or within the prior three years.

- Shareholding disclosure: holders must comply with Exchange Act Section 13(d). Amcor may require confirmation and details of current or prior (within three years) interests. Noncompliance results in loss of voting rights, withholding of dividends without interest, and transfer restrictions, except for “excepted transfers” (takeover acceptances under Jersey law; trades on NYSE/ASX/other listed exchanges; transfers of entire beneficial interest to an unaffiliated third party).

- CHESS Depositary Interests (CDIs): facilitate ASX trading/settlement for Amcor shares; legal title held by Cede & Co., with beneficial title held by CHESS Depositary Nominees for CDI holders; 1 CDI = 1 ordinary share. Key differences from ordinary shares include lack of legal title, indirect voting via instructions/proxy to the Depositary Nominee, and no direct access to certain Jersey shareholder remedies; CDIs can be converted to ordinary shares to vote directly.

- Standard Table under the Jersey Companies Law does not apply.

- Notes overview: 1.125% Senior Notes due 2027 issued by Amcor UK Finance plc, guaranteed by Amcor, AFUI, Amcor Pty Ltd, and Bemis, under an indenture dated June 23, 2020 with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas as trustee and subject to the Trust Indenture Act. Issued as global notes in €100,000 denominations (plus €1,000 increments), held via a common depositary for Euroclear and Clearstream; no U.K. security register.

nodes.title: CHESS Depositary Interests
nodes.heading: CHESS Depositary Interests
nodes.start_phrase: CDIs are quoted and traded on the financial market operated by ASX.
nodes.summary:
- The document explains why Amcor’s ordinary shares are not traded directly on ASX: the CHESS settlement system cannot record or transfer legal title for companies incorporated in jurisdictions (like Jersey) that do not recognize CHESS. To facilitate trading in Australia, CHESS Depositary Interests (CDIs) are used.
- CDIs are depositary receipts that give holders a beneficial interest in Amcor’s underlying ordinary shares. Legal title is held by Cede & Co., and beneficial title is held by CHESS Depositary Nominees Pty Ltd on behalf of CDI holders. Each CDI represents one ordinary share and is traded and settled electronically on ASX via CHESS.
- Key differences between holding CDIs and ordinary shares include:
  - CDI holders do not have legal title to the underlying shares.
  - CDI holders cannot vote directly at shareholder meetings; they must provide voting instructions to the Depositary Nominee or request appointment of themselves or a third party as proxy. Alternatively, they may convert CDIs into ordinary shares in time to vote personally.
  - CDI holders lack certain direct statutory rights of ordinary shareholders under Jersey law, such as applying to a Jersey court for unfair prejudice relief or requesting a regulator-appointed investigation.
- A brief reference is made to transfer of a person’s entire beneficial interest in shares to an unaffiliated third party (context suggests transferability provisions).
- The “standard table” under the Jersey Companies Law does not apply to Amcor.
- The document also summarizes the 1.125% Senior Notes due 2027 issued by Amcor UK Finance plc:
  - Issued under an indenture dated June 23, 2020 among the issuer, Amcor and certain affiliates as guarantors (AFUI, Amcor Pty Ltd, and Bemis), with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas as trustee, and subject to the Trust Indenture Act of 1939.
  - The indenture is filed as an exhibit to Amcor’s Form 10-K (Exhibit 4.26).
  - Notes are in fully registered form, denominations of €100,000 and integral multiples of €1,000 thereafter, issued as global notes without coupons, deposited with a common depositary and registered in the name of its nominee for Euroclear and Clearstream.
  - There is no security register for the Notes in the United Kingdom.

Each CDI represents one ordinary share and is transferable/settled through CHESS.

nodes.title: DESCRIPTION OF THE NOTES
nodes.heading: DESCRIPTION OF THE NOTES
nodes.start_phrase: The following description of the 1.125% Senior Notes due 2027 (the “Notes ”) issued by Amcor UK Finance plc, a subsidiary of Amcor (the “Issuer”) summarizes certain material terms of the Notes.
nodes.summary:
- Overview of CHESS Depositary Interests (CDIs) for Amcor on ASX, created because CHESS cannot directly register or transfer securities of non-Australian issuers like Amcor.
- Structure of ownership: each CDI represents a beneficial interest in one Amcor ordinary share; legal title held by Cede & Co.; beneficial title held by CHESS Depositary Nominees Pty Ltd on behalf of CDI holders.
- CDIs can be held, transferred, and settled electronically through CHESS; ordinary shares themselves are not traded on ASX.
- Key differences from ordinary shares:
  - CDI holders lack legal title to the underlying ordinary shares.
  - Voting is via voting instruction to the Depositary Nominee, or by appointing the CDI holder/nominee as proxy; direct shareholder voting requires prior conversion of CDIs into ordinary shares.
  - CDI holders are not directly entitled to certain Jersey law shareholder rights (e.g., unfair prejudice claims in Jersey court, applications to the Jersey Financial Services Commission for an inspector).
- Note that a fragment references transfer of a person’s whole beneficial interest in shares to an unaffiliated third party.
- Statement that the “standard table” provisions under Jersey Companies Law do not apply.
- Description of Amcor UK Finance plc’s 1.125% Senior Notes due 2027:
  - Issued under an indenture dated June 23, 2020 among the Issuer, Amcor and certain guarantors (AFUI, Amcor Pty Ltd, Bemis), with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas as Trustee; terms incorporate the Trust Indenture Act of 1939.
  - Aggregate principal amount €500,000,000; fully registered form in €100,000 denominations with €1,000 multiples; issued as global notes via a common depositary for Euroclear and Clearstream.
  - No security register in the UK or Australia; the Trustee acts as paying agent, transfer agent, and registrar; agents may be changed.
  - Maturity: June 23, 2027, at 100% of principal; no sinking fund; defeasance and covenant defeasance available.
  - Business day conventions: payments move to next Business Day without additional interest if a due date is not a Business Day.
  - Interest: 1.125% per annum, paid annually on June 23, starting June 23, 2021; Record Date is the clearing system business day immediately preceding payment for global notes, and 15 calendar days prior for others; day count Actual/Actual (ICMA); standard Business Day adjustment for interest and maturity dates.
  - Currency: all payments in euro; if euro becomes unavailable or is no longer used by EMU members/international settlements, payments switch to U.S. dollars using Federal Reserve mandated rate or, failing that, the Wall Street Journal or Issuer-determined market rate; such currency substitution is not an Event of Default; Trustee/paying agent not responsible for conversion calculations.
  - Example reference rate as of August 14, 2020: €1 = US$1.1833.

nodes.title: General
nodes.heading: General
nodes.start_phrase: Unless earlier redeemed in the circumstances set out below, the Not es will mature on June 23, 2027 at a price equal to 100% of their principa l amount.
nodes.summary:
- Roles and agents: The Trustee serves as paying agent, transfer agent, and registrar. Notes may be transferred or exchanged at the registrar’s offices. The issuer may change these agents without notice to holders (paying agent change upon notice to the Trustee).
- Maturity and size: Notes mature on June 23, 2027 at 100% of principal; total offering size €500,000,000. No sinking fund. Notes are subject to defeasance and covenant defeasance.
- Business Day convention: If a payment or redemption date is not a Business Day, payment is made on the next Business Day with no additional interest accrual for the delay.
- Interest terms: Interest accrues from issuance and is payable annually on June 23, starting June 23, 2021.
  - Record dates: For global notes, the clearing system business day immediately before the payment date; for others, 15 calendar days prior (whether or not a Business Day).
  - Day count: Actual/Actual (ICMA), from the last interest payment date (or June 23, 2020 if none) to but excluding the next scheduled payment date.
  - If an interest payment date is not a Business Day, it moves to the next Business Day without additional interest; same for maturity payments.
- Currency and payments: All payments (interest, principal, redemption/repurchase) are in euro.
  - Fallback to USD if the euro becomes unavailable or ceases to be used for relevant settlements; conversion based on:
    - The Federal Reserve Board’s mandated rate as of close of business two Business Days before payment; if unavailable, the most recent USD/EUR rate in The Wall Street Journal by that time; if still unavailable, the issuer determines the rate at its discretion from the most recent market rate.
  - USD payments under these circumstances do not constitute an Event of Default. The Trustee and paying agent are not responsible for conversion calculations.
- Reference exchange rate: As of August 14, 2020, €1 = $1.1833.

nodes.title: Interest
nodes.heading: Interest
nodes.start_phrase: The Notes bear interest from the date of issuance, payable annually on June 23 of each year, beginning June 23, 2021, to the persons in whose na mes such Notes are registered at the close of business on the date that is (i) in the case of Notes represented by a global note, the clearing system business day (for this purpose, a day on which Clea rstream and Euroclear settle payments in euro) immediately preceding the relevant interest payment and (ii) in a ll other cases, 15 calendar days prior to the relevant interest payment dat e (whether or not a Business Day) (for the purposes of clauses (i) and (ii), such day, the "Record Date").
nodes.summary:
- Roles and administration: The Trustee serves as paying agent, transfer agent, and registrar. Notes may be presented for transfer/exchange at the registrar’s offices. The Issuer may change these agents without notice to holders (paying agent changes require notice to the Trustee).
- Maturity and size: Notes mature on June 23, 2027 at 100% of principal. Aggregate offering size is €500,000,000. No sinking fund. Notes are subject to defeasance and covenant defeasance.
- Business day/payment convention: If a payment or redemption date is not a Business Day, payment moves to the next Business Day with no additional interest for the delay. Same applies at maturity.
- Interest terms: Interest accrues from issuance and is payable annually each June 23, starting June 23, 2021.
  - Record Dates: For global notes, the clearing system business day immediately before the payment date; for others, 15 calendar days before the payment date (whether or not a Business Day).
  - Day-count: Actual/Actual (ICMA), from and including the last interest payment date (or June 23, 2020 if none) to but excluding the next scheduled payment date.
  - If an interest payment date is not a Business Day, it is postponed to the next Business Day with no extra interest.
- Currency and fallback: All payments (interest, premium, principal, redemptions/repurchases) are in euro. If the euro becomes unavailable or ceases to be used by EMU member states or for international settlements, payments switch to U.S. dollars until euro use resumes.
  - USD conversion: Use the Federal Reserve Board–mandated rate as of the close two Business Days before payment; if unavailable, the most recent WSJ published USD/EUR rate by two Business Days before; if still unavailable, the Issuer determines the rate based on the most recently available market rate.
  - Payments in USD under these circumstances are not Events of Default. The Trustee and paying agent are not responsible for any calculation or conversion.
- Reference rate example: As of August 14, 2020, the Fed’s published euro/USD rate was €1 = $1.1833.

nodes.title: Issuance in euro
nodes.heading: Issuance in euro
nodes.start_phrase: All payments of interest, premium, if any, and principal, including paym ents made upon any redemption or repurchase of the Notes, will be made in euro; provided that if the euro is unavailable to us due to the imposition of exchange controls or other circumstances bey ond our control or if the euro is no longer being used by the then member st ates of the European Monetary Union that have adopted the euro as their currency or for the settlement of transactions by public institutions of or within the international banking communit y, then all payments in respect of the Notes will be made in U.S. dollars until the euro is again available to us or so used.
nodes.summary:
- Parties and administration: The Trustee also serves as paying agent, transfer agent, and registrar. Notes may be presented for transfer/exchange at the registrar’s offices. The Issuer may change these agents without notice to holders, but must notify the Trustee if the paying agent changes.
- General terms: €500,000,000 aggregate principal amount. Notes mature on June 23, 2027 at 100% of principal. No sinking fund. Subject to defeasance and covenant defeasance. If a payment or redemption date is not a Business Day, payment is made on the next Business Day with no additional interest; same applies to any Additional Amounts.
- Interest: Interest accrues from issuance and is payable annually on June 23, starting June 23, 2021. Record Date: for global notes, the clearing system business day (when Clearstream/Euroclear settle in euro) immediately before payment; for others, 15 calendar days before payment (whether or not a Business Day). Day count: Actual/Actual (ICMA). If an interest payment date is not a Business Day, payment moves to the next Business Day without extra interest; same for maturity payments.
- Currency and FX fallback: All payments are in euro. If the euro becomes unavailable or is no longer used by EMU member states or for international settlement, payments switch to U.S. dollars until euro use resumes. Conversion uses the Federal Reserve Board mandated rate two Business Days before payment; if unavailable, the most recent USD/EUR rate in The Wall Street Journal; if that is unavailable, a rate determined by the Issuer based on the most recently available market rate. USD payments under this fallback do not constitute an Event of Default. The Trustee and paying agent are not responsible for FX calculations. Example reference rate as of August 14, 2020: €1 = $1.1833.

nodes.title: Further issues
nodes.heading: Further issues
nodes.start_phrase: The indenture provides that the Notes may be issued from time to time without limitation as to aggregate principal amount.
nodes.summary:
- Further issues: The issuer may issue unlimited additional notes under the same indenture without holder consent, with identical terms except for certain dates and transfer/registration provisions; non-fungible tranches for U.S. tax purposes will have different CUSIPs. Any such Additional Notes form a single series with the existing Notes.
- Guarantee: Amcor, Amcor Finance (USA), Inc., Amcor Pty Ltd, and Bemis Company, Inc. unconditionally guarantee timely payment of principal, interest, premium, and other amounts on the Notes. Guarantees remain until all obligations are satisfied, and holders can proceed directly against guarantors upon an event of default.
- Additional subsidiary guarantors: Amcor must cause any subsidiary that guarantees or is otherwise obligated on any Specified Indebtedness to become a guarantor of the Notes within 30 days via a supplemental indenture. Any legal limitations required by the subsidiary’s jurisdiction may be included, provided they match limitations in that subsidiary’s other Specified Indebtedness guarantees.
- Release of subsidiary guarantors: A subsidiary guarantor may be released without noteholder consent if no default is continuing and either it ceases to be a subsidiary or it has no outstanding guarantees/obligations on Specified Indebtedness (or is released under the Notes concurrently with release under all such indebtedness).
- Ranking: The Notes are unsecured, unsubordinated obligations of the issuer ranking pari passu with its other unsecured, unsubordinated debt; the guarantees are likewise unsecured and unsubordinated obligations of each guarantor, subject to any debts preferred by law.

nodes.title: Guarantee
nodes.heading: Guarantee
nodes.start_phrase: Under the Guarantee, each of Amcor, Amcor Finance (USA), Inc. (“AFUI”), Amcor Pty Ltd a nd Bemis Company, Inc. (“Bemis,” and collectively, the “Guarantors”) wil l fully and unconditionally guarantee the due and punctual payment of the principal, interest, pre mium (if any) and all other amounts due under the indenture and on the Notes when the Notes become due and payable, whether at maturity, pursuant to optional redemption, by acceleration or oth erwise, in each case after any applicable grace periods or notice requirem ents, according to the terms of the Notes.
nodes.summary:

The guarantees are unsecured, unsubordinated obligations of each guarantor, ranking pari passu with their other unsecured, unsubordinated debt, except for debt mandatorily preferred by law.

nodes.title: Additional subsidiary guarantors
nodes.heading: Additional subsidiary guarantors
nodes.start_phrase: Amcor has covenanted and agreed under the indenture that it will ca use each of its Subsidiaries (other than the Issuer and any Subsidiary that is already a Guarantor under the indenture) that at any time has outstanding a guarantee with respect to any Specified Ind ebtedness, or is otherwise an obligor, a co-obligor or jointly liable with the Issuer or any applicable Guarantor with respect to any Specified Indebtedness, to execute and deliver to the Trustee a supple mental indenture within 30 days of such Subsidiary guaranteeing, or otherwise becoming an obligor, a co-obligor or jointly liable with the Issuer or any applicable Guarantor in respect of, such Specifi ed Indebtedness, pursuant to which such Subsidiary will guarantee t he Notes issued under the indenture on the same terms and subject to the same conditions and limitations as set forth in the i ndenture.
nodes.summary:

Guarantees remain until all obligations are satisfied, and holders may proceed directly against guarantors upon a default.

nodes.title: Release of subsidiary guarantors
nodes.heading: Release of subsidiary guarantors
nodes.start_phrase: As more fully described in the indenture, any Subsidiary of Amcor that provides a Guarantee in respect of the Notes (a "Subsidiary Guarantor") may be relea sed at any time from its Guarantee without the consent of any holder of the Notes if, at such time, no Defaul t or Event of Default has occurred and is continuing, and either (a) such Sub sidiary Guarantor is no longer, or at the time of release will no longer be, a Subsidiary of Amcor or (b) such Subsidiary Guarantor shal l not have outstanding a guarantee with respect to any Specified Indebtedn ess or otherwise be an obligor, co- obligor or jointly liable with respect to any Specified Indebtedness (or sha ll be released with respect to its Guarantee under the indenture simultane ously with its release under guarantees or other obligations with respect to all Specified Indebtedness).
nodes.summary:
- Further issuance: The indenture allows the issuer to issue unlimited additional notes under the same terms as existing Notes without holder consent (differences may include issue date, initial interest accrual/payment dates, and transfer/registration terms). If not U.S. tax-fungible with existing Notes, additional notes will have a different CUSIP. Any such Additional Notes will form a single series with the existing Notes.
- Guarantee: Amcor, Amcor Finance (USA), Inc., Amcor Pty Ltd, and Bemis Company, Inc. fully and unconditionally guarantee payment of principal, interest, premium (if any), and all other amounts due on the Notes when payable, regardless of the enforceability of the Notes. The guarantees remain until all obligations are satisfied. Holders may proceed directly against the guarantors upon an event of default without first pursuing the issuer.
- Additional subsidiary guarantors: Amcor must cause any subsidiary (other than the issuer or an existing guarantor) that guarantees, or is otherwise obligated with respect to, any Specified Indebtedness to become a guarantor of the Notes within 30 days via a supplemental indenture. Such supplemental indentures may include jurisdiction-required limitations, which must also appear in that subsidiary’s other Specified Indebtedness guarantees.
- Release of subsidiary guarantors: A subsidiary guarantor may be released without noteholder consent if no default or event of default is continuing and either (a) it ceases to be a subsidiary of Amcor, or (b) it has no outstanding guarantee or other obligation with respect to any Specified Indebtedness (or is released under those obligations simultaneously).
- Ranking: The Notes are unsecured, unsubordinated obligations of the issuer ranking pari passu with its other unsecured, unsubordinated debt. Each guarantee is an unsecured, unsubordinated obligation of the applicable guarantor ranking pari passu with its other unsecured, unsubordinated indebtedness, subject to any debt mandatorily preferred by law.

nodes.title: Ranking
nodes.heading: Ranking
nodes.start_phrase: The Notes are unsecured obligations of the Issuer and rank on a parity basis with all of the Issuer's other unsecured and unsubordinated obligatio ns, and each of the Guarantees are an unsecured obligation of the applicable Guarantor and rank on a parity basis with all other unsecured and unsubordinated indebtedness of such Guarantor except, in each case, indebtedness mandatorily preferred by law.
nodes.summary:
- Further issues: The issuer may create unlimited Additional Notes under the same indenture without holder consent. These will have identical terms to existing Notes (except for certain dating and transfer terms) and form a single series; if not U.S. tax‑fungible, they will have a different CUSIP.
- Guarantees: Amcor, Amcor Finance (USA), Inc. (AFUI), Amcor Pty Ltd, and Bemis Company, Inc. irrevocably and unconditionally guarantee all amounts due on the Notes. Holders may proceed directly against the Guarantors upon an event of default, and the guarantees remain until all obligations are satisfied.
- Additional subsidiary guarantors: Any Amcor subsidiary that guarantees, or becomes an obligor/co‑obligor for, any Specified Indebtedness must, within 30 days, become a guarantor of the Notes via supplemental indenture on the same terms. Required local‑law limitations may be included if they are also included in that subsidiary’s other Specified Indebtedness guarantees.
- Release of subsidiary guarantors: A Subsidiary Guarantor may be released without holder consent if no Default/Event of Default is continuing and the subsidiary ceases to be an Amcor subsidiary, or no longer guarantees/is an obligor for any Specified Indebtedness (or is released therefrom simultaneously).
- Ranking and subordination: The Notes and Guarantees are unsecured, unsubordinated obligations ranking pari passu with other unsecured, unsubordinated debt of the Issuer/Guarantors. They are effectively subordinated to secured debt to the extent of collateral and structurally subordinated to liabilities of non‑guarantor subsidiaries. As of June 30, 2020: Issuer/Guarantors had $6,129.8 million total debt (none secured); non‑guarantor subsidiaries (including JVs) had $104.8 million total debt ($30.5 million secured) and represented 93% of sales revenue. Initial Guarantors are Amcor, AFUI, Amcor Pty Ltd, and Bemis.
- Registration of transfer and exchange: Notes may be exchanged or transferred (subject to global note limits) through the Registrar/transfer agents with proper documentation. No service charge applies, but taxes/governmental charges may be required. Transfers may be declined during the 15 days before any payment date. The Trustee is the Registrar, and there must always be a transfer agent in Manhattan, New York.
