nodes.title: Registration of transfer and exchange
nodes.heading: Registration of transfer and exchange
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to the limitations applicable to global notes, the Not es may be presented for exchange for other Notes of any authorized denomination s and of a like tenor and aggregate principal amount or for registration of transfer by the holder thereof or his attorney duly authorized in writing and, if so required by the Issuer, the Guarantors or the Trustee, with the form of transfer thereon duly endorsed or accompanied by a written instrument of transfer in form satisfact ory to the Issuer, the Guarantors or the Registrar (as defined below) duly ex ecuted, at the office of the Registrar or at the office of any other transfer agent designated by the Issuer or such Guarant ors for such purpose.
nodes.summary:
- Subordination of Notes: The Notes are unsecured and effectively subordinated to any existing and future secured obligations of the Issuer up to the value of the collateral securing those obligations; in bankruptcy or insolvency, secured lenders have priority claims to collateral.
- Subordination of Guarantees: Each Guarantee is unsecured and effectively subordinated to any existing and future secured obligations of the relevant Guarantor to the extent of collateral value; in bankruptcy or insolvency, secured lenders of each Guarantor have priority claims. As of June 30, 2020, the Issuer and Guarantors had no secured indebtedness outstanding.
- Structural subordination: The Notes and related Guarantees are structurally subordinated to all existing and future indebtedness and liabilities of Amcor subsidiaries that do not guarantee the Notes (other than Amcor UK), including future acquired or established subsidiaries that do not provide guarantees.
- Guarantors: Initial Guarantors are Amcor, AFUI, Amcor Pty Ltd, and Bemis.
- Indebtedness snapshot (as of June 30, 2020): Issuer and Guarantors had $6,129.8 million in total indebtedness (none secured). Non‑guarantor subsidiaries (including joint ventures) had $104.8 million of total indebtedness ($30.5 million secured) and represented 93% of Amcor’s sales revenue for the year ended June 30, 2020.
- Registration of transfer and exchange: Notes may be exchanged or transferred for Notes of authorized denominations and like tenor/aggregate principal amount upon satisfactory documentation of title and identity; no service charge applies, but holders must cover related taxes or governmental charges.
- Transfer mechanics and limitations: The Registrar may decline requests during the 15 days before any payment date. The Trustee is appointed as Registrar, and the Issuer/Guarantors may change or add transfer agents, with a continuing requirement to maintain a transfer agent in the Borough of Manhattan, New York City.
- Payment of Additional Amounts (tax gross-up): Payments of principal, premium, interest, and under the Guarantees will be made without withholding or deduction for taxes imposed by specified “Relevant Jurisdictions” (U.S., Jersey, Australia, U.K., and any jurisdiction where the Issuer/Guarantor becomes tax resident or through which payments are made). If withholding is required, Additional Amounts will be paid to gross up payments, subject to specified exceptions, including an exception beginning with taxes that would not have been imposed but for holder-specific circumstances (full list not included in the excerpt).

nodes.title: General
nodes.heading: General
nodes.start_phrase: Subject to the limitations applicable to global notes, the Not es may be presented for exchange for other Notes of any authorized denomination s and of a like tenor and aggregate principal amount or for registration of transfer by the holder thereof or his attorney duly authorized in writing and, if so required by the Issuer, the Guarantors or the Trustee, with the form of transfer thereon duly endorsed or accompanied by a written instrument of transfer in form satisfact ory to the Issuer, the Guarantors or the Registrar (as defined below) duly ex ecuted, at the office of the Registrar or at the office of any other transfer agent designated by the Issuer or such Guarant ors for such purpose.
nodes.summary:
- Priority and subordination:
  - The Notes are unsecured and effectively subordinated to existing and future secured obligations of the Issuer to the extent of the collateral’s value; secured lenders have priority in insolvency.
  - Each Guarantee is unsecured and effectively subordinated to the corresponding Guarantor’s secured obligations; secured lenders of a Guarantor have priority in its insolvency.
  - Structural subordination: the Notes and Guarantees are structurally subordinated to all liabilities (secured or unsecured) of non-guarantor subsidiaries.

- Current indebtedness and guarantor scope (as of June 30, 2020):
  - Issuer and Guarantors: $6,129.8 million total indebtedness (excluding intercompany), none secured.
  - Non‑guarantor subsidiaries (including JVs): $104.8 million total indebtedness, $30.5 million secured; they represented 93% of Amcor’s sales revenue for the year.
  - Initial Guarantors: Amcor, AFUI, Amcor Pty Ltd, and Bemis; Amcor UK is the Issuer.

- Registration of transfer and exchange:
  - Notes may be exchanged or transferred for Notes of authorized denominations of like tenor and aggregate principal amount, subject to global note limitations.
  - Transfers/exchanges require satisfactory documentation and identification; no service charge, but holders must cover applicable taxes or governmental charges.
  - Registrar may decline requests during the 15 days preceding any payment date.
  - The Trustee is appointed as Registrar; Issuer/Guarantors may change or add transfer agents but must maintain a transfer agent in the Borough of Manhattan, New York City.

- Payment of additional amounts (tax gross-up):
  - Payments on the Notes and Guarantees will be made without withholding for taxes imposed by specified Relevant Jurisdictions (U.S., Jersey, Australia, U.K., or any jurisdiction of tax residence or payment) unless required by law.
  - If withholding is required, the Issuer/Guarantors will pay Additional Amounts to gross-up payments so holders receive amounts as if no withholding occurred, subject to specified exceptions (partially listed and truncated in the excerpt).

nodes.title: Payment of additional amounts
nodes.heading: Payment of additional amounts
nodes.start_phrase: All payments of, or in respect of, principal of, and any premium and intere st on, the Notes, and all payments pursuant to the Guarantees, sha ll be made without withholding or deduction for, or on account of, any present or future taxes, duties, assessments or governme ntal charges of whatever nature imposed or levied by or on behalf of the Uni ted States (including the District of Columbia and any state, possession or territory thereof), Jersey, Australia, the United Ki ngdom or any other jurisdiction in which the Issuer or the Guarantors bec omes a resident for tax purposes (whether by merger, consolidation or otherwise) or through which the Issuer or any Guara ntor makes payment on the Notes or any Guarantee (each, a "Relevant Jurisdi ction") or any political subdivision or taxing authority of any of the foregoing, unless such taxes, duties, assessments or governmental charges are required by the law of the Relevant Jurisdic tion or any political subdivision or taxing authority thereof or therein to be withheld or deducted.
nodes.summary:
- Capital structure and priority: The Notes and related Guarantees are unsecured and effectively subordinated to any existing or future secured obligations to the extent of the collateral value. In insolvency, secured creditors have priority over collateral. As of June 30, 2020, the Issuer and Guarantors had no secured debt outstanding.
- Structural subordination: The Notes and Guarantees are structurally subordinated to all liabilities (secured or unsecured) of non-guarantor subsidiaries. Initial Guarantors are Amcor, AFUI, Amcor Pty Ltd, and Bemis.
- Indebtedness profile (as of June 30, 2020): Issuer and Guarantors had $6,129.8 million of total indebtedness (excluding intercompany, none secured). Non-guarantor subsidiaries (including JVs) had $104.8 million of total indebtedness ($30.5 million secured) and accounted for 93% of Amcor’s sales revenue.
- Registration of transfer and exchange: Notes may be exchanged or transferred through the Registrar/transfer agents upon satisfactory documentation and identity verification. No service charge applies, but holders may bear taxes/governmental charges. Requests may be declined within 15 days before a payment date. The Trustee acts as Registrar, and a transfer agent must always be maintained in New York City (Borough of Manhattan).
- Payment of Additional Amounts (tax gross-up): Payments on Notes and Guarantees will be made free of withholding/deduction for taxes imposed by Relevant Jurisdictions (U.S., Jersey, Australia, U.K., or others where the Issuer/Guarantors become tax resident or make payments), with Additional Amounts paid if withholding is required.
- Gross-up exceptions: No Additional Amounts for taxes arising from holder’s connections to a Relevant Jurisdiction (e.g., residency, presence, permanent establishment), presentation in a taxing jurisdiction when not required, late presentation beyond 30 days, specified U.S. tax status/connections, estate/gift/transfer taxes, non-withheld taxes, failure to provide required documentation (e.g., IRS Forms W‑8/W‑9 or similar), Australian Commissioner of Taxation notices, FATCA-related withholding, combinations of these, or where the holder is not the sole beneficial owner (certain fiduciary/partnership contexts).
- Interpretation and survival: References to payments include any due Additional Amounts; obligations to pay Additional Amounts survive indenture termination and final payments.
- Additional amounts on reorganizations: Certain mergers, consolidations, or asset transfers by the Issuer/Guarantors may trigger additional gross-up obligations.
- Tax redemption (“tax call”): If changes in law/administration would require payment of Additional Amounts on the next interest date and cannot be avoided by commercially reasonable measures, the Issuer may redeem all (not part) of the Notes at 100% of principal plus accrued interest, with 30–60 days’ notice. Notice timing restrictions apply (not earlier than 60 days before the obligation would arise), the obligation must still be in effect at notice, and an opinion of counsel and officer’s certificate are required. Notice mechanics differ for global notes (via Euroclear/Clearstream) vs. definitive notes.
- Optional redemption (make-whole): The Notes are optionally redeemable by the Issuer, in whole or in part, at the greater of 100% of principal or a make-whole amount determined by a Quotation Agent (provision text is truncated).

nodes.title: Redemption for changes in withholding taxes
nodes.heading: Redemption for changes in withholding taxes
nodes.start_phrase: If, as the result of (a) any change in or any amendment to the laws, regulatio ns, published practice or published tax rulings of any Relevant Jurisdict ion, or of any political subdivision or taxing authority thereof or therein, affecting taxation,
nodes.summary:
- Additional Amounts (tax gross-up): The issuer and guarantors agree to pay Additional Amounts on the Notes and Guarantees to offset certain withholding taxes, with exclusions where payments are treated as received by fiduciaries, partnerships, or beneficial owners who would not be entitled to such amounts if they were the holder. References to principal, premium, interest, or Guarantee payments are deemed to include these Additional Amounts where applicable. The obligation to pay Additional Amounts survives termination of the indenture and full payment of the Notes. Additional Amounts may also arise due to consolidations, mergers, or transfers under the “Consolidation, merger and sale of assets” covenant.
- Tax redemption (change of law): If, due to post-issuance changes in law, regulations, published practice/rulings, or their official administration/interpretation in a Relevant Jurisdiction (including one that later becomes relevant through corporate changes or change in place of payment), the issuer or a guarantor would be required to pay Additional Amounts on the next interest payment and cannot avoid this by commercially reasonable measures, the issuer may redeem all (not part) of the affected Notes at 100% of principal plus accrued interest, with 30–60 days’ notice. Conditions: (1) notice cannot be given earlier than 60 days before the earliest date the Additional Amounts would be due; and (2) the obligation to pay such amounts must still exist when notice is given. Before redeeming, the issuer/guarantor/successor must deliver to the trustee an opinion of counsel confirming conditions are met and an officer’s certificate stating the obligation cannot be avoided by commercially reasonable measures. Notice mechanics differ for global notes (via Euroclear/Clearstream) and definitive notes (directly to holders).
- Optional redemption (make-whole): The Notes are optionally redeemable, in whole or in part, at the issuer’s option at the greater of 100% of principal or a make-whole amount determined by a Quotation Agent (section continues beyond the excerpt).

nodes.title: Optional redemption
nodes.heading: Optional redemption
nodes.start_phrase: The Notes are redeemable, in whole or in part, at the option of the Issuer at a ny time at a redemption price equal to the greater of (1) 100% of the princi pal amount of the Notes being redeemed
nodes.summary:
- Additional Amounts (tax gross-up): Clarifies when Additional Amounts are payable on Notes and Guarantees, including how payments to fiduciaries, partnerships, or beneficial owners are treated so that gross-up is not provided where the ultimate holder wouldn’t have been entitled. States that references to principal, premium, or interest include Additional Amounts where applicable, and that such obligations may also arise after certain mergers or asset transfers. Obligation to pay Additional Amounts survives termination of the indenture and full payment of the Notes.
- Tax redemption (change in withholding): The Issuer may redeem all (not part) of the Notes at 100% plus accrued interest if changes in law, regulation, published practice/rulings, or official interpretation in a Relevant Jurisdiction after the issue date (or after that jurisdiction becomes relevant) would require payment of Additional Amounts that cannot be avoided by commercially reasonable measures. Conditions include: 30–60 days’ notice; no notice earlier than 60 days before the obligation would arise; the obligation must still be in effect when notice is given; and delivery to the Trustee of a legal opinion and officer’s certificate confirming the conditions and unavoidability.
- Optional redemption (make-whole and par call): Redeemable at the Issuer’s option, in whole or in part, at the greater of (1) 100% of principal or (2) the make-whole amount based on the present value of remaining payments discounted at the Comparable Government Bond Rate plus 30 bps, plus accrued interest. On or after the Par Call Date (April 23, 2027), redeemable at 100% of principal plus accrued interest. Minimum denominations: €100,000 and €1,000 increments. Interest due on or before the redemption date remains payable to holders of record on the relevant record date.
- Definitions and calculation mechanics: Defines Comparable Government Bond (German government bond closest to the par call date, as determined by an independent investment bank acting as Quotation Agent with broker input) and Comparable Government Bond Rate (gross redemption yield based on middle market prices at 11:00 A.M. London time, three business days before redemption; price rounded to three decimals).
- Redemption procedures: 30–60 days’ notice via Euroclear/Clearstream for global notes or by mail for definitive notes. Interest ceases to accrue on redeemed Notes from the redemption date unless the Issuer defaults. If partially redeemed, selection is per Euroclear/Clearstream procedures or pro rata/by lot/other fair method; the Trustee may select in amounts of €100,000 and €1,000 increments.
- Governing law: The indenture and Notes are governed by New York law.
- Trustee relationship: Discloses existing and potential ordinary-course banking and custodial relationships with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas, which may also serve as trustee for other Issuer/Guarantor debt.

nodes.title: Governing law
nodes.heading: Governing law
nodes.start_phrase: The indenture and the Notes are governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of New York.
nodes.summary:
- Early redemption pricing: Prior to the Par Call Date, Notes may be redeemed at a “make-whole” price equal to the present value of principal plus remaining scheduled interest (excluding interest accrued to the redemption date), discounted on an Actual/Actual ICMA basis at the Comparable Government Bond Rate + 30 bps, plus accrued and unpaid interest to the redemption date.
- Par call: On or after the Par Call Date (April 23, 2027), Notes are redeemable at 100% of principal plus accrued interest.
- Minimum denominations after partial redemption: Any remaining principal must be €100,000 or higher integral multiples of €1,000.
- Interest payments around redemption: Interest installments due on or before the redemption date are paid on the scheduled payment date to holders of record as of the relevant record date.
- Definitions and determination mechanics:
  - Comparable Government Bond: A German government bond with maturity closest to the Par Call Date (or another appropriate German government bond) selected by an independent investment bank (the Quotation Agent) with input from three brokers/market makers.
  - Comparable Government Bond Rate: The price (to three decimal places, 0.0005 rounded up) at which the Notes’ gross redemption yield equals that of the Comparable Government Bond, based on its middle market price at 11:00 a.m. London time on the third Business Day before redemption, as determined by the Quotation Agent.
- Redemption notice: 30–60 days’ prior notice; delivered via Euroclear/Clearstream for global notes or by mail for definitive notes. Interest ceases to accrue on redeemed Notes on and after the redemption date unless the issuer defaults on payment.
- Selection for partial redemption: 
  - If held through Euroclear/Clearstream, per their standard procedures.
  - If not in a clearing system, on a pro rata basis, by lot, or another fair method determined by the Trustee.
  - Trustee may select Notes/portions in amounts of €100,000 and integral multiples of €1,000 in excess thereof.
- Governing law: State of New York.
- Trustee relationship disclosure: Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas serves as trustee; the issuer and guarantors have existing and may have future ordinary-course banking/custodial relationships with Deutsche Bank or its affiliates; Deutsche Bank may also act as trustee for other issuer/guarantor debt.

nodes.title: Concerning our relationship with the trustee
nodes.heading: Concerning our relationship with the trustee
nodes.start_phrase: The Issuer and the Guarantors have commercial deposits and custod ial arrangements with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas, or "Deutsch e Bank," and may have borrowed money from Deutsche Bank or its affiliates in the normal course of business.
nodes.summary:
- Optional redemption terms:
  - Before the Par Call Date (April 23, 2027): Make-whole call at a price equal to the sum of (a) the present value of principal and (b) the present value of remaining scheduled interest payments (excluding interest accrued to the redemption date), discounted on an Actual/Actual ICMA basis to the redemption date at the Comparable Government Bond Rate + 30 bps, plus accrued and unpaid interest to the redemption date.
  - On or after the Par Call Date: Redeemable at 100% of principal (par), plus accrued and unpaid interest to the redemption date.
- Interest payment treatment: Installments due on or before the redemption date remain payable to holders of record on the relevant record date.
- Denominations and partial redemptions:
  - Any Note remaining after a partial redemption must be €100,000 or higher integral multiples of €1,000.
  - Trustee may select Notes or portions for redemption in amounts of €100,000 or integral multiples of €1,000 in excess thereof.
- Notice of redemption: 30–60 days’ notice; for global notes, via Euroclear/Clearstream to holders; for definitive notes, by mail to registered holders.
- Interest cessation: Interest stops accruing on redeemed Notes (or portions) from the redemption date, unless the Issuer defaults on the redemption price and accrued interest.
- Selection of Notes if less than all are redeemed:
  - Through Euroclear/Clearstream: in accordance with their standard procedures.
  - Outside clearing systems: pro rata, by lot, or another method the Trustee deems fair and appropriate.
- Definitions and mechanics:
  - Comparable Government Bond: A German government bond with maturity closest to the Par Call Date (or another appropriate German bond as determined by an independent Quotation Agent with broker/market-maker input).
  - Comparable Government Bond Rate: The price (as a percentage, rounded to three decimals) at which the gross redemption yield on the Notes (if purchased on the third Business Day before redemption) equals the gross redemption yield of the Comparable Government Bond, based on its middle market price at 11:00 a.m. London time on that day, as determined by the Quotation Agent.
- Governing law: The indenture and the Notes are governed by New York law.
- Trustee relationship disclosure: The Issuer and Guarantors have banking, custodial, and potential lending relationships with Deutsche Bank Trust Company Americas and its affiliates and may maintain similar relationships in the future; Deutsche Bank may also act as trustee for other Issuer/Guarantor debt.

nodes.title: Offers to purchase; open market purchases
nodes.heading: Offers to purchase; open market purchases
nodes.start_phrase: Neither the Issuer nor any of the Guarantors is required to make any sinking fu nd payments or any offers to purchase with respect to the Notes or the Guarante es.
nodes.summary:
- No mandatory redemption: The issuer and guarantors are not required to make sinking fund payments or any mandatory offers to purchase the notes; they may repurchase notes at any time in the open market or otherwise.
- Change of Control repurchase right: Upon a Change of Control Triggering Event, unless the notes are redeemed, each holder can require the issuer to repurchase all or part of their notes at 101% of principal plus accrued interest, subject to record-date interest rights.
- Notice and timing mechanics: The issuer must mail a notice of the Change of Control Offer within 30 days of the event (or, at its option, after public announcement but before consummation), setting a purchase date 30–60 days from mailing; the offer may be conditioned on consummation of the Change of Control. Holders must tender notes (with the election form or via book-entry) by the third business day before the payment date.
- Third-party offer: The issuer need not make a Change of Control Offer if a third party conducts a compliant offer and purchases all properly tendered notes.
- Scope ambiguity: The term “all or substantially all” of assets within the Change of Control definition lacks a precise legal standard, creating potential uncertainty for certain asset dispositions.
- Limitation on Liens covenant: Amcor and its subsidiaries may not secure indebtedness with liens on their assets unless the notes and guarantees are equally and ratably secured (or secured prior to such indebtedness), with exceptions, including:
  - Liens securing indebtedness outstanding on the indenture date.
  - Liens securing intercompany indebtedness owed to Amcor or its subsidiaries (excluding a Project Subsidiary).
  - Pre-existing liens on assets acquired after the issue date, subject to conditions (e.g., not created in anticipation of the acquisition).

nodes.title: Certain covenants
nodes.heading: Certain covenants
nodes.start_phrase: Pursuant to the indenture, the Issuer and each of the Guarantors have cove nanted and agreed as follows.
nodes.summary:
- No mandatory purchases or sinking fund: The issuer and guarantors are not required to make sinking fund payments or any purchase offers for the notes/guarantees, but may buy notes at any time in the open market or otherwise.
- Change of Control repurchase right: If a Change of Control Triggering Event occurs (and the issuer does not redeem the notes), each holder may require the issuer to repurchase all or part of their notes at 101% of principal plus accrued and unpaid interest to the purchase date, subject to record date interest rights.
- Notice and timing mechanics: Within 30 days of the triggering event (or earlier after public announcement of a pending change of control), the issuer must mail notice to holders and the trustee. The purchase date must be 30–60 days from mailing (subject to law). If notice is mailed before consummation, the offer may be conditioned on the change of control occurring by the payment date.
- Holder tender procedures: Holders must deliver notes (with the “Option of Holder to Elect Purchase” completed) or transfer by book-entry to the trustee by close of business on the third business day before the payment date.
- Third-party substitute offer: The issuer need not make its own offer if a third party makes a compliant offer and purchases all properly tendered notes.
- Scope uncertainty: The “Change of Control” definition includes transfers of “all or substantially all” assets; the precise meaning of “substantially all” is uncertain under applicable law, creating potential ambiguity in trigger applicability for partial asset dispositions.
- Limitation on liens covenant: While notes/guarantees are outstanding, Amcor and its subsidiaries may not place liens on assets to secure indebtedness unless the notes and guarantees are equally and ratably (or seniorly) secured, subject to permitted liens, including:
  - Existing liens securing indebtedness outstanding on the indenture date.
  - Liens securing indebtedness owed to Amcor or its subsidiaries (excluding a Project Subsidiary).
  - Pre-existing liens on assets acquired after the original issue date, provided the lien was not created in anticipation of the acquisition and other stated conditions (partially excerpted).

nodes.title: Offer to repurchase upon change of control triggering event
nodes.heading: Offer to repurchase upon change of control triggering event
nodes.start_phrase: The indenture provides that, upon the occurrence of a Change Of Control Tri ggering Event, unless the Issuer has exercised its right to redeem the No tes in accordance with their terms, each holder of the Notes will have the right to require the Issuer to purchase all or a portio n of such holder's Notes pursuant to the offer described below (the "Chang e of Control Offer"), at a purchase price equal to 101% of the principal amount thereof plus accrued and unpaid interest, if a ny, to the date of purchase, subject to the rights of holders of the Notes o n the relevant record date to receive interest due on the relevant interest payment date.
nodes.summary:
- No obligation for sinking fund payments or mandatory offers to purchase the Notes or Guarantees; the Issuer or Guarantors may repurchase Notes at any time in the open market or otherwise.
- Change of Control Triggering Event put right: unless the Notes are redeemed, each holder may require the Issuer to repurchase all or part of its Notes at 101% of principal plus accrued and unpaid interest, subject to record-date interest rights.
- Change of Control Offer mechanics: notice by first-class mail within 30 days of the event (or earlier after public announcement), setting a payment date 30–60 days from mailing; offer may be conditioned on consummation of the Change of Control; holders must surrender Notes (with the election form) or deliver by book-entry to the Trustee by the third business day before the payment date.
- If a third party makes a compliant offer and purchases all properly tendered Notes, the Issuer need not make a separate offer.
- Acknowledgment that “all or substantially all” of assets is not precisely defined in law, creating potential uncertainty about when the repurchase requirement applies in partial asset disposition scenarios.
- Limitation on Liens covenant: so long as any Notes/Guarantees are outstanding, Amcor and its Subsidiaries will not place Liens on assets to secure Indebtedness unless the Notes/Guarantees are equally and ratably secured, subject to exceptions, including:
  - Liens securing Indebtedness outstanding on the indenture date.
  - Liens securing Indebtedness owed to Amcor or a Subsidiary (other than a Project Subsidiary).
  - Pre-existing Liens on assets acquired after the issue date, provided they were not created in anticipation of the acquisition and subject to stated conditions (text truncated).

nodes.title: Limitation on liens
nodes.heading: Limitation on liens
nodes.start_phrase: Pursuant to the indenture, for so long as any of the Notes or any of the Guara ntees are outstanding, Amcor will not, and will not permit any Subsi diary to, create, assume, incur, issue or otherwise have outstanding any Lien upon, or with respect to, any of the present or future business, property, undertaking, assets or revenues (including, without l imitation, any Equity Interests and uncalled capital), whether now owned or hereafter acquired (together, "assets") of Amc or or such Subsidiary, to secure any Indebtedness, unless the Notes and applicable Guarantees are secured by such Lien equally and ratably with (or prior to) such Indebtedness, except for the follow ing, to which this covenant shall not apply:
nodes.summary:
- No mandatory repurchases or sinking fund: The issuer and guarantors are not required to make sinking fund payments or purchase offers for the notes, but may buy notes at any time in the open market or otherwise.
- Change of Control repurchase right:
  - If a Change of Control Triggering Event occurs (and the issuer has not redeemed the notes), each holder may require the issuer to repurchase all or part of its notes at 101% of principal plus accrued interest.
  - Notice must be mailed within 30 days of the event (or earlier after public announcement), with a payment date 30–60 days after notice; if mailed before consummation, the offer is conditional on the transaction closing.
  - Holders must deliver notes (or transfer by book-entry) by the third business day before the payment date.
  - A compliant third‑party offer that purchases all properly tendered notes can satisfy the issuer’s obligation.
  - The meaning of “all or substantially all” assets in the Change of Control definition is uncertain under applicable law.
- Limitation on Liens (negative pledge):
  - Amcor and its subsidiaries will not place liens on assets to secure indebtedness unless the notes (and guarantees) are equally and ratably secured, subject to extensive permitted lien exceptions, including:
    - Existing liens; intercompany debt; pre‑existing liens on acquired assets (with limits and discharge timelines); liens on assets of newly acquired/merged subsidiaries (with limits and discharge timelines); purchase-money and acquisition/development liens limited to the financed assets; export/import financing liens; development agency financing liens; joint venture-related liens; ordinary‑course goods/letters of credit liens (≤180 days); liens arising by operation of law; project‑asset liens securing limited‑recourse debt; banking netting/set‑off; refinancings of permitted liens (with scope and amount limits and original discharge timelines); liens from changes in lease accounting standards; and an additional basket allowing other secured indebtedness up to 10% of Total Tangible Assets.
  - No restriction on the amount of unsecured indebtedness.
- Consolidation, merger, sale/lease of substantially all assets:
  - The issuer or a guarantor may not merge, consolidate, or transfer/lease substantially all assets to a non‑issuer/non‑guarantor unless:
    - The successor is duly organized and existing, is or becomes the issuer/guarantor, and assumes all obligations under the notes/guarantees and indenture (including Additional Amounts).
    - No Event of Default (or event that could become one) exists immediately after the transaction, giving effect to any debt incurred.
    - If the successor is organized outside the U.S., its states/DC, Jersey, Australia, or the U.K./its territories, it must:
      - Indemnify holders/beneficial owners for taxes and related costs arising from the transaction.
      - Ensure all payments on the notes/guarantees are made free of withholding or deduction for taxes of its jurisdiction.

nodes.title: Consolidation, merger and sale of assets
nodes.heading: Consolidation, merger and sale of assets
nodes.start_phrase: The indenture provides that for so long as any of the Notes of any series issued thereunder or Guarantees thereunder are outstanding, neither the Iss uer nor any applicable Guarantor may consolidate with or merge into any other Person that is not the Issuer or an applica ble Guarantor, or convey, transfer or lease all or substantially all of its properties and assets to any Person that is not the Issuer or an applicable Guarantor, unless:
nodes.summary:
- Permitted Liens: Specifies additional categories of allowed Liens, including (m) netting/set-off Liens in ordinary-course banking, (n) refinancings of permitted Liens subject to strict limits (no extension to new assets, no increase in secured principal, original discharge timelines preserved), (o) Liens arising from changes in lease accounting standards, and (p) a general basket for other Liens securing Indebtedness capped at 10% of Total Tangible Assets. Also references Liens over project-related equity interests tied to limited recourse debt at direct subsidiaries.
- Unsecured Debt: States there is no indenture cap on the amount of unsecured Indebtedness Amcor or its subsidiaries may incur.
- Consolidation, Merger, and Sale of Assets: Restricts mergers, consolidations, and transfers/leases of all or substantially all assets to non-Issuer/non-Guarantor entities unless the successor is a validly existing entity that assumes the Notes/Guarantees (including Additional Amounts), no Event of Default results, and specified conditions are met. If the successor is organized outside the U.S., D.C., Jersey, Australia, the U.K. (or their states/territories), it must indemnify holders for taxes/costs arising from the transaction and agree to gross-up payments (Successor Additional Amounts) similar to Additional Amounts. Notes that these provisions may not protect against highly leveraged transactions.
- Modification and Waiver: Identifies three categories of changes (only the unanimous-consent category is detailed here). Changes requiring each affected holder’s consent include: altering maturity, interest rate, or Additional Amounts; changing place or currency of payment; impairing the right to sue; reducing principal payable upon acceleration or any amounts due; lowering consent thresholds; adversely modifying modification/waiver provisions or Guarantor payment terms; waiving payment defaults (with limited exception tied to rescission of acceleration by majority holders); subordinating the Notes or Guarantees; or releasing a Guarantee other than as permitted by the indenture.

nodes.title: Modification and waiver
nodes.heading: Modification and waiver
nodes.start_phrase: There are three types of changes the Issuer can make to the indenture and the Notes.
nodes.summary:
- Explains that if a successor entity’s jurisdiction requires tax withholding on payments under the Notes or Guarantees, that entity must pay “Successor Additional Amounts” to gross up holders to the amount they would have received absent such withholding, subject to the same exceptions that apply to the Issuer/Guarantors’ Additional Amounts (with the successor’s jurisdiction substituted as the Relevant Jurisdiction).
- Notes that these tax gross-up provisions do not necessarily protect holders against risks from highly leveraged or other adverse transactions involving the Issuer or Guarantors.
- Introduces the “Modification and waiver” framework, stating there are three categories of changes to the indenture and the Notes.
- Details the category requiring unanimous holder approval, including any change that would:
  - Alter stated maturity, principal or interest (including the interest rate), premium, or the obligation to pay Additional Amounts.
  - Change the place or currency of payment.
  - Impair a holder’s ability to sue for payment.
  - Reduce principal payable upon acceleration after an Event of Default or reduce any amounts due.
  - Lower the consent thresholds for amendments, waivers of indenture provisions, or waivers of certain defaults.
  - Adversely modify provisions governing modification or waiver.
  - Adversely affect Guarantors’ payment obligations (including Additional Amounts).
  - Waive payment defaults (except rescission of acceleration by majority holders and related payment default waiver).
  - Subordinate the Notes or Guarantees to other obligations.
  - Release any Guarantee other than as permitted by the indenture.

nodes.title: Changes requiring unanimous approval
nodes.heading: Changes requiring unanimous approval
nodes.start_phrase: First, there are the following changes, which the Issuer cannot make to the Notes or the indenture without the specific consent of the holder o f each Note affected thereby:
nodes.summary:
- Tax gross-up and Successor Additional Amounts: If withholding or deduction of taxes is required by a new jurisdiction (e.g., after a merger or reorganization), the successor must pay “Successor Additional Amounts” so holders receive the same net amounts as if no withholding applied, subject to the same exceptions as the standard Additional Amounts provisions.
- Limited protection in change-of-control/leveraged transactions: The document notes that these provisions may not protect noteholders in highly leveraged or other transactions involving the issuer or guarantors.
- Modification and waiver framework: Three tiers of amendments to the indenture/Notes:
  - Changes requiring unanimous holder consent include: altering maturity, principal, interest rate, or Additional Amounts; changing payment currency/place; impairing the right to sue; reducing principal upon acceleration; reducing any amounts due; lowering consent thresholds; adversely modifying modification/waiver mechanics; adversely changing guarantor payment obligations (including Additional Amounts); waiving payment defaults (except rescission of acceleration by majority); subordinating Notes/Guarantees; improperly releasing guarantees; or changing any of these unanimity provisions.
  - Changes requiring majority consent: With holders of a majority in aggregate principal amount of affected Notes, broad amendments are permitted, except for the unanimity items and payment default waivers.
  - Changes not requiring consent: Clarifications and other limited amendments that do not materially adversely affect holders, as specified in the indenture.
- Voting/consent mechanics:
  - Voting principal is calculated as the amount due if the Notes were accelerated on the voting date.
  - Notes are not “outstanding” (and cannot vote) if cash has been set aside for payment/redemption or if canceled.
  - Record dates may be set by the issuer (or in limited cases by the trustee); only holders as of the record date may act, and actions must occur within 180 days (adjustable by the issuer/trustee within that limit).
- Satisfaction and discharge of the indenture:
  - The indenture is discharged when either (a) all issued securities (other than replaced/lost) are delivered for cancellation; or (b) undelivered securities are due/within one year of maturity or redemption and the issuer irrevocably deposits sufficient US dollars and/or non-callable U.S. Government Obligations with the trustee to pay principal, premium, and interest in full to maturity/redemption, without assuming reinvestment.
  - No default/Event of Default may be continuing or created by the deposit, and the deposit must not breach other agreements binding the issuer.

nodes.title: Changes requiring majority approval
nodes.heading: Changes requiring majority approval
nodes.start_phrase:
With the consent of the holders of not less than a majority in aggrega te principal amount of the outstanding the Notes affected thereby, the Iss uer and the Trustee may modify the indenture or the
Notes for the purpose of adding any provisions to or changing in any ma nner or eliminating any of the provisions of the indenture or of modifying in any manner the rights of the holders of such
Notes; provided that the Issuer cannot obtain a waiver of a payment default or any change in respect of the indenture or the Notes listed under "— Changes requiring unanimous approval" without the
nodes.summary:
- Amendment categories
  - Unanimous approval: Certain fundamental changes require consent of each holder, including any change to provisions that themselves require holder consent and any waiver of a payment default.
  - Majority approval: With consent of holders of a majority in aggregate principal amount of the outstanding Notes affected, the issuer and trustee may add, change, eliminate provisions of the indenture or modify holders’ rights, except for matters in the unanimous-approval category.
  - No approval: Clarifications and specified technical or other changes that do not materially adversely affect holders.

- Voting/consent mechanics
  - Voting amount is the principal that would be due on the voting date if the Notes were accelerated due to an Event of Default.
  - Notes are not “outstanding” (and cannot vote) if cash has been deposited or set aside in trust for their payment/redemption, or if they’ve been cancelled or delivered for cancellation.
  - Record dates: The issuer (and in limited cases the trustee) may set a record date to determine eligible holders. Only holders on that date may act, and the action must occur within 180 days (a period the setter may shorten or lengthen, but not beyond 180 days).

- Satisfaction and discharge of the indenture
  - The indenture terminates for all securities issued under it when either:
    - All such securities (with limited exceptions for replaced lost/stolen/destroyed or previously trust-paid/discharged series) are delivered to the trustee for cancellation; or
    - All undelivered securities have become due and payable, will become due within one year, or are called for redemption within one year, and the issuer has irrevocably deposited in trust cash in U.S. dollars, non-callable U.S. Government Obligations, or both, sufficient (without assuming reinvestment) to pay principal, any premium, and accrued interest to maturity or redemption.
  - Additional conditions: No default or Event of Default is continuing or will occur as a result of the deposit, and the deposit does not breach or default any other instrument binding the issuer.

nodes.title: Changes not requiring approval
nodes.heading: Changes not requiring approval
nodes.start_phrase: The third type of change does not require any vote or consent by holders of the Notes.
nodes.summary:
- Amendment thresholds:
  - Unanimous approval required to change provisions that themselves require holder consent.
  - Majority approval (at least a majority in aggregate principal of affected outstanding Notes) allows adding, changing, or eliminating indenture/Note provisions or modifying holder rights, but cannot waive a payment default or make any change listed as requiring unanimous approval without each affected holder’s consent.
  - No holder approval needed for clarifications and other specified changes that do not materially and adversely affect holders.

- Voting/consent mechanics:
  - Voting principal calculated as the amount that would be due if the Notes were accelerated on the voting date due to an Event of Default.
  - Notes are not “outstanding” (and cannot vote) if funds have been deposited or set aside in trust for their payment/redemption, or if they have been cancelled or delivered for cancellation.
  - The Issuer may set record dates for holder actions; the Trustee may do so in limited cases. Only holders of record on that date may act, and actions must occur within 180 days (or a shorter period set by the Issuer/Trustee, but not beyond 180 days).

- Satisfaction and discharge of the indenture:
  - The indenture is discharged for all debt securities when either:
    - All securities (except replaced or paid lost/stolen/destroyed ones and any previously discharged from trust) are delivered to the Trustee for cancellation; or
    - Undelivered securities are (i) due and payable, (ii) will mature within one year, or (iii) are to be redeemed within one year, and the Issuer irrevocably deposits with the Trustee cash in U.S. dollars, non-callable U.S. Government Obligations, or a combination, sufficient (without reinvestment) to pay principal, any premium, and accrued interest to maturity or redemption.
  - No default or Event of Default may be continuing on the deposit date or result from the deposit, and the deposit must not breach other instruments binding the Issuer.

nodes.title: Further details concerning voting / consenting
nodes.heading: Further details concerning voting / consenting
nodes.start_phrase:
When taking a vote or obtaining a consent, the Issuer will use the princ ipal amount that would be due and payable on the voting date, if the mat urity of the corresponding Notes were accelerated to
that date because of an Event of Default.
nodes.summary:
- Outlines amendment mechanics for an indenture and Notes, divided into three categories:
  - Changes requiring unanimous approval by each affected holder (referenced but not itemized here), which cannot be altered or waived without every holder’s consent, including waivers of payment defaults.
  - Changes requiring majority approval, allowing the issuer and trustee to add, change, eliminate indenture or Note provisions or modify holder rights with consent of holders of a majority in aggregate principal amount of the affected Notes, except for matters reserved for unanimous approval.
  - Changes not requiring approval, limited to clarifications and specified immaterial changes that do not materially adversely affect holders.

- Describes voting/consent mechanics:
  - Voting principal equals the amount that would be due if the Notes were accelerated on the voting date due to an Event of Default.
  - Notes are not “outstanding” (and cannot vote) if funds for payment/redemption have been set aside in trust, or if Notes have been cancelled or delivered for cancellation.
  - The issuer may set a record date (and in limited cases the trustee may do so) to determine eligible holders; only holders of record on that date may act, and action must occur within 180 days of the record date (a period the issuer may adjust, but not beyond 180 days).

- Sets out satisfaction and discharge of the indenture:
  - The indenture is discharged for all debt securities when either (a) all have been delivered to the trustee for cancellation (with customary treatment for lost, stolen, or destroyed securities and those previously paid/discharged), or (b) all undelivered securities are due and payable (by notice of redemption or otherwise), will mature within one year, or are to be redeemed within one year, and the issuer irrevocably deposits with the trustee, in trust solely for holders, cash in U.S. dollars, non-callable U.S. Government Obligations, or a combination, sufficient (without assuming reinvestment) to pay principal, any premium, and accrued interest to maturity or redemption.
  - No default or Event of Default may have occurred and be continuing on the deposit date or result from the deposit, and the deposit must not breach other instruments binding the issuer.

nodes.title: Satisfaction and discharge
nodes.heading: Satisfaction and discharge
nodes.start_phrase: The indenture will be discharged and will cease to be of further e ffect as to all debt securities issued thereunder, when:
nodes.summary:
- Amendment and waiver framework:
  - Certain fundamental changes require unanimous holder consent (reference made to “Changes requiring unanimous approval”; one example bullet is shown).
  - Majority amendments: with consent of holders of a majority in aggregate principal amount of the affected Notes, the issuer and trustee may add, change, or eliminate indenture/Note provisions; however, waivers of payment defaults and matters listed under unanimous approval still require each holder’s consent.
  - No-consent changes: clarifications and other specified amendments that do not materially adversely affect holders.

- Voting/consent mechanics:
  - Voting amount is the principal that would be due if the Notes were accelerated on the voting date.
  - Notes are not “outstanding” (and cannot vote) if money for their payment/redemption has been set aside, or if cancelled or delivered for cancellation.
  - Issuer generally may set a record date; in limited cases the trustee may do so. Actions are limited to holders of record on that date and must occur within 180 days (period can be shortened/lengthened up to 180 days).

- Satisfaction and discharge of the indenture:
  - The indenture terminates when either (a) all securities are delivered for cancellation, or (b) undelivered securities are due/within one year of maturity or redemption and the issuer irrevocably deposits sufficient cash and/or non-callable U.S. Government Obligations to pay principal, premium, and interest in full.
  - Conditions: no default results from the deposit; no breach of other instruments; all sums under the indenture (including amounts due to the trustee) are paid; irrevocable payment instructions delivered.
  - Requires officers’ certificate and opinion of counsel confirming conditions satisfied.

- Defeasance and covenant defeasance:
  - Legal defeasance: issuer/guarantors are discharged from Note obligations (except certain administrative and trustee payment duties) upon depositing sufficient funds/U.S. Government Obligations and delivering a tax ruling/opinion that holders will not recognize gain or loss for U.S. federal income tax purposes and tax treatment remains unchanged.
  - Covenant defeasance: issuer/guarantors may cease complying with specified restrictive covenants (including limitation on liens and consolidation/merger/sale of assets) upon similar deposit and delivery of a comparable tax opinion.

- Guarantees:
  - Each guarantor unconditionally guarantees due and punctual payment of principal, interest, premium, and other amounts under the Notes/indenture, irrespective of enforceability of the Notes.
  - Guarantees remain until all obligations are satisfied; holders may proceed directly against a guarantor upon an event of default without first proceeding against the issuer.

- Fraudulent conveyance/transfer (England and Wales):
  - Notes that, under English insolvency law, an administrator or liquidator may seek court orders affecting transactions; the discussion is truncated.

nodes.title: Defeasance and covenant defeasance
nodes.heading: Defeasance and covenant defeasance
nodes.start_phrase: The indenture provides that the Issuer and the Guarantors, at the Issuer’s or the applicable Guarantor(s)'s option with respect to the Notes and t he Guarantees:
nodes.summary:
- Conditions for satisfaction and discharge of the indenture: the issuer must pay all amounts due under the indenture, deliver irrevocable instructions to the trustee to apply deposited funds to pay the debt at maturity or redemption, and provide an officer’s certificate and a trustee-acceptable legal opinion confirming all conditions precedent are met.
- Defeasance options: the issuer and guarantors may achieve (1) legal defeasance (discharge from most obligations, with specified obligations surviving such as transfer/exchange, replacement of notes, maintaining paying agents, holding funds in trust, and paying trustee amounts) or (2) covenant defeasance (cessation of compliance with certain restrictive covenants, including limitations on liens and on consolidation, merger, and asset sales).
- Funding requirement for defeasance: deposit with the trustee cash and/or U.S. Government Obligations (or a combination) sufficient to pay principal, premium, interest, and any then-known Additional Amounts on the due dates, with government obligations providing funds not later than one day before each payment date.
- Tax opinions required: for legal defeasance, an IRS ruling or a change in U.S. federal income tax law must support that holders will not recognize gain or loss and will have unchanged tax treatment; for covenant defeasance, a legal opinion must confirm no gain or loss recognition and unchanged tax treatment.
- Guarantees: each guarantor unconditionally guarantees due and punctual payment of all amounts on the notes and under the indenture, regardless of the enforceability of the notes, and remains liable until all obligations are satisfied; holders may proceed directly against a guarantor upon an event of default without first proceeding against the issuer.
- Fraudulent conveyance/transfer considerations (England and Wales): introduces English insolvency law risks, noting that in administration or liquidation an administrator or liquidator may apply to the court for orders affecting transactions, with implications for the enforceability or recovery related to the guarantees and obligations.

nodes.title: Guarantees
nodes.heading: Guarantees
nodes.start_phrase:
Under each Guarantee, each Guarantor unconditionally guaranteed the due and punctual payment of the principal, interest (if any), premium (if a ny) and all other amounts due on the Notes and under
the applicable indenture when the same shall become due and payable , whether at maturity, pursuant to mandatory or optional redemption or rep ayments, by acceleration or otherwise, in each case
after any applicable grace periods or notice requirements, according to t he terms of the Notes.
nodes.summary:
- Sets out conditions for “satisfaction and discharge” of the indenture: the issuer must pay all amounts due under the indenture (including trustee amounts), deliver irrevocable instructions to the trustee to apply deposited funds to pay the notes at maturity or redemption, and provide an officer’s certificate and an acceptable legal opinion confirming all conditions precedent are met.
- Describes defeasance and covenant defeasance options:
  - Full discharge of issuer/guarantor obligations on the notes, except for limited administrative obligations (e.g., transfer/exchange, note replacement with indemnity, trustee payments, maintaining paying agents, and holding funds in trust).
  - Alternatively, termination of compliance with certain restrictive covenants (including limitations on liens and on consolidation, merger, and sale of assets).
  - Preconditions: deposit with the trustee of cash and/or U.S. Government Obligations sufficient to pay principal, premium, interest, and any known Additional Amounts on due dates (funds available at least one day before each payment).
  - Tax opinions required: for full discharge, an IRS ruling or change in U.S. federal income tax law confirming no gain/loss recognition and unchanged tax treatment for holders; for covenant defeasance, a legal opinion confirming no gain/loss recognition and unchanged tax treatment.
- Details of Guarantees:
  - Each guarantor unconditionally guarantees due and punctual payment of principal, interest, premium, and other amounts under the notes and indenture, whether at maturity, redemption/repayment, acceleration, or otherwise (subject to any grace/notice periods).
  - Guarantor obligations are unconditional and continue until all obligations under the notes and indenture are satisfied, regardless of the notes’ enforceability.
  - Noteholders may proceed directly against a guarantor upon an event of default without first proceeding against the issuer.
- Introduces fraudulent conveyance/transfer considerations under England and Wales: upon administration or liquidation, administrators or liquidators have powers to seek court orders (section truncated), signaling potential challenges to transactions under English insolvency law.

nodes.title: Fraudulent conveyance or transfer considerations
nodes.heading: Fraudulent conveyance or transfer considerations
nodes.start_phrase:
Under English insolvency law, if a company enters administration or goes into liquidation, then the administrator or liquidator, as appli cable, has certain powers to, among other things, apply to the
court for such order as the court sees fit
nodes.summary:
- Satisfaction and discharge of the indenture: requires the issuer to pay all sums due under the indenture (including amounts owed to the trustee), give irrevocable instructions to the trustee to apply deposited funds to pay the relevant series at maturity or redemption, and deliver an officers’ certificate and a counsel opinion confirming all conditions precedent are met.
- Defeasance and covenant defeasance: the issuer/guarantors may either (1) be deemed discharged from obligations on the Notes except for limited ongoing duties (registration/transfer, replacement of Notes, trustee payments, maintaining paying agents, and holding funds in trust), or (2) cease complying with certain restrictive covenants (including limitation on liens and consolidation/merger/sale of assets), if they deposit with the trustee cash, U.S. Government Obligations, or a combination sufficient to pay principal, premium, interest, and known Additional Amounts when due.
- Tax opinions for defeasance: for full defeasance (clause 1), a counsel opinion based on an IRS ruling or a change in U.S. federal income tax law must confirm holders will not recognize gain or loss and will have the same tax treatment as if defeasance had not occurred; for covenant defeasance (clause 2), a counsel opinion must confirm the same tax result.
- Guarantees: each Guarantor unconditionally guarantees due and punctual payment of principal, interest, premium, and all other amounts under the Notes and indenture; obligations are unconditional and continue until all such obligations are satisfied; holders may proceed directly against a Guarantor upon an event of default without first proceeding against the issuer.
- Fraudulent conveyance/transfer considerations (England and Wales): on administration or liquidation, an administrator or liquidator may apply to court for appropriate orders; section appears to address potential vulnerabilities of transactions/guarantees in insolvency (text truncated).

nodes.title: England and wales
nodes.heading: England and wales
nodes.start_phrase:
Under English insolvency law, if a company enters administration or goes into liquidation, then the administrator or liquidator, as appli cable, has certain powers to, among other things, apply to the
court for such order as the court sees fit
nodes.summary:
- Conditions for satisfaction and discharge of the indenture: issuer must pay all sums due, give irrevocable payment instructions to the trustee for maturity/redemption, and deliver an officers’ certificate and acceptable legal opinion confirming all conditions precedent are met.
- Defeasance and covenant defeasance options: issuer/guarantors can either (1) be deemed discharged from most obligations on the Notes (with certain administrative and trustee-payment obligations surviving) or (2) cease complying with specified restrictive covenants (e.g., limitation on liens; consolidation, merger, sale of assets), if they deposit sufficient cash and/or U.S. Government Obligations to cover all scheduled payments. Tax opinions are required to confirm no U.S. federal income tax gain/loss to holders under either option.
- Guarantees: each guarantor unconditionally guarantees timely payment of principal, interest, premium, and other amounts under the Notes/indenture; obligations remain until all are satisfied; holders may proceed directly against a guarantor upon an event of default without first pursuing the issuer.
- Fraudulent conveyance/transfer considerations:
  - England and Wales: transactions at undervalue (within two years pre-insolvency) and preferences (within six months, or two years for connected persons) may be set aside if insolvency tests and intent/desire elements are met; separate remedy for transactions defrauding creditors with no specific statutory look-back (subject to limitation), and potential good-faith/business-purpose defense.
  - Australia: a guarantee may be unenforceable if the guarantor was insolvent or rendered insolvent when given and, if winding up begins within four years, the guarantee is found to be an “uncommercial transaction” considering benefits/detriments and other relevant factors.
  - United States: a guarantee may be avoided or subordinated if incurred with actual intent to hinder/delay/defraud, for less than reasonably equivalent value, or when the guarantor was insolvent, undercapitalized, or intended/believed it would incur debts beyond its ability to pay.

nodes.title: Australia
nodes.heading: Australia
nodes.start_phrase:
Under Australian insolvency laws, a guarantee may not be enforceable a gainst a guarantor if a court were to find, in an insolvency or liquidation proc eeding, (a) that the guarantor was insolvent
(unable to pay its debts as they become due) at the time it prov ided its guarantee
nodes.summary:
- Focus: Legal risks and clawback/avoidance actions affecting transactions and guarantees under insolvency/fraudulent transfer regimes in the UK, Australia, and the United States, including when courts can unwind transactions and the standards applied.

- United Kingdom (Insolvency Act 1986):
  - Transactions at an “undervalue” within two years pre-insolvency can be set aside to restore the pre-transaction position. “Undervalue” includes gifts, no consideration, or consideration significantly below what the company gave.
  - Good-faith/business-purpose defense: courts generally won’t intervene if done in good faith for carrying on business with reasonable belief of benefit.
  - Preferences within six months pre-insolvency (two years for connected persons) can be unwound if they improve a creditor/surety/guarantor’s position on insolvency.
  - Orders require insolvency at the time or caused by the transaction; for preferences, a “desire to prefer” is required (presumed for connected persons).
  - Transactions defrauding creditors (putting assets beyond reach or prejudicing claimants) can be set aside without requiring company insolvency or formal process; victims (with leave) and officeholders can sue; no special statutory time limit beyond general limitation periods.

- Australia:
  - A guarantee may be unenforceable if, in a winding-up begun within four years of its issuance, the guarantor was insolvent when given or rendered insolvent by it, and the guarantee is an “uncommercial transaction.”
  - Uncommercial transaction test: whether a reasonable person in the guarantor’s circumstances would have issued the guarantee, considering benefits to the guarantor, detriment to the guarantor, benefits to other parties, and any other relevant factors.

- United States:
  - Under bankruptcy and state fraudulent transfer laws, a guarantee can be avoided or subordinated if, at incurrence, the guarantor:
    - intended to hinder, delay, or defraud creditors, or received less than reasonably equivalent value/fair consideration;
    - was insolvent or rendered insolvent;
    - had unreasonably small capital for its business; or
    - intended or believed it would incur debts beyond its ability to pay as they matured.

nodes.title: United States
nodes.heading: United States
nodes.start_phrase:
Under United States bankruptcy law and comparable provisions of sta te fraudulent transfer laws, a guarantee can be voided, or claims under a guarantee may be subordinated to all other debts of that
guarantor if, among other things, the guarantor, at the time it incurred the ind ebtedness evidenced by its guarantee:
nodes.summary:
- Focus on insolvency and fraudulent transfer/avoidance rules affecting guarantees and related transactions across multiple jurisdictions (UK, Australia, US, Jersey).
- United Kingdom:
  - Courts can unwind transactions at an undervalue entered within two years before insolvency onset, subject to a good-faith/business-purpose defense.
  - Preferences can be set aside if given within six months (two years for connected persons), requiring insolvency and a “desire to prefer” (presumed for connected persons).
  - Separate regime for transactions defrauding creditors (putting assets beyond reach), with broad remedies, potential claims by “victims,” no insolvency prerequisite, and no special statutory time limit beyond general limitation periods.
- Australia:
  - Guarantees may be unenforceable if the guarantor was insolvent when given or rendered insolvent by giving them, and if within a four-year look-back they are deemed “uncommercial transactions” under the Corporations Act 2001, assessed by a reasonable person test considering benefits/detriments and other relevant factors.
- United States:
  - Guarantees can be avoided or subordinated under bankruptcy and state fraudulent transfer laws if incurred with actual intent to hinder/delay/defraud, for less than reasonably equivalent value, when insolvent or rendered insolvent, with unreasonably small capital, or with debts beyond the ability to pay; payments under guarantees may be clawed back.
  - Insolvency measures include balance-sheet insolvency, cash-flow insolvency, and capital adequacy tests.
- Jersey:
  - Courts can set aside guarantees as transactions at an undervalue (five-year look-back) or as preferences (12-month look-back) under the Bankruptcy (Désastre) (Jersey) Law 1990 and the Companies Law.
  - Requirements include insolvency and, for preferences, a desire to prefer; presumptions apply for connected persons, with burden shifting.
  - Broad restorative powers and recognition of customary law (e.g., Pauline action) to set aside dispositions intended to defeat creditors.
- Definitions provided for “Accounts” (consolidated financial statements under U.S. GAAP) and “Australian Act” (Corporations Act 2001).

nodes.title: Jersey
nodes.heading: Jersey
nodes.start_phrase:
Under Article 17 of the Bankruptcy (Désastre) (Jersey) Law 1990, as amended (the "Jersey Bankruptcy Law") and Article 176 of the Jersey Companies Law, the court may, on the application of the
Viscount of Jersey (in the case of a company whose property has been dec lared "en désastre") or liquidator (in the case of a creditors' winding up , a procedure which is instigated by shareholders not
creditors), set aside a guarantee entered into by a company with any pers on at an undervalue.
nodes.summary:
- Highlights the risk that payments under a guarantee may be voided and clawed back under fraudulent transfer/insolvency laws, with insolvency commonly assessed by balance-sheet insolvency, inadequate asset value to cover debts as they mature, or inability to pay debts when due.
- Sets out Jersey law mechanisms to unwind guarantees:
  - Transactions at an undervalue (Articles 17 Bankruptcy (Désastre) (Jersey) Law 1990 and 176 Jersey Companies Law): 5‑year look‑back from winding up or désastre; applications by the Viscount or a liquidator; court can restore the pre‑transaction position; applicant must prove insolvency unless the beneficiary is a connected person, in which case insolvency is presumed and must be rebutted by the connected person.
  - Preferences, including guarantees (Articles 17A and 176A): 12‑month look‑back; a preference is one that improves a creditor’s or surety’s position in an insolvent winding up; broad court powers to unwind; requires showing the company was influenced by a desire to prefer, with a presumption of such desire where the beneficiary is connected (rebuttable by that party). Applicant must also show insolvency at the relevant time.
- Notes additional Jersey customary law (e.g., Pauline action) allowing transactions intended to defeat creditors to be set aside.
- Includes defined terms:
  - “Accounts”: the Group’s consolidated financial statements prepared under U.S. GAAP, with accompanying reports/notes.
  - “Australian Act”: the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) of Australia.

nodes.summary:
- Addresses the risk that payments made by a guarantor under a guarantee may be voided and clawed back under fraudulent transfer/insolvency laws, with general insolvency tests outlined (balance sheet insolvency, insufficient asset value to cover debts as they mature, and inability to pay debts when due).
- Details Jersey law remedies to set aside guarantees:
  - Transactions at an undervalue (Article 17 Jersey Bankruptcy Law; Article 176 Jersey Companies Law): 5-year lookback; court powers to restore the pre-transaction position; insolvency must be shown by the Viscount or liquidator unless the beneficiary is a connected person, in which case insolvency is presumed and the connected person must rebut.
  - Preferences (Article 17A Jersey Bankruptcy Law; Article 176A Jersey Companies Law): 12-month lookback; a guarantee is a preference if it improves a creditor/surety/guarantor’s position in an insolvent winding up; court may restore the prior position if the company was influenced by a desire to prefer; burden on Viscount/liquidator to prove insolvency and desire to prefer unless a connected person benefits, in which case desire to prefer is presumed and must be rebutted.
  - Notes that Jersey customary law (e.g., Pauline action) also allows setting aside dispositions intended to defeat creditors.
- Provides an extensive “Certain definitions” section for an Amcor-related indenture/notes framework, including:
  - Financial/reporting and timing terms: Accounts, Business Day (NYC, London, TARGET2), U.S. GAAP, Finance Lease.
  - Corporate control and rating-related triggers: Change in Lease Accounting Standard, Change of Control (asset sale, >50% beneficial ownership, merger outcomes, board change, liquidation plan), Change of Control Trigger Period, and Change of Control Triggering Event (ratings-based downgrades below Investment Grade by engaged Rating Agencies; deemed occurrence if insufficient agencies rate the notes).
  - Governance/person definitions: Continuing Director, Person, Subsidiary (control and partnership thresholds), Voting Stock.
  - Credit and security terms: Default, Indebtedness (comprehensive list including guarantees, secured debt, derivatives, finance leases, letters of credit, deferred purchase price, factoring, instruments), Investment Grade, Lien, Specified Indebtedness.
  - Project finance concepts: Limited Recourse Indebtedness, Project, Project Assets (including ring-fenced equity), and limitations on creditor recourse.
  - Ratings and agencies: Moody’s, S&P, Fitch, Rating Agency, Substitute Rating Agency.
  - Other: Group, Hedge Agreement (excluding employee equity plans), Total Tangible Assets (net of Project Assets subject to Limited Recourse Indebtedness, plus certain equity proceeds), U.S. Government Obligations, Australian Act.
- Mentions Exhibit 10.8: Amcor Rigid Plastics Deferred Compensation Plan (as amended and restated effective January 1, 2013).

nodes.summary:

- History and compliance: Originally established September 5, 2000; multiple corporate name changes; amended in 2005 to comply with Internal Revenue Code Section 409A with pre-2005 amounts grandfathered; further restated in 2013.
- Purpose: Provide deferred compensation opportunities to eligible key employees.
- Key structural elements outlined in the Table of Contents:
  - Definitions of core terms (Accounts, Affiliates, Beneficiaries, various contribution types, Grandfathered vs. 409A Accounts, Investment Funds, Plans, Trust/Trustee).
  - Eligibility and participation criteria.
  - Contributions:
    - Employee: Salary Deferral and Bonus deferrals; Long-Term Incentive Plan contributions.
    - Employer: Make-Up Matching, Make-Up Pension, Special Contributions, and 10% Target Contributions; coordination with company savings and pension plans.
  - Accounting and vesting: Vesting schedules, treatment upon termination for cause or non-compete violations, forfeiture rules, allocation methods, and account maintenance.
  - Funding and investments: Use of a trust (likely a rabbi trust), investment fund elections by participants, and expense handling.
  - Timing and form of payment: Distribution rules for Grandfathered vs. 409A Accounts, payment events (separation, death, disability), hardship distributions, beneficiary designations, and procedures for unclaimed benefits.
  - Nature of participant interest: Benefits are unsecured obligations of the employer (typical of unfunded nonqualified plans).
  - Administration: Committee structure and authority (Administrative and Investment Committees), tax withholding, claims and disability claims procedures, limitation of liability, finality of decisions, and governing law.
  - Employment rights disclaimer: Participation does not create employment rights.
  - Change in control: Special provisions for treatment of Grandfathered and 409A Accounts upon a change in control.
  - Amendment, suspension, and termination: Employer’s rights to modify or end the plan.

nodes.title: Eligibility and Participation
nodes.heading: SECTION 3 Eligibility and Participation
nodes.start_phrase: Each Plan Year, the Committee will determin e those Employees who are Eligible Employees.
nodes.summary:
- Eligibility (Section 3.1):
  - Determined each Plan Year by the Committee.
  - Eligible Employee generally is key management whose annualized base pay plus bonus is expected to exceed Code Section 414(q) limits ($105,000, indexed).
  - Employees may be designated for different contribution types: Employee Contributions, Employer Make-Up Matching, Employer Make-Up Pension, Employer Special, and/or Employer 10% Target Contributions.

- Participation (Section 3.2):
  - For Employee Contributions, participation starts on the later of designation as Eligible or the employee’s election to contribute.
  - For Employer contributions, participation starts upon designation as Eligible.
  - Eligibility/contribution levels in one Plan Year do not guarantee eligibility/levels in other years.
  - Committee may suspend or terminate participation at any time; existing Account balances are not reduced except as provided in Sections 5.1 and 5.2.
  - Participation ends when employment with all Employers/Affiliates terminates and the vested Account balance is distributed to the Participant or Beneficiaries.

- Contributions (Section 4):
  - Long-Term Incentive Plan (LTIP) Contributions (4.1):
    - Before January 1, 2005, Eligible Employees could defer LTIP awards into the Plan.
    - Stock appreciation rights tied to a change in control could be deferred by September 30, 2000.
    - These deferrals are part of the Participant’s Grandfathered Account.
  - Salary Deferral Contributions (4.2):
    - Allowed at 1%–50% of Compensation.
    - New eligibles: 30-day election window; effective prospectively as soon as administratively feasible.
    - Others: elect by December 15 prior to the Plan Year; effective January 1; elections are irrevocable for the Plan Year.
    - If a Participant takes a hardship distribution from the Savings Plan: the election is cancelled for the rest of that calendar year, deferrals are suspended for six months, and may resume the following January 1.
  - Bonus Contributions (4.3):
    - Allowed at 1%–100% of bonus paid from an Employer’s U.S. payroll.
    - New eligibles: 30-day election window; effective prospectively as soon as administratively feasible.
    - Others: elect by December 15; effective for bonuses earned in any Employer fiscal year ending after that date, provided the election is made at least six months before the end of the related service period.
