nodes.title: Bonus Contributions
nodes.heading: 4.3 Bonus Contributions
nodes.start_phrase: Th e Plan permits Bonus Contributions of between 1% and 100% of an Eligible Employee’s bonus paid from an Employer’s U.S. payroll.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: This partial document is Section 4 (Contributions) of a nonqualified deferred compensation plan. It details types of employee deferrals and discretionary employer “make-up” contributions, eligibility, timing, and special conditions.

- 4.1 Long-Term Incentive Plan (LTIP) Contributions:
  - Before January 1, 2005, eligible employees could defer LTIP awards and certain stock appreciation rights (SARs) payments (e.g., upon a change in control).
  - These LTIP/SAR deferrals are held in a Participant’s Grandfathered Account.

- 4.2 Salary Deferral Contributions:
  - Employees may defer 1%–50% of Compensation.
  - Newly eligible employees: may elect within 30 days; effective prospectively as soon as administratively feasible.
  - All others: must elect by December 15 before the Plan Year; effective the following January 1.
  - Elections apply for one Plan Year and are irrevocable for that year.
  - Hardship distribution from the Savings Plan cancels the current election for the rest of that calendar year; deferrals are suspended for six months and may resume the January 1 after the suspension.

- 4.3 Bonus Contributions:
  - Employees may defer 1%–100% of bonuses paid from an Employer’s U.S. payroll.
  - Newly eligible employees: may elect within 30 days; effective prospectively as soon as administratively feasible.
  - All others: must elect by December 15; effective for bonuses earned in any Employer fiscal year ending after that date, provided the election is at least six months before the end of the related service period.
  - Employees may defer awards under the Amcor PET Packaging Management Incentive Plan; elections are irrevocable.
  - For performance-based bonuses tied to service periods of 12 months or more, elections (effective January 1, 2005) must be made no later than six months before the end of the performance period.

- 4.4 Employer Make-Up Matching Contributions:
  - Effective January 1, 2005, the Employer may, at its discretion, contribute amounts to replace Savings Plan matching contributions not received due to:
    - Code §401(a)(17) compensation limits,
    - Code §415 contribution limits, and
    - This Plan’s deferrals not counting as Savings Plan compensation.
  - Eligibility requires the employee to contribute the maximum permitted to the Savings Plan.

- 4.5 Employer Make-Up Pension Contributions:
  - Effective January 1, 2005 and prior to January 1, 2012, the Employer may, at its discretion, contribute amounts to approximate Pension Plan benefits not earned due to:
    - Code §401(a)(17) compensation limits,
    - Code §415 limits, and
    - This Plan’s deferrals not counting as pensionable compensation.
  - Employer may choose to contribute for some/all participants, or less than the full make-up.
  - Calculation assumptions include:
    - Termination and commencement at the later of age 60 or attainment of five years of service, with early commencement reductions unless age 65 with five years.
    - Termination after age 55 with five years but before age 60 yields a reduced make-up amount.
  - Section ends mid-sentence, indicating additional rules may follow.

nodes.title: Employer Make-Up Matching Contributions
nodes.heading: 4.4 Employer Make-Up Matching Contributions
nodes.start_phrase: Effective as of January 1, 2005, the Employer may, in its sole discretion, make a contribution each Plan Year to Eligible Employees in the amount necessary to provide suc h Participants with the employer matching contributions they will not receive under the Savings Plan due to: (i) the limitation of Section 401(a)(17) of the Code, (ii) the limitations of Section 415 of the Code, and (iii) the fact that a Participant’s Employee Contributions into this Plan are not included as compensation for purposes of determining contributions under the Savings Plan (“Emplo yer Make-Up Matching Contributions”).
nodes.summary:
- Bonus/incentive deferrals: Eligible Employees may elect to defer all or part of a bonus, incentive pay, or award under the Amcor PET Packaging Management Incentive Plan, following Committee-prescribed procedures; elections are irrevocable once made.
- Timing for performance-based bonus deferrals: For bonuses tied to services over 12+ months, deferral elections effective January 1, 2005 must be made at least six months before the end of the performance period.
- Employer Make-Up Matching Contributions (effective 1/1/2005): At the Employer’s discretion each Plan Year, contributions may be made to replace Savings Plan matching amounts not received due to (i) Code §401(a)(17) compensation limits, (ii) Code §415 limits, and (iii) exclusion of this Plan’s deferrals from “compensation” for Savings Plan purposes. To receive these, an Eligible Employee must contribute the maximum permitted to the Savings Plan.
- Employer Make-Up Pension Contributions (effective 1/1/2005 and prior to 1/1/2012): At the Employer’s discretion each Plan Year, contributions may be made to approximate Pension Plan benefits not accrued due to (i) Code §401(a)(17), (ii) Code §415, and (iii) exclusion of this Plan’s deferrals from “compensation” for Pension Plan accruals. The Employer may choose not to make, or to make less than full, contributions for some or all Participants in any year.
- Assumptions for calculating Make-Up Pension Contributions: 
  - Assume termination and Pension Plan benefit commencement at the later of age 60 or attainment of 5 years of service.
  - Benefits are assumed reduced for early commencement unless the Participant has reached age 65 with at least 5 years of service.
  - Termination after age 55 with 5 years of service but before age 60 results in a smaller make-up contribution.
- The excerpt ends mid-sentence, indicating further rules may follow regarding continued employment and contribution calculations.

nodes.title: Employer Make-Up Pension Contributions
nodes.heading: 4.5 Employer Make-Up Pension Contributions
nodes.start_phrase: Effectiv e as of January 1, 2005 and prior to January 1, 2012, the Employer may, in its sole discretion, mak e a contribution each Plan Year to Eligible Employees in the amount necessary to provide such Participants with the approximate benefits they will not receive under the Pension Plan due to: (i) the limitations of Section 401(a)(17) of the Code, (ii) the limitations of Section 415 of the Code, and (iii) the fact that a Participant’s Employee Contributions into this Plan are not included as compensationfor purposes of benefit accruals under the Pension Plan (“Employer Make-Up Pension Contribut ions”).
nodes.summary:
- Bonus/incentive deferral elections: Eligible Employees may elect to defer all or part of awards under the Amcor PET Packaging Management Incentive Plan; elections are irrevocable once made and, for performance-based bonuses tied to service periods of 12+ months, must be made no later than six months before the end of that period (effective January 1, 2005).
- Employer Make-Up Matching Contributions (effective January 1, 2005): At the Employer’s discretion, contributions may be made to replace Savings Plan employer matching not received due to Code §§401(a)(17) and 415 limits and because deferrals to this plan aren’t treated as compensation for the Savings Plan. Eligibility requires the employee to contribute the maximum allowable to the Savings Plan.
- Employer Make-Up Pension Contributions (effective January 1, 2005 and prior to January 1, 2012): Discretionary contributions to approximate Pension Plan benefits not received due to Code §§401(a)(17), 415 limits, and non-inclusion of this plan’s deferrals in pension compensation. The Employer may fund none, some, or less than the full amount.
  - Calculation assumptions: termination assumed at later of age 60 or 5 years of service; early commencement reductions unless age 65 with 5 years; leaving after 55 with 5 years but before 60 reduces make-up; continued eligibility past age 60 if still employed.
  - Actuarial basis: Compensation, GAM 94 mortality, assumed compensation growth of inflation + 1.5% (assumptions may be changed by the Committee).
  - Hypothetical earnings on prior make-up pension contributions: 10-year U.S. Treasury average + 2% as of January 1, 2005 (actual investment allocation per participant choices under Section 6.2).
  - Funding: fully funded at later of age 60 or completion of 5 years of service; procedures for continued funding after age 60 set by the Committee.
- Employer Special Contributions: The Employer may make additional discretionary contributions in any Plan Year in amounts determined by the Committee.
- Employer 10% Target Contributions (effective January 1, 2008): Discretionary supplemental retirement contribution equal to 10% of Compensation for the Plan Year, reduced by: (a) Savings Plan Retirement Savings Contributions, (b) Savings Plan New Employer Matching Contributions, (c) Savings Plan Employer Discretionary Matching Contributions, and (d) the Employer portion of OASDI Social Security tax on the employee’s Compensation (paid/accrued or deemed paid/accrued for the same year).
- Governance/discretion: The Committee prescribes election procedures and may adjust actuarial assumptions; several employer contributions are expressly discretionary.

nodes.title: Employer Special Contributions
nodes.heading: 4.6 Employer Special Contributions
nodes.start_phrase: The Employer may, in its sole discretion, make an additional Employer Special Contribution in any Plan Year to Eligible Employees in any amount determined by the Com mittee.
nodes.summary:
- Describes Employer Make-Up Pension Contributions:
  - Contributions continue for participants beyond age 60 and five years of service to account for ongoing service.
  - Annual contribution amounts are determined using participant Compensation, the GAM 94 mortality table, and assumed Compensation growth of inflation plus 1.5%, with all actuarial assumptions adjustable by the Committee.
  - Prior make-up contributions are assumed to earn a Committee-specified rate (as of Jan 1, 2005, 10-year U.S. Treasury average + 2%), even though actual amounts are invested in participant-selected funds under Plan section 6.2.
  - These contributions are fully funded by the Employer at the later of age 60 or completion of five years of service; if employment continues after age 60, the Committee sets future funding procedures.

- Permits Employer Special Contributions:
  - The Employer, at its sole discretion, may make additional contributions in any Plan Year to Eligible Employees in amounts determined by the Committee.

- Establishes Employer 10% Target Contributions (effective Jan 1, 2008):
  - The Employer may, at its discretion, make a supplemental retirement savings contribution each Plan Year.
  - The contribution equals 10% of the participant’s Compensation for the Plan Year, reduced by:
    - Savings Plan Retirement Savings Contributions,
    - Savings Plan New Employer Matching Contributions,
    - Savings Plan Employer Discretionary Matching Contributions, and
    - The Employer portion of Social Security (OASDI) tax on the employee’s Compensation.
  - Reductions apply to amounts paid, accrued, or deemed paid/accrued for the same Plan Year.

nodes.title: Employer 10% Target Contributions
nodes.heading: 4.7 Employer 10% Target Contributions
nodes.start_phrase: Effective as of January 1, 2008, the Employer m ay, in its sole discretion, make a contribution each Plan Year to Eligible Employees to provide such Participant with a supplemental retirement savings contribution (“Employer 10% TargetContribution”).
nodes.summary:
- Describes Employer Make-Up Pension Contributions for participants reaching age 60 with at least five years of service, including continuation of such contributions for service after that date and Committee-determined procedures if employment continues past age 60.
- Sets actuarial assumptions for calculating annual Employer Make-Up Pension Contributions: based on Compensation, GAM 94 mortality, and assumed Compensation growth of inflation plus 1.5%, with all assumptions adjustable by the Committee.
- Specifies a hypothetical earnings rate for prior make-up contributions, set by the Committee (as of January 1, 2005, equal to the average 10-year U.S. Treasury rate plus 2%), even though actual amounts are invested in participant-selected funds.
- States funding timing: these make-up pension contributions will be fully funded by the Employer at the later of age 60 or completion of five years of service (as defined under the Pension Plan).
- Allows discretionary Employer Special Contributions to Eligible Employees in any Plan Year and amount as determined by the Committee.
- Introduces an optional Employer 10% Target Contribution effective January 1, 2008: calculated as 10% of the Participant’s Compensation for the Plan Year reduced by (a) Savings Plan Retirement Savings Contributions, (b) Savings Plan New Employer Matching Contributions, (c) Savings Plan Employer Discretionary Matching Contributions, and (d) the Employer portion of OASDI Social Security tax (currently 6.2% of Compensation). For items (b) and (c), employees are deemed to have contributed at the maximum level and to have received the maximum matching contribution regardless of actual contributions.

nodes.title: Accounting and Vesting
nodes.heading: SECTION 5 Accounting and Vesting
nodes.start_phrase: Except as provided in subsection 5.2, a Particip ant will fully vest in his Plan Accounts as follows:
nodes.summary:
- Section 5 (Accounting and Vesting), subsection 5.1 outlines vesting rules for different types of contributions in participant accounts.
- Employee Contributions: always 100% vested.
- Employer Special Contributions: 100% vested after 5 years of service (service defined under the Pension Plan).
- Employer 10% Target Contributions: graded vesting based on years of vested service (as defined under the Savings Plan): less than 1 year 0%; 1 year 20%; 2 years 40%; 3 years 60%; 4 years 80%; 5 or more years 100%.
- Employer Make-Up Matching and Employer Make-Up Pension Contributions: vest at the later of age 55 or completion of 5 years of service (service defined under the Pension Plan).
- Accelerated vesting: all Employer Contributions fully vest upon death or Disability while actively employed.
- Limitation: even if vested, a participant who terminates before age 60 may not receive the full amount of Employer Make-Up Pension Contributions needed to restore the Pension Plan benefit.
- Forfeiture: participants who terminate employment (other than due to death or Disability) before vesting in Employer Contributions forfeit 100% of those Employer Contributions.

nodes.title: Vesting
nodes.heading: 5.1 Vesting
nodes.start_phrase: Except as provided in subsection 5.2, a Particip ant will fully vest in his Plan Accounts as follows:
nodes.summary: The excerpt outlines Section 5.1 (Vesting) of a plan, specifying when different types of contributions become nonforfeitable. Employee Contributions are always 100% vested. Employer Special Contributions vest 100% after five years of service as defined in the Pension Plan. Employer 10% Target Contributions vest on a graded schedule based on years of vested service under the Savings Plan: 0% (<1 year), 20% (1 year), 40% (2), 60% (3), 80% (4), and 100% (5+). Employer Make-Up Matching and Make-Up Pension Contributions vest at the later of age 55 or five years of service (Pension Plan definition). All Employer Contributions fully vest upon death or Disability while actively employed. Despite vesting, a participant who terminates before age 60 may not receive the full amount of Employer Make-Up Pension Contributions needed to restore Pension Plan benefits. Participants who terminate employment before vesting in Employer Contributions (and not due to death or Disability) forfeit 100% of those Employer Contributions. The rules apply except as otherwise provided in Section 5.2.

nodes.title: Termination for Cause or Violation of Non-Compete Restrictions
nodes.heading: 5.2 Termination for Cause or Violation of Non-Compete Restrictions
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding any provisions in the Plan to the contrary, any Participant terminated for cause shall forfeit 100% of the Participant’s Accounts.
nodes.summary:
- Termination for cause results in forfeiture of 100% of a Participant’s Accounts. “Cause” includes fraud, misappropriation or embezzlement of Employer assets, and intentional, material damage to Employer or Affiliate property, as determined in the Committee’s sole discretion.
- Violation of non‑compete restrictions (working for, advising, or assisting a “competing business” before or after a 409A-defined separation from service, including death) results in forfeiture of 100% of Employer Contributions. If a partial distribution was already made, any unpaid portion is forfeited. A “competing business” is any entity conducting the same or competing business as the Company, as determined by the Committee.
- Forfeitures are used to reduce Employer Contributions for the current or future Plan Years, or to pay reasonable Plan administrative expenses.
- Allocation of contributions (Salary Deferral, Bonus, Employer Make-Up Matching, Employer Make-Up Pension, Employer Special, and Employer 10% Target Contributions) to Participants’ Accounts occurs periodically as determined by the Committee.
- Accounts: The Employer establishes and maintains Accounts for each Participant. Grandfathered Accounts remain separate from 409A Accounts; Employer Contributions are held in 409A Accounts. Beginning in 2007, the Plan uses class-year accounting with separate subaccounts within 409A Accounts. Accounts are credited with earnings, losses, distributions, and contributions as of accounting dates set by the Investment Committee. All credited amounts are for bookkeeping only and remain Employer assets subject to the claims of the Employer’s general creditors.

nodes.title: Forfeitures
nodes.heading: 5.3 Forfeitures
nodes.start_phrase: All Fo rfeitures shall be used to reduce Employer Contributions for the current Plan Year or succeeding Plan Years, or shall be used to pay reasonable administrative expenses of the Plan.
nodes.summary:
- Termination for cause and non-compete violations trigger forfeitures:
  - If terminated for cause (as determined by the Committee), a Participant forfeits 100% of all Accounts. Cause includes fraud, misappropriation or embezzlement of Employer assets, or intentional and material damage to Employer/Affiliate property.
  - If a Participant works for, counsels, advises, or assists a competing business at any time before or after separation from service (as defined under Section 409A), the Participant forfeits 100% of Employer Contributions; any unpaid portion is forfeited even if partial distributions have occurred. The Committee determines what constitutes a “competing business.”
- Forfeitures are applied to reduce Employer Contributions in the current or future Plan Years or to pay reasonable Plan administrative expenses.
- Allocation of contributions:
  - Salary Deferral, Bonus, Employer Make-Up Matching, Employer Make-Up Pension, Employer Special, and Employer 10% Target Contributions are allocated to Participants’ Accounts periodically as determined by the Committee.
- Accounts and accounting:
  - The Employer maintains one or more Accounts for each Participant as described in Section 5.4.
  - Grandfathered Accounts are kept separate from 409A Accounts; Employer Contributions are held in 409A Accounts unless otherwise specified.
  - From 2007 onward, class-year accounting applies, with separate subaccounts within 409A Accounts for each contribution year.
  - Accounts are credited with earnings, losses, distributions, and contributions as of accounting dates set by the Investment Committee.
  - All credited amounts are for bookkeeping purposes only and remain Employer assets subject to the claims of the Employer’s general creditors.

nodes.title: Allocation of Employee Contributions and Employer Contributions
nodes.heading: 5.4 Allocation of Employee Contributions and Employer Contributions
nodes.start_phrase: The total amount, if any, of Salary Deferral Co ntributions, Bonus Contributions, Employer Make-Up Matching Contributions, Employer Make -UpPension Contributions, Employer Special Contributions, and Employer 10% Target Con tributions for any Plan Year made on behalf of a Participant will be allocated to the Participant’s Accounts periodically as determined by the Committee.
nodes.summary:
- Termination for cause results in forfeiture of 100% of the Participant’s Accounts; “cause” includes fraud, misappropriation, embezzlement, or intentional/material damage to Employer/Affiliate property, as determined by the Committee.
- Violation of non-compete restrictions (working with, advising, or assisting a competing business before or after separation from service under Section 409A, including death) causes forfeiture of 100% of Employer Contributions; any unpaid Employer Contributions are forfeited even if partial distributions were already made. “Competing business” is defined at the Committee’s discretion.
- Forfeitures are used to reduce Employer Contributions for the current or future Plan Years or to pay reasonable Plan administrative expenses.
- Contributions (Salary Deferral, Bonus, Employer Make-Up Matching, Employer Make-Up Pension, Employer Special, and Employer 10% Target) are allocated to Participants’ Accounts periodically as determined by the Committee.
- Accounts: Employer establishes and maintains Accounts per contribution type; Grandfathered Accounts remain separate from 409A Accounts; beginning in 2007, class-year accounting applies with separate subaccounts within 409A Accounts; Employer Contributions are generally held in 409A Accounts.
- Accounts are credited with earnings, losses, distributions, and contributions on accounting dates set by the Investment Committee.
- All credited amounts are for accounting purposes only and remain Employer assets subject to the claims of the Employer’s general creditors.

nodes.title: Accounts
nodes.heading: 5.5 Accounts
nodes.start_phrase: The Employer shall establish a nd maintain one or more Accounts described in subsection 5.4 in the name of each Participant.
nodes.summary:
- For-cause termination leads to forfeiture of 100% of the Participant’s Accounts; “cause” includes fraud, misappropriation/embezzlement, or intentional and material damage to Employer/Affiliate property, as determined by the Committee.
- Working with or assisting a competing business, before or after separation from service (as defined under Section 409A, including death), triggers forfeiture of 100% of Employer Contributions; if a partial distribution was already made, any unpaid portion is forfeited. “Competing business” is defined at the Committee’s discretion.
- Forfeited amounts are used to reduce Employer Contributions in the current or future Plan Years or to pay reasonable Plan administrative expenses.
- Various contribution types (Salary Deferral, Bonus, Employer Make-Up Matching, Employer Make-Up Pension, Employer Special, Employer 10% Target) are allocated to Participants’ Accounts periodically as determined by the Committee.
- The Employer maintains Accounts for each Participant; grandfathered Accounts remain separate from 409A Accounts. Employer Contributions are generally held in 409A Accounts. Beginning in 2007, class-year accounting applies with separate subaccounts by contribution year.
- Accounts are credited with earnings, losses, distributions, and contributions on accounting dates set by the Investment Committee. Amounts are for accounting purposes only, remain Employer assets subject to general creditors, and Participants’ rights are limited to those provided under the Plan.

nodes.title: Funding and Investments
nodes.heading: SECTION 6 Funding and Investments
nodes.start_phrase: The Trust shall hold all assets of the Pla n.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that all Plan assets are held in a Trust, with investments determined by the Investment Committee.
- Allows the Trustee to temporarily hold assets in cash, commercial paper, short-term obligations, or short-term collective funds pending investment, reinvestment, or distribution.
- Authorizes the Investment Committee to create or terminate Investment Funds as needed.
- Permits Participants to allocate their Account balances among one or more Investment Funds and to change or transfer allocations, subject to the Investment Committee’s prescribed timing, manner, and discretion.
- Requires separate investment elections for Employer Contributions and Employee Contributions.
- Empowers the Investment Committee to decide whether Plan administration expenses are paid from the Trust or by Employers and to determine the allocation of such expenses.

nodes.title: Trust Fund
nodes.heading: 6.1 Trust Fund
nodes.start_phrase: The Trust shall hold all assets of the Pla n.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that all Plan assets are held in a Trust, with investments selected by the Investment Committee. The Trustee may temporarily hold assets in cash, commercial paper, short-term obligations, or short-term collective funds. The Investment Committee can create or terminate Investment Funds.
- Allows Participants to allocate their Account balances among available Investment Funds and to change or transfer allocations, with all elections made in the time and manner prescribed and effective at the Investment Committee’s discretion. Participants make separate elections for Employer Contributions and Employee Contributions.
- Authorizes the Investment Committee to determine whether Plan administrative expenses are paid from the Trust or by Employers, including how such costs are allocated.

nodes.title: Investment Fund Elections
nodes.heading: 6.2 Investment Fund Elections
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant may elect to invest all or a portion of the Participant’s Account in one or more Investment Funds selected by the Investment Committee.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that all Plan assets are held in a Trust, with investments selected and managed at the Investment Committee’s discretion.
- Allows the Trustee to temporarily hold assets in cash or short-term instruments pending investment, reinvestment, or distribution.
- Empowers the Investment Committee to create or terminate Investment Funds as needed.
- Permits Participants to allocate their Account balances among available Investment Funds and to change/transfer allocations, subject to the Investment Committee’s procedures and timing.
- Requires separate investment elections for Employer Contributions and Employee Contributions.
- Authorizes the Investment Committee to decide whether Plan administration expenses are paid from the Trust or by Employers, and to allocate such costs among Employers.

nodes.title: Expenses
nodes.heading: 6.3 Expenses
nodes.start_phrase: The Investment Committee shall determ ine whether expenses incurred in administering the Plan shall be paid from the Trust or by the Employers in such proportions and allocations as the Investment Committee determines.
nodes.summary:
- Section 6 (Funding and Investments)
  - Trust Fund: All plan assets are held in a Trust; the Investment Committee determines investments. The Trustee may temporarily hold assets in cash or short-term instruments pending investment or distribution.
  - Investment Funds: The Investment Committee can establish or terminate Investment Funds and controls the timing/effectiveness of participant elections.
  - Participant Investment Elections: Participants may allocate and transfer their accounts among available Investment Funds, with separate elections for Employer Contributions and Employee Contributions.
  - Expenses: The Investment Committee decides whether plan administrative expenses are paid from the Trust or by Employers, and in what proportions.

- Section 7 (Timing and Form of Payment)
  - Grandfathered Accounts:
    - Participants elect timing and form of payment via a Committee-prescribed form, choosing either payment at termination of employment or on a specified date.
    - If termination occurs before retirement, distribution is a mandatory lump sum.
    - For pre-termination requests, retirement, or Disability, distributions may be a lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 1–10 years.
    - Elections apply to all Grandfathered Account amounts unless changed at least 12 months before distribution; default is lump sum if no election is made.
    - The Committee determines whether a termination is due to retirement or Disability.
  - Employee Contributions in 409A Accounts:
    - An Initial Election of timing and form is required before amounts are allocated; from 2007 onward, a separate annual election is made for each year’s contributions.
    - Distributions occur on the earlier of: (i) the first day of the seventh month after separation from service (as defined under Code Section 409A, including death), or (ii) a participant-elected specific date.
    - Payment form may be a lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years.

nodes.title: Timing and Form of Payment
nodes.heading: SECTION 7 Timing and Form of Payment
nodes.start_phrase: A Particip ant may elect the timing and form of payment for the Participant’s Grandfathered Accounts by completing a benefit election form prescribed by the Committee.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt defines how and when benefits are paid under Section 7, covering two account types:

- Grandfathered Accounts (pre-409A amounts):
  - Participants elect timing and form of payment via a Committee-prescribed benefit election form, choosing payment at termination of employment or on a specified date.
  - If a participant terminates service from all employers and affiliates before retirement, the account is paid in a lump sum.
  - If a distribution is requested before termination, or termination is due to retirement or Disability, payment may be in a lump sum or in substantially equal annual installments over 1–10 years.
  - The election applies to all Grandfathered Account amounts unless changed; any change must be submitted at least 12 months before the distribution.
  - Default form if no election is made: lump sum.
  - The Committee determines whether a termination is due to retirement or Disability.

- Employee Contributions in 409A Accounts:
  - Before contributions are allocated, participants must make an Initial Election for timing and form of payment, following Committee procedures.
  - Starting with 2007 contributions, a separate distribution election is required for each year’s employee contributions.
  - Distributions may be elected for the earlier of: (i) the first day of the seventh month after separation from service (as defined under Section 409A, including death), or (ii) a specific date chosen by the participant.
  - Payment options are a lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years.
  - The text begins to define how installment series are treated for plan purposes but is truncated.

nodes.title: Participant’s Grandfathered Accounts
nodes.heading: 7.1 Participant’s Grandfathered Accounts
nodes.start_phrase: A Particip ant may elect the timing and form of payment for the Participant’s Grandfathered Accounts by completing a benefit election form prescribed by the Committee.
nodes.summary:
- Section 7 sets rules for when and how benefits are paid.

- 7.1 Grandfathered Accounts:
  - Participants elect timing and form of payment via a Committee-approved benefit election form.
  - Payment timing options: upon termination of employment or on a participant-specified date.
  - If service ends before retirement (from all Employers/Affiliates), payment is a mandatory lump sum.
  - For in-service distributions or terminations due to retirement or Disability, payments may be a lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 1–10 years.
  - The election applies to all Grandfathered Account amounts unless changed; any change must be submitted at least 12 months before a distribution.
  - Default form is a lump sum if no election is made.
  - The Committee determines whether a termination qualifies as retirement or Disability.

- 7.2 Employee Contributions in 409A Accounts:
  - Before contributions are allocated, participants must make an Initial Election (timing and form) per Committee procedures.
  - Beginning with 2007 contributions, a separate distribution election is required for each contribution year.
  - Distribution timing may be the earlier of: (i) the first day of the seventh month after separation from service (as defined under Section 409A, including death) or (ii) a participant-elected specific date.
  - Payment forms: lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years.
  - The text begins to define installment series for plan purposes but is cut off.

nodes.title: Employee Contributions in 409A Accounts
nodes.heading: 7.2 Employee Contributions in 409A Accounts
nodes.start_phrase: Prior to the a llocation of Employee Contributions to the Participant’s 409A Accounts, a Participant must elect the timing and form of payment for such Employee Contributions from the Participant’s 409A Accoun ts by completing a distribution election form in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Committee (the “Initial Election”).
nodes.summary:
- Section 7 outlines when and how benefits are paid under the plan, with separate rules for Grandfathered Accounts and 409A Accounts (Employee and Employer Contributions), and compliance with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code.

- 7.1 Grandfathered Accounts:
  - Participants elect timing (at termination of employment or a specified date) and form (lump sum or 1–10 years of substantially equal annual installments in certain cases) via a Committee-prescribed form.
  - If service ends before retirement, payment is a mandatory lump sum.
  - If requesting distribution before termination, or if termination is due to retirement or Disability, payment may be lump sum or installments over 1–10 years.
  - Elections apply to all Grandfathered amounts unless changed; any change must be submitted at least 12 months before the distribution.
  - Default if no election: lump sum.
  - The Committee determines whether a termination qualifies as retirement or Disability.

- 7.2 Employee Contributions in 409A Accounts:
  - Before contributions are allocated, Participants must make an Initial Election for timing and form; beginning with 2007, a separate election is required for each year’s Employee Contributions.
  - Distribution timing may be the earlier of: (i) the first day of the 7th month after separation from service (as defined under 409A, including death), or (ii) a Participant-elected specific date.
  - Form of payment: lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years; installment series is treated as a single payment under 409A regulations.
  - Initial Election governs pre-2007 Employee Contributions (and earnings/losses) unless replaced by a Second Election, which:
    - Takes effect 12 months after it is made.
    - Must defer payment at least 5 years beyond the original payment date.
    - Must be made at least 12 months before the first scheduled payment.
    - Cannot accelerate payments and can only choose among permitted forms.
  - No Second Election is allowed for Employee Contributions made on or after January 1, 2007.
  - Default if no election: lump sum on the first day of the 7th month following separation.
  - Beginning January 1, 2007, elections for 2005–2006 Employee Contributions may be modified, subject to the Second Election restrictions.

- 7.3 Employer Contributions in 409A Accounts:
  - Upon selection to receive Employer Contributions, Participants elect the form of payment via a Committee-prescribed distribution election; starting with 2007, a separate election is required for each year’s Employer Contributions.
  - Employer Contributions are distributed on the first day of the 13th month following separation from service (as defined under 409A, including death).
  - The excerpt ends before listing the permitted forms of payment for Employer Contributions.

nodes.title: Employer Contributions in 409A Accounts
nodes.heading: 7.3 Employer Contributions in 409A Accounts
nodes.start_phrase: Upon being selected by the Committe e to receive Employer Contributions, a Participant will elect the form of payment for theParticipant’s Employer Contributions held in the Participant’s 409A Accounts by completing a distribution election form in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Committee.
nodes.summary:
- Describes distribution elections for Employee Contributions in 409A Accounts, distinguishing pre-2007 amounts and 2005–2006 modification rights effective January 1, 2007, all subject to Section 409A rules.
- Outlines “Second Election” restrictions for Employee Contributions: 12-month waiting period to take effect, at least a 5-year deferral beyond the prior payment date, must be made at least 12 months before the first scheduled payment, no acceleration allowed, and limited to approved payment forms; no Second Elections allowed for Employee Contributions made on or after January 1, 2007.
- Provides default payment for Employee Contributions if no election is made: lump sum on the first day of the seventh month following separation from service.
- Sets rules for Employer Contributions in 409A Accounts: participants elect payment form; beginning with 2007 contributions, a separate election is required each year; distributions occur on the first day of the thirteenth month after separation (including death).
- Specifies allowable forms for Employer Contributions: lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years; installments are treated as a single payment under 409A; once elected, neither timing nor form may be changed; default is lump sum if no election is made.
- Establishes hardship distribution provisions: available from vested accounts upon an Unforeseeable Financial Emergency; paid in a lump sum within 90 days; paid from 409A Accounts before Grandfathered Accounts.
- Defines Unforeseeable Financial Emergency (illness/accident of participant or dependent, casualty loss, or similar extraordinary, unforeseeable events beyond the participant’s control), requires reduction for insurance/reimbursement and feasible asset liquidation, and leaves eligibility/amount determinations to the Committee based on facts and circumstances.
- States that receiving a hardship distribution suspends the participant’s Employee Contributions for the remainder of that calendar year.

nodes.title: Hardship Distributions
nodes.heading: 7.4 Hardship Distributio ns
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant may receive a distribution from the Participant’s vested Accounts for hardship reasons, provided the Participant has suffered an Unforeseeable Financial Emergency (as defined below ).
nodes.summary:
- Describes distribution options for Employer Contributions in 409A Accounts: either a lump sum or substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years, at the participant’s election.
- States that an installment series is treated as a single payment under Section 409A regulations.
- Once a payment election is made, neither the participant nor the employer may change the timing or form of distribution; absent an election, payment defaults to a lump sum.
- Outlines hardship distribution rules: available in case of an “Unforeseeable Financial Emergency,” paid in a lump sum within 90 days of request.
- Establishes payment ordering for hardship withdrawals: amounts are taken from 409A Accounts before Grandfathered Accounts.
- Defines “Unforeseeable Financial Emergency” as severe financial hardship arising from sudden illness/accident of the participant or dependent, loss of property due to casualty, or similar extraordinary, unforeseeable events beyond the participant’s control.
- Requires that hardship distribution amounts be reduced by insurance/reimbursements or by liquidation of assets, unless liquidation would itself cause severe hardship.
- Assigns the plan committee authority to determine eligibility and payment amounts based on all relevant facts and circumstances.
- Provides that receiving a hardship distribution suspends the participant’s employee contributions for the remainder of the calendar year.

nodes.title: Payments After Death
nodes.heading: 7.5 Payments After Death
nodes.start_phrase: If a Participant dies before receiving the entire balance of the Participant’s Accounts, the remaining balance in the Participant’s Accounts shall become 100% vested and shall be paid to the Participant’s Beneficiaries designated in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Committee.
nodes.summary:
- Payments after death (Section 7.5): If a participant dies before full distribution, all account balances become 100% vested and are paid to designated beneficiaries in a single lump sum within 90 days after the Committee is notified of the death.
- Payments upon disability (Section 7.6): Regardless of prior elections, any accounts not yet in distribution are automatically distributed as soon as administratively practicable after a Disability (as defined in 2.10).
  - Grandfathered Accounts: payable either as a lump sum or in substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years, per the participant’s election; changes to disability distribution elections must comply with subsection 7.1.
  - 409A Accounts: distributed according to the participant’s elections applicable to each year of contributions; changes to disability distribution elections for Employee Contributions must comply with subsection 7.2.
- Special distribution rules for 409A Accounts (Section 7.7):
  - If Code Section 162(m) would limit or eliminate the employer’s deduction, payment is deferred to the first year the deduction is expected to be available or to the year of separation from employment.
  - If payment would violate securities or other laws, or breach loan covenants/contract terms causing material harm, payment is deferred to the first calendar year when no such violation or material harm is anticipated.
  - Mentions plan payments related to employment taxes or income inclusion (text truncated).

nodes.title: Payments Upon Disability
nodes.heading: 7.6 Payments Upon Disability
nodes.start_phrase: Notwithstanding a Participant’s elections and any provisio n of the Plan to the contrary, all Accounts that have not yet commenced distribution shall automatically be distributed to a Participant as soon as administratively practicable following the Participant’s Disability as defined under subsection 2.10.
nodes.summary:
- Payment after death: If a participant dies before full distribution, the remaining account balance becomes 100% vested and is paid to designated beneficiaries in a single lump sum within 90 days after the Committee is notified.
- Payment upon disability: Upon a disability (as defined in the plan), any accounts not already in distribution are automatically distributed as soon as administratively practicable.
  - Grandfathered Accounts: Paid either as a lump sum or in substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years per the participant’s election; any changes to disability-related elections must follow the plan’s change rules in subsection 7.1.
  - 409A Accounts: Distributed according to the participant’s prior distribution elections for each contribution year; changes to disability-related elections for Employee Contributions must comply with subsection 7.2.
- Special distribution rules for 409A Accounts:
  - Section 162(m) limitation: If payment would not be deductible due to the corporate tax deduction limit, payment is deferred to the first year it is expected to be deductible or to the year of separation from employment.
  - Legal/contractual constraints: If payment would violate securities or other laws, or breach loan covenants/contract terms causing material harm, payment is deferred to the first year such issues no longer apply and payment would not cause material harm.
  - Notes an allowance for payments related to employment taxes or income inclusion (text truncated).

nodes.title: Special Distribution Rules for 409A Accounts
nodes.heading: 7.7 Special Distribution Rules for 409A Accounts
nodes.start_phrase: If the Company or Affiliate’ s deduction for payment of all or any portion of to a Participant’s 409A Accounts would be limited oreliminated by the application of Section 162(m) of the Code, then the Plan will defer payment of such Participant’s 409A Accounts either (i) to a date in the first year in which the Company or the Com mittee reasonably anticipates that such payment will not result in a deduction limitation under Section 162(m) or (ii) to the year in which the Participant’s separation from employment occurs.
nodes.summary:
- Payments after death: If a participant dies before full distribution, all account balances become 100% vested and are paid in a single lump sum to designated beneficiaries within 90 days of the Committee being notified.
- Payments upon disability: All undistributed accounts are paid as soon as administratively practicable after the participant’s Disability (as defined in 2.10). Grandfathered Accounts are paid either as a lump sum or in substantially equal annual installments over 2–10 years per the participant’s election (changes must follow 7.1). 409A Accounts are paid per the participant’s prior elections for each contribution year (changes to Employee Contributions must follow 7.2).
- Special rules for 409A Accounts: Payments are deferred if they would be nondeductible under Section 162(m), until the first year the deduction is expected to be allowed or the year of separation from employment. Payments are also deferred if they would violate securities/applicable laws or loan/contract terms causing material harm, until the first year no such violation/harm is anticipated. The Plan may make payments to cover employment taxes (FICA and related income tax) or due to 409A income inclusion, consistent with Treasury Regulations and IRS guidance. If a payment window spans two Plan Years, the recipient cannot choose the tax year of payment.
- Beneficiary designations: Participants may designate primary and contingent beneficiaries (including trusts/estates) and allocation proportions for all accounts, and may change designations; the last filed designation controls. If none is on file, balances are paid to the participant’s estate.
- Facility of payment: If a recipient is under a legal disability or unable to manage affairs, payments may be made to a legal representative or applied for the person’s benefit as determined by the Committee.
- Unclaimed benefits: If a participant/beneficiary’s whereabouts are unknown and benefits are unclaimed within two years after employment termination, the Committee may pay as if the participant died. If neither the participant nor any beneficiary can be located within three years after termination, all benefits are irrevocably forfeited.

nodes.title: Designation of Beneficiary
nodes.heading: 7.8 Designation of Beneficiary
nodes.start_phrase: A Participant may, by completing a Beneficiary designation form in accordance with procedures prescribed by the Committee, designate one or more primary and contingent Beneficiaries (which may include a trust or an estate) to receive the Participant’s Account balance following the Participant’s death and may designate the proportions in which such Beneficiaries receive payments.
nodes.summary:
- 409A compliance/corrections: The Company/Committee may take actions permitted under Treasury Regulations, IRS Notice 2005-1 Q&A-15, and subsequent guidance to address failures under Section 409A.
- Employment taxes defined: Includes FICA on deferred compensation (Sections 3101 and 3121(v)(2)), income tax under Section 3401 on the FICA amount, and additional income tax attributable to pyramiding wages and taxes.
- Payment timing: If a payment period spans two Plan Years, the Participant/Beneficiary cannot choose the tax year of payment.
- Beneficiary designations: Participants may designate primary and contingent beneficiaries (including trusts/estates), specify proportions, and change designations; the last on file controls. If none is on file, the estate receives the balance.
- Facility of payment: If a payee is under legal disability or unable to manage affairs, payments may be made to a legal representative or applied for the person’s benefit as the Committee decides.
- Unclaimed benefits: If whereabouts are unknown and benefits are unclaimed within two years after employment termination, the Committee may pay as if the Participant had died. If the Participant/Beneficiaries cannot be located within three years after termination, all benefits are irrevocably forfeited.

nodes.title: Facility of Payment
nodes.heading: 7.9 Facility of Payment
nodes.start_phrase: Any amounts payable under the Plan to a Participant or Beneficiary who is under a legal disability or who, in the judgment of the Committee, is unable to manage such person’saffairs, may be paid to the legal representative of such person or may be applied for the benefit of such person in any manner the Committee shall select.
nodes.summary:
- Compliance with Section 409A: Allows Company/Committee discretion to accelerate or adjust payments only as permitted by Treasury Regulations and IRS Notice 2005-1 (Q&A-15) and later guidance. Defines “Employment taxes” to include FICA on deferred compensation (Sections 3101 and 3121(v)(2)), income tax under Section 3401 on the FICA Amount, and amounts to cover pyramiding wages/taxes. If a payment period spans two Plan Years, the recipient cannot choose the tax year of payment.
- Beneficiary Designation (Section 7.8): Participants may designate primary and contingent beneficiaries (including trusts/estates) for all Plan accounts, specify proportions, and update designations; the last filed designation controls. If none is on file at death, benefits go to the estate.
- Facility of Payment (Section 7.9): If a payee is under a legal disability or unable to manage affairs, payments may be made to a legal representative or applied for the person’s benefit as the Committee decides.
- Unclaimed Benefits (Section 7.10): If a participant/beneficiary cannot be located and no claim is made within two years after employment termination, the Committee may pay benefits as if the participant had died. If neither the participant nor any beneficiary can be located within three years after termination, all vested benefits are irrevocably forfeited.

nodes.title: Unclaimed Benefits
nodes.heading: 7.10 Unclaimed Benefits
nodes.start_phrase: If a Participant or Beneficiary’s whereabouts are unknown to the Employer, and if the Participant or the Participant’s Beneficiary fails to claim the Participant’s benefits within two years following termination of the Participant’s employment, the Committee may elect to make payment of the Participant or Beneficiary’s vested benefits as if they had died.
nodes.summary:
- Clarifies Section 409A compliance: the Company/Committee may make distributions or take actions permitted under Treasury Regulations and IRS Notice 2005-1 (and subsequent guidance), including to address failures under Section 409A.
- Defines “Employment taxes” to include FICA on deferred compensation under Code Sections 3101 and 3121(v)(2), income tax under Section 3401 on the FICA amount, and additional amounts to cover pyramiding wages and taxes.
- Specifies that when a payment period spans two Plan Years, the Participant/Beneficiary cannot choose the tax year of payment.
- Outlines beneficiary designations: Participants may designate primary/contingent beneficiaries (including trusts/estates) and allocation proportions; the latest designation controls; if none, payment defaults to the estate.
- Provides for payment to or for the benefit of individuals under legal disability or unable to manage affairs, at the Committee’s discretion.
- Addresses unclaimed benefits: if benefits are unclaimed within two years after employment termination and the individual’s whereabouts are unknown, payments may be made as if the Participant had died; if neither the Participant nor any Beneficiary can be located within three years after termination, all benefits are irrevocably forfeited.

nodes.title: Nature of Interest of Participant
nodes.heading: SECTION 8 Nature of Interest of Participant
nodes.start_phrase: Participation in this Plan will not create, in favor of any Participant, any right or lien in or against any of the assets of any Employer, and a Participant’s Account balances shall remain an unrestricted asset of the Participant’s Employer.
nodes.summary:
- Participants have no lien or right against employer assets; account balances remain employer assets.
- Benefits are non-assignable and cannot be anticipated, pledged, transferred, or encumbered.
- All benefits are paid in cash from the employer’s general funds; no separate fund or asset segregation is created.
- The Plan does not create a trust or fiduciary relationship; the employer’s promise to pay remains unfunded with respect to participants.
- Administration is by a Committee with authority to interpret the Plan, resolve ambiguities, adopt rules, enforce the Plan and any trust, direct trustees on distributions, provide employers with required information, and hire/delegate to service providers in writing.
- An Investment Committee has full authority over appointing trustees and investment managers and overseeing investment of Plan assets.
- Employers may withhold required federal, state, or local taxes from Plan payments.

nodes.title: Administration
nodes.heading: SECTION 9 Administration
nodes.start_phrase: This Plan will be administered by the Committee.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the Plan is administered by a Committee.
- Grants the Administrative Committee broad authority to: interpret the Plan and resolve ambiguities; adopt procedures and regulations consistent with the Plan and Trust; enforce the Plan; direct Trustees on payments/distributions; provide employers with necessary information (e.g., for tax purposes); and hire and delegate duties to professionals (agents, attorneys, accountants, actuaries, etc.) with delegations and acceptances in writing.
- Grants the Investment Committee full authority over appointing trustees and investment managers and overseeing the investment of Plan assets.
- Confirms employers’ right to withhold required federal, state, and local taxes from Plan payments.

nodes.title: Committee
nodes.heading: 9.1 Committee
nodes.start_phrase: This Plan will be administered by the Committee.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the Plan is administered by a Committee.
- Grants the Committee broad, discretionary authority to interpret the Plan, resolve ambiguities, adopt administrative rules, and enforce the Plan and Trust.
- Authorizes the Committee to direct Trustees on payments and distributions and to provide Employers with necessary information for tax or other purposes.
- Permits the Committee to hire and delegate duties to agents (e.g., attorneys, accountants, actuaries), including individuals also employed by the Employers, with all delegations and acceptances in writing.
- Assigns the Investment Committee full authority over appointing trustees and investment managers and overseeing investment of Plan assets.
- Confirms Employers’ right to withhold required federal, state, and local taxes from Plan payments.

nodes.title: Powers of the Administrative and Investment Committees
nodes.heading: 9 .2 Powers of the Administrative and Investment Committees
nodes.start_phrase: The Committee’s powers will include, but will not be limited to, the power:
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the Plan is administered by a Committee.
- Grants the Administrative Committee broad discretionary authority to:
  - Interpret Plan terms and resolve ambiguities or omissions.
  - Adopt procedures and regulations consistent with the Plan and Trust.
  - Enforce the Plan and related rules.
  - Direct Trustees on payments and distributions.
  - Provide employers with required information (e.g., for tax purposes).
  - Hire and delegate duties to agents, attorneys, accountants, actuaries, and others (including those also employed by the employers), with delegations documented in writing.
- Assigns the Investment Committee full authority over appointing trustees and investment managers and overseeing investment of Plan assets.
- Authorizes employers to withhold applicable federal, state, and local taxes from Plan payments.

nodes.title: Withholding
nodes.heading: 9.3 Withholding
nodes.start_phrase: The Employers shall have the right to deduct from any payment to be made under the Plan any federal, state, or local taxes required by law to be withheld.
nodes.summary:
- Establishes that the Plan is administered by a Committee.
- Grants the Administrative Committee broad discretion to interpret the Plan, resolve ambiguities, adopt procedures and regulations consistent with the Plan and Trust, enforce the Plan, direct trustees on payments and distributions, provide employers with required information, and hire and delegate duties to professionals via written delegations.
- Grants the Investment Committee full authority over appointing trustees and investment managers and managing the investment of Plan assets.
- Authorizes employers to withhold required federal, state, and local taxes from Plan payments.

nodes.title: Retirement Claims Procedures
nodes.heading: 9.4 Retirement Claims Procedures
nodes.start_phrase: To the extent that a Participant’s claim relates to a determination with respect to his Accounts, other than a Disability determination, the Committee will provide the Participant with notice of the status of his claim for retirement benefits within a reasonable period of time after a complete claim has been filed, but no later than 90 days after receipt of the Participant’s benefit claim.
nodes.summary:
- Scope: Outlines Retirement Claims Procedures for benefit claims related to a participant’s accounts other than disability determinations, and begins the Disability Claims Procedures section.
- Initial claim decision (retirement claims):
  - Committee must issue a status/decision within a reasonable time, no later than 90 days after receiving a complete claim.
  - One 90-day extension permitted for special circumstances with notice given before the initial 90-day period ends.
- Incomplete claims:
  - Participant is notified of missing information and given 90 days to supply it.
  - The Committee’s response deadline is tolled from the notice of insufficiency until the participant’s response.
  - Failure to provide the information within 90 days results in denial.
- Denial notice contents (retirement claims):
  - Specific reasons for denial.
  - References to specific plan provisions relied upon.
  - Description of additional information needed and why.
  - Explanation of the plan’s claims review and appeal procedures.
  - Statement of right to bring a civil action under ERISA Section 502(a) after an appeal denial.
- Appeal rights and process (retirement claims):
  - Participant has 60 days from receipt of the denial to file a written appeal.
  - Participant may obtain, free of charge, all documents, records, and other information relevant to the claim.
  - Participant may submit additional comments, records, and information regardless of whether they were provided initially.
  - Committee conducts a full and fair review and issues a decision within 60 days; may extend up to a total of 120 days for special circumstances with timely written notice.
- Final appeal decision contents (retirement claims):
  - Specific reasons for the decision.
  - References to specific plan provisions relied upon.
  - Statement of the participant’s right to free access to relevant documents and records.
  - Statement of the right to bring a civil action under ERISA Section 502(a) after an appeal denial.
- Disability claims procedures:
  - Section 9.5 begins, indicating the Committee will provide notice of the status of a disability claim within a reasonable period after a complete claim is filed; further details are not included in the excerpt.

nodes.title: Disability Claims Procedures
nodes.heading: 9.5 Disability Claims Procedures
nodes.start_phrase: To the extent that a Participant’s claim relates to a Disability determination with respect to his Accounts, the Committee will provide the Participant with notice of the status of his claim for Disability benefits within a reasonable period of time after a complete claim has been filed, but no later than 45 days after receipt of the Participant’s benefit claim.
nodes.summary:
- Retirement claims procedures (non-disability):
  - Committee must issue a benefit claim decision within 90 days of a complete filing; one 90-day extension allowed with prior notice.
  - If information is insufficient, participant is notified and given 90 days to provide more; response time is tolled until information is received; failure to respond within 90 days results in denial.
  - Denial notice must state reasons, cite specific Plan provisions, identify needed additional information and why, explain review/appeal procedures, and note ERISA §502(a) civil action rights.
  - Appeal must be filed within 60 days of denial; participant may obtain, free of charge, all documents relevant to the claim and submit additional evidence.
  - Committee conducts full and fair review; decision ordinarily within 60 days, extendable to 120 days with prior notice; final decision must include reasons, Plan citations, right to free access to relevant documents, and ERISA §502(a) rights.

- Disability claims procedures:
  - Committee must decide within 45 days of a complete filing; may extend once by 30 days, and a second time by another 30 days if circumstances outside its control persist, with prior notices.
  - If information is insufficient, participant is notified and given 45 days to provide more; response time is tolled until received; failure to respond within 45 days results in denial.
  - Denial notice content mirrors retirement claims (reasons, Plan provisions, needed information and why, review/appeal procedures, ERISA §502(a) rights).
  - Appeal must be filed within 180 days; participant may obtain, free of charge, all relevant documents and submit additional evidence; Committee may consult medical or vocational experts.
  - Committee decision on appeal ordinarily within 45 days, extendable to 90 days with prior notice; final decision must include reasons, Plan citations, right to free access to relevant documents, and ERISA §502(a) rights.

- Liability and indemnification:
  - Administrative and Investment Committee members are not liable for acts or omissions in Plan administration except in cases of bad faith, gross misconduct, or fraud.
  - Employers will indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Committee members against damages, losses, or costs (including reasonable costs), except in the foregoing circumstances.

nodes.title: Liability
nodes.heading: 9.6 Liability
nodes.start_phrase: No member of the Administrative or Investment Committees shall be liable for any act of commission or omission in connection with the administration of the Plan, except in circumstances involving bad faith, gross misconduct, or fraud.
nodes.summary:
- Disability benefit claim decision timelines: initial determination within 45 days of receipt; one 30‑day extension for special circumstances with advance notice; a second 30‑day extension if circumstances outside the Committee’s control persist, with advance notice.
- Incomplete claims: if insufficient information is submitted, the Participant is notified and given 45 days to provide additional data; the Committee’s decision period is tolled from the notice date until the Participant’s response; failure to submit within 45 days results in denial.
- Denial notice content: reasons for denial, specific Plan provisions cited, description of any additional required information and why, explanation of review/appeal procedures, and notice of right to bring a civil action under ERISA Section 502(a) after an appeal denial.
- Appeal process: Participant has 180 days from receipt of the initial denial to file a written appeal; may request, free of charge, all documents and records relevant to the claim; may submit additional comments and evidence; the Committee may consult medical or vocational experts.
- Appeal decision timelines: decision ordinarily within 45 days of appeal receipt; up to 90 days if special circumstances require, with written notice of extension before the end of the first 45‑day period.
- Final appeal decision content: reasons for the decision, specific Plan provisions cited, notice of right to access (free) all relevant documents, and notice of right to bring a civil action under ERISA Section 502(a) after an appeal denial.
- Liability and indemnification (Section 9.6): Administrative and Investment Committee members are not liable for acts/omissions in Plan administration except for bad faith, gross misconduct, or fraud; Employers will indemnify, defend, and hold them harmless (including reasonable attorneys’ fees) for losses arising from Plan administration.
- Finality and litigation limits (Section 9.7): Committee/Investment Committee determinations are final and binding; participants must exhaust the Plan’s claim and appeal procedures before filing suit; in ERISA actions (other than breach of fiduciary duty), court evidence is limited to what was timely presented to the Committee; any legal action must be filed within 120 days of the Committee’s final decision; benefits are payable only upon Committee determination of entitlement.
- Governing law (Section 9.8): The Plan is governed by Delaware law to the extent not preempted by ERISA.

nodes.title: Finality of Committee Determinations
nodes.heading: 9.7 Finality of Committee Determinations
nodes.start_phrase: Determinations by the Comm ittee or Investment Committees and any interpretation, rule, or administrative decision adopted by t he Committee or Investment Committees shall be final and binding for all Plan purposes and upon all interested persons, their heirs, and their personal representatives.
nodes.summary:
- Addresses coverage/indemnification of plan-related expenses, including attorneys’ fees, arising from the implementation or administration of the Plan.
- Establishes that determinations, interpretations, rules, and administrative decisions by the Committee or Investment Committees are final and binding on all parties.
- Requires exhaustion of the Plan’s internal claim and appeal procedures before any lawsuit to recover benefits may be filed.
- Limits judicial review (except for breach of fiduciary duty claims) to the evidence timely presented to the Committee.
- Imposes a 120-day statute of limitations to file legal action after the Committee denies an appeal.
- States that benefits are payable only if the Committee determines eligibility.
- Provides that, to the extent not preempted by ERISA, Delaware law governs the Plan.

nodes.title: Governing Law
nodes.heading: 9.8 Governing Law
nodes.start_phrase: To the extent this Plan is not preempted by ERISA, the Plan shall be governed by laws of the State of Delaware.
nodes.summary:
- Addresses responsibility for costs and liabilities (including attorneys’ fees) arising from implementation or administration of the Plan.
- Establishes the finality of determinations by the Committee and Investment Committees; their interpretations, rules, and administrative decisions are binding on all parties, heirs, and personal representatives.
- Requires exhaustion of the Plan’s claim and review procedures before any lawsuit to recover benefits may be filed.
- Limits judicial review (for ERISA actions other than breach of fiduciary duty) to the evidence that was timely presented to the Committee.
- Imposes a 120-day deadline to bring any legal action after the Committee’s final denial of an appeal.
- Clarifies that benefits are payable only if the Committee determines the Participant or Beneficiary is entitled to them.
- Sets governing law: ERISA preempts where applicable; otherwise, Delaware law applies.

nodes.title: No Employment Rights
nodes.heading: SECTION 10 No Employment Rights
nodes.start_phrase: No provisions of the Plan or any action taken by the Compa ny, the Board of Directors, the Committee, or the Investment Committee shall give any person any right to be retained in the employ of any Employer, and the right and power of an Employer to dismiss o r discharge any Participant is specifically reserved.
nodes.summary: Section 10 (“No Employment Rights”) states that participation in the Plan and any actions by the Company, Board of Directors, Committee, or Investment Committee do not confer any right to continued employment. It expressly reserves the Employer’s authority to dismiss or discharge any Participant at any time, clarifying that the Plan does not alter employment-at-will or create employment guarantees.

nodes.title: Change in Control
nodes.heading: SECTION 11 Change in Control
nodes.start_phrase: In the eve nt that the stock or substantially all the assets of an Employer, its subsidiary, or one of its divisions is sold, or if a majority of the beneficial ownership of an Employer, subsidiary, or one of its divisions alters (“Change in Control”), the Grandfathered Accounts of Participants affected by such sale shall become immediately due and payable unless a successor of the Employer assumes the lia bilities and responsibilities relating to the affected Participants.
nodes.summary:
- Section 11 outlines consequences of a Change in Control on participant accounts.
- 11.1 Grandfathered Accounts: If the Employer, a subsidiary, or a division experiences a sale of stock or substantially all assets, or a majority change in beneficial ownership, affected participants’ Grandfathered Accounts become immediately due and payable, unless a successor assumes the related liabilities and responsibilities.
- 11.2 409A Accounts: Upon a Change in Control Event as defined under Code Section 409A (change in ownership, effective control, or substantial asset ownership), affected participants’ 409A Accounts become 100% vested and are immediately payable in a lump sum.

nodes.title: Amounts Held in Grandfathered Accounts
nodes.heading: 11.1 Amounts Held in Grandfathered Accounts
nodes.start_phrase: In the eve nt that the stock or substantially all the assets of an Employer, its subsidiary, or one of its divisions is sold, or if a majority of the beneficial ownership of an Employer, subsidiary, or one of its divisions alters (“Change in Control”), the Grandfathered Accounts of Participants affected by such sale shall become immediately due and payable unless a successor of the Employer assumes the lia bilities and responsibilities relating to the affected Participants.
nodes.summary:
The excerpt outlines how participant accounts are treated upon a change in control:

- Section 11 sets payout/vesting rules triggered by corporate control changes.
- 11.1 (Grandfathered Accounts): If the Employer, a subsidiary, or a division experiences a sale of stock or substantially all assets, or a majority change in beneficial ownership, affected participants’ grandfathered accounts become immediately due and payable, unless a successor assumes all related liabilities and responsibilities.
- 11.2 (409A Accounts): If there is a change in ownership, effective control, or a substantial asset sale of the Employer as defined under IRC Section 409A, affected participants’ 409A accounts become 100% vested and are paid immediately in a lump sum.
- Key distinctions: 409A treatment follows IRS-defined “Change in Control Event” and mandates lump-sum payment and full vesting; grandfathered accounts trigger immediate payment but allow an exception if a successor assumes obligations.

nodes.title: Amounts Held in 409A Accounts
nodes.heading: 11.2 Amounts Held in 409A Accounts
nodes.start_phrase: In the event that there is a change in ownership of the Employer, a change in effective control of the Employer, or a change in the ownership of a substantial portion of the assets of the Employer, as defined in Code Section 409A and the regulations thereunder (collectively, a “Change in Control Event”), the 409A Accounts of Participants affected by such Change in Control Event shall become 100% vested and shall be immediately due and payable in a lump sum.
nodes.summary: Section 11 outlines how participant accounts are treated upon a Change in Control. For Grandfathered Accounts, if the employer, a subsidiary, or a division is sold or its majority ownership changes, affected participants’ balances become immediately due and payable unless a successor assumes the related liabilities. For 409A Accounts, a Change in Control Event as defined by Code Section 409A (change in ownership, effective control, or substantial asset sale) causes affected participants’ accounts to become 100% vested and paid immediately in a lump sum.
